LessonsInDissonance said:
Have you ever thought that perhaps every single purity route will be part of one true ending?
Click to expand...
It's possible, though I would expect the ending to be something to the tune of moving past the purity routes. The fundamental question is "how can one harmonize 35 different routes," and alternatively, "in what situation would one be given 35 choices." Harmonization is most easily achieved by 'walking past them' and making them a matter of the past (this is the case in visual novels where routes are conceptualized as 'past loops' and the MC remembers past loops but then proceeds into the future with only a little of their baggage). It is second-most easily achieved by making them non-canon 'side paths.' This is kind of what I expect for LiL. Like a situation where it's like: "Okay, I choose to stay in fiction, and within it I shall wed my beloved [character of your choice]." Then the true ending could slice that all off by being "Okay, I do NOT choose to stay in fiction, in fact I will go outside and touch grass." That also addresses 'in what situation would one be given 35 choices' - when Sensei has the choice to stay within LiL and choose who he wants to be with. This is all very traditional for visual novels. And finally, a fun interpretation trick to do with games like LiL is to remember that the beginnings and ends were conceived at the very start of the process. If one asks "what kind of ending would Selebus have been able to predict starting from the very beginning of the game," the list of possibilities somewhat narrows down, and precludes many cases of 35 distinct routes being part of the true ending in some kind of complex plot scheme.

All that said, I weight all of this somewhat minimally. I just want to openly parody the idea of the 'touch grass ending' since I have like 35% - 45% confidence in it and if it's correct then making fun of it will induce a psychological response. In the 55%-65% case it's wrong then it's just random banter indistinguishable from any old post. Basically very high troll EV.

Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

I may forgive characters over time for a past mistake, bumping them back up.

A character most likely won't lose their position just because I haven't seen them enough in a while.

I have a few observations/funfacts from the replay that didn't make to their own post because I was trying to speedrun chapter 2 to catch up to my schedule:
1. Yumi's clothes are her mom's. She never says this to Akira, but he comments that a long skirt should be kind of hot during summer and she says to get off her case. Later on Yuki says that Yumi keeps using her own clothes from when she was Yumi's age. So this is already foreshadowing for when Yumi starts to give Yuki a chance again. Despite what happened, she remained a mommy's girl (to a degree) even when she "gave up on her" by refusing to use anything but her clothes.
2. Io's self destructive nature is shown early on with Yuki as well. So, this is an interesting one: Upon an early visit to the bathhouse, Io will fangirl over Yuki's tattoo and insist she let Akira look at it. However, during the end of said event, Io will start regretting her decision because Yuki and Akira start to sort of flirt, and she realises that she made things even harder for her by pairing him with an adult. This is very subtle and is likely to only be observed if you understand her head.
3. As it has been said, huggyboy does foreshadow a lot of things, which isn't the case of this picture, at least not intentionally, but I found it funny, given that Nodoka's parting words when she dies is that she should have hugged Akira more:
4. One of the worst events of LiL, in terms of logic, is Kirin's first invite over because there is just no justification for Ami to find a pair of boots in the entrance, accept that Akira bought it for her, and then go into her bedroom to give Kirin time to leave with her boots.
5. The first half of chapter 2 is when Maya Prime starts to realise that Akira is her Akira, and slowly starts to help him/fight Noriko in helping him recover his memories. However, there is a third layer to these events, which is that only when we meet alt Maya Prime that we realise for how long she was waiting for her Akira to appear, and for the longest time she didn't even think it possible. So yeah, these events, to Maya Prime's perspective are a miracle that hasn't happened once in a thousand years - which makes things even more dire in case someone resets him.
6. Makoto keeps dreaming about her suicide after she's reset, and it is revealed that she even left a suicide note for her mother - although that never reaches her, as Maki has no idea about it. Makoto also has one of the worst relationships to Akira in terms of abuse, as even when she calls him over for a weekend getaway (after killing herself) and he recognizing that she has depression, he'll not throw her a bone. She demands he treats her better, and he really doesn't tbh (even though in narration he admits he likes her and could say so to her - making him even further a dick by not doing it).
7. On the subject of being a dick, one of Haruka's events will end up with Ami calling her a slut, making her cry and telling it is her right to do so. Akira, instead of reprimanding her, will just ask if she hasn't said enough, to what she says no - and Akira just lets Haruka leave crying. His response to Ami is just to cuddle with her after it while watching tv. This to me, destroys Akira's character much more than some of the worst shit he's done.
8. Osako notes in multiple events how much Wakana likes Akira and how uncommon that is for her. That however is something that brings Osako joy up until the soup event. From then on, Osako points out how she's afraid that Wakana will just wake up one day and realise that she deserves much better than Osako. That is further reinforced because Osako notes that it took extreme effort for her to break Wakana's barriers, while Akira did it in a matter of weeks by actively not trying or even rejecting Wakana (to a degree). This is brought to the forefront later but it was already present here.
9. Nightvision is mentioned by Yasu as well (the ability to perceive more of the world by closing one's eyes, which Ami claims to have). However there is one event in which Ami actively seems to take advantage of Akira's blackouts, and explains that she has them as well. It is unclear if she is using triggers to make Akira slip, but it gets to the point where she locks Maya out of the room and she has to drag Makoto to save Akira from Ami.
10. Uta doesn't wear pants in the dorms. That is a trait noted by multiple characters. And we should all be thankful for it. Praise be.

posts.content_html_raw:
Since many are on their replay, I seek fresh eyes for an age-old question of mine about a certain conversation by the end of Ch2. Why did Uta skip her work unannounced? What happened?
This event is within the 4th reset event chain, so the last time Sensei privately spoke to Uta prior to this would be Uta's Blood Everywhere, or anywhere during the 2nd Christmas party (particularly, Dodging Snowflakes) if updates can establish some chronological order. Then, the first time Sensei had any meaningful conversation with Uta is by the end of Creatures of Habits. However, none of the event above really gives solid enough hints on why Uta skipped work without notice and I can't find any direct confirmation about anything related.

Now, even if Uta's past has not been revealed yet at that time, I am all about attributing this mysterious absence to her not feeling like working due to perhaps unsolicitedly receiving more of her own nudes yet again. Judging from what Uta said by the end of Creatures of Habits, it's easy to intentionally believe that Uta here was insinuating that her nightmare had recently resurfaced.

What stops from just assuming so is that:
- That's not the only possible take on her words. Moreover, Uta actually looked pretty bashfully happy when delivering those words, so she might be implying her trend of having crushes rather than something haunting. Even bringing up "her pictures" would significantly dim her aura, so it doesn't really feel fitting here.
- Even if she did recently received her own nudes around the time of Somnambula, a direct confirmation on the cause/effect is still lacking (i.e., skipping work is true and receiving nudes is true, but is receiving nudes leading to skipping work true?)
- When Uta finally confided to Io in Neverender about receiving nudes again, Uta seemed to be talking only about that one scenario in After the Rain when she washed Sensei's back. I feel like Uta would've mentioned that it actually had already happened twice if we want to assume her skipping work all the way back in Ch2 was caused by nudes. It would be something like "I was about to go to work...then my phone went off" and "then months later I was about to take a bath...then my phone went off", for example. Instead, she made it sound like the nude she got during After the Rain was something that happened for the first time after a long while.

(I took the liberty of believing that she was not being completely honest when she said "I was about to take a bath" when confiding to Io)

So, my actual question is did I miss something? Was her absence actually being brought up and discussed in some other events so I don't have to make this assumption that isn't that impeccable in my book?

But as of this writing, the DRM only kicks in if the care packages are installed in the game.

posts.content_html_raw:
throwawaysponge said:
Maybe it's me but the 'illusion of choice' from the sandbox option does give a lot of (heavy quotation) "Value" to this game.
Click to expand...
I generally agree with this idea. Renpy style games could do without the grinding, but having definite stops to do things at the players own pace, or access repeatables, secondary gameplay elements or such adds something to the experience. It's mostly monkey brain logic, but the illusion of choice makes it still feel somewhat like a game, rather than just reading.

LiL is probably one of the worst examples for it, though. No hints, many events obscurely hidden, a huge number of them only trigger on specific days, grinding for point requirements to start them rather than just click to start the next part, no secondary gameplay elements other than the repeatables which only get variation maybe once per chapter. And the ever present concern that the next event will lock you into a long chain with an obnoxious puzzle.
I recall someone referring to LiL's gameplay loop as hostile, which I think is pretty accurate.

First it was the green haired girl, now it's the spiky pink haired girl looming in the background. Honestly I'm not into the spiky hair.

Does cheating on your husband/wife who is out in space some indeterminate amount of distance away from Earth probably dying a lonely horrible death somehow make you a bad person? So Kaori is officially 22 years old. Isn't that like, the first official mention of a character's age?
You think her "reason's to like sensei" journey thing includes things like "He can breath human oxygen" or something?

No space in my brain to memorize phone numbers or addresses. The only addresses I know are my current, sort of my parents and sort of mine childhood home. I don't even memorize my own phone number, especially not anyone else's unless you include two different emergency numbers. 112 which is my own countries and 911 which, I guess belongs to many other countries like America.

Mc gets offended Haruka has Rin's number and he doesn't... Bro, she's literally Rin's boss. This almost seems like a contractual agreement thing.

Six eggplant emoji's... It's pretty safe to say Molly would date her teacher, wow.

If I could under emergency circumstances rent out a bathhouse for 253$ for an hour which wouldn't exactly break the bank and just means almost one months worth of savings gone, then a rich girl most certainly could and it would indeed be negligible.

Yeah, actually being caught once probably changes your perception on doing sexual stuff in public again.
Also, green haired girl is back. Maybe will get to know her name now.
All of a sudden it's 316$. Huh.

Yeah, I can see it. Ayane would be a good mom. She's kind of one of those "appearances can be deceiving" types. You think she may not be a good one but she would likely surprise you just how good she would be.

I prefer the Ayane that shows some weakness and talks about her problems. This was definitely needed for character development. Talking about Kirin catching them.
You don't suppose Kirin secretly saw the exchange before they entered the in where she caught them? Maybe she hoped to catch them in the first place.

Oh god, Futaba has never snapped like that, has she?

That might be the first time I've seen Rin form the side. Never really knew what was going on with her hair.

Futaba has an eating disorder... That makes sense.

Rich looking girl? Now that's an interesting plot development.
Yeah, just one look at her and I get that rich and elegant feel even down to the hair.
Looking even closer at what she's wearing... yeah, 100% rich girl. Wouldn't be surprised if she's richer than Ayane. But then again, maybe Ayane haven't learned as much discipline as this other girl has.
Okay her name is Touka... Tomonori and Tsukioka aren't difficult to pronounce but reading them would take a couple tries at worst.

I think I get what's going on. Ayane's family is like the modern rich kind. More disorganized and modern in their approach. Meanwhile Touka's family might be the older more traditional kind who put high value on how they appear to others and are more strict. I was gonna say sort of like Tsuneyo's but Tsuneyo's is probably not rich and they went too far on the sheltering part.

Ouch... Touka is the kind of rich girl you hoped Ayane wasn't. Around Ayane you can easily let your guard down and just love her and the things she can do for you. But Touka has that unapproachable aura that Ayane lacks. Intimidating. Of course that doesn't mean the mc isn't gonna try his best to break through that barrier and have his way with her too sooner or later... But it will be a complete 180 from Ayane who loved you from the get go. You are comparing an unrestrained person with a very restrained person, best way of putting it. Childish vs professional and dignified. A joyful person with a frustratingly traditional or something.

Man, I feel bad for Ayane. I guess she no one could have expected this kind of rivalry.
Knowing Ayane dislikes her father and they already have a dojo at home, her chances of preventing the dojo from being bought up doesn't seem very high, unlike her father conveniently hates the family trying to buy it.
I suppose the only reason they aren't asking why they can't just build their own dojo at their estate is because the best karate trainer happens to be Ayane's.

It's a complete clash between old and new when it comes to being wealthy. I have Touka figured out right away. Of course I don't know her secrets yet... every girl seems to have one.

Touka's family is probably the kind who would buy up a place, spend a lot of money building it up, use it for a little while and then throw it away. Certainly seems like that's gonna be the case if Touka plans to learn karate... Guess that opens up a great opportunity for Ayane to beat Touka up a bit and accidentally start a war between two rich families. I started laughing mid way through that sentence.

I'm pretty damn sure if I was there with the mc, Ayane and Touka earlier, I could have talked Touka down from her decision.

Oh great, NOW what is Ayane wearing?
Well that's a new one. "When god gives you lemons, you find a new god"

Been thinking about this for a while now. Maki's clothes are kinda... boyish or unsexy, aren't they? Maybe a little unexpected from someone like her.

"Pointed dual face openings" wtf? Weirdest description for a nose I've heard.

It took me this long to realize Kaori has a spider accessory in her hair.

Wait, pirating is bad? I had no idea! (can you smell the sarcasm?)

Love this sexual dynamic slowly creeping into Miku and his relationship.

Holy fuck, Miku! "If I wanted to touch your heckin' penis I'd have taken off my shorts and gone spread-eagle on the bed for ya already!" I didn't think she had it in her to say something like that!

Wow, mc is being a bit too bold with the hands there! This was only suppose to be a thigh massage!

If there's one thing I've come to learn, it's that you never know when to expect a lewd scene. I guess in a way that's comforting, but in a way the lust counter is a sort of giveaway that it won't go too far.

Ahh yes... It's right about this time that everyone starts getting sick. I can usually avoid that but I hear many just can't. Well, it would have been that reason, if it didn't involve food poisoning instead.

Tonsil hockey... what a disturbing alternative to French kissing.

Oof, lightning always come after the rain and lightning is loud... She looks like a fucking ghost.
Like I'm telling you dude. She has some kind of insane trauma with a loud sound. If it's not the murder by gunshot of someone she knows, it better be a convincing reason to explain the kind of traumatic trance like state she enters.

What do you mean I have a choice? What am I about to see? Choosing the wrong answer sets you back in time.

God damnit, the static got me that time. Just wanted to knock on Mikoto's door in peace. I knew that "Bluejay" name seemed too suspicious. And now that I look closer, it's triggered after some progress with Miku, which just so happens to her little thunder freakout.

That mention of the seed again... Is there a deeper meaning here?

WHAT
Makoto fucking jumped off the roof!?
Wait, did Makoto somehow figure out she's living in a simulation or something? She felt herself jump, she probably felt herself hit the ground and now she's back at the top like it never happened and having an internal meltdown from it.
But wtf? What even prompted this? Why would she do that? Is there something we don't yet know?
Now I'm speechless. What am i suppose to make of that?

"I'm sure she's fine" After what she just pulled, I don't think she is.

Yep, need to do that event with Makoto to visit Maki and it's pretty safe to say I know why she's so out of it. How would you feel trying to make such a drastic action only to discover the world doesn't want you to do that?

Maki: "As long as you are not screwing my daughter-"
Me: "about that..."
Mc: "about that..."
Same brain cells.
Some slight changes but nothing major.

This tierlist is starting to confuse me. Where the hell do I put Miku when I find out the exact reason to her loud noise reactions? I have a pretty solid theory as to what it would be but that seems too convenient.



Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

spoilers.title: Tierlist
spoilers.html:
This tierlist is starting to confuse me. Where the hell do I put Miku when I find out the exact reason to her loud noise reactions? I have a pretty solid theory as to what it would be but that seems too convenient.



Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

I may forgive characters over time for a past mistake, bumping them back up.

A character most likely won't lose their position just because I haven't seen them enough in a while.


Some edited since yesterday.
Yumi: I can't WAIT to see how the story with her escalates. Every time he messes with her, it's so fun and I like her appearance too.
Ayane: She's obsessed with you. Her lack of a father figure hurts her more than I realized...
Ami: Red hair, she loves you.
Chika: I expected an annoying gyaru girl who acts way too popular but I got someone chill and down to earth, fun to be around.
Makoto: I love it when he messes with her. I slightly dislike her hair and how studious she is.
Sana: Very precious.
Sara: Hot mom, I repeat, hot mom!
Maya: The mystery behind her is intriguing.
Miku: Not usually into tomboys.
Futaba: Not into big girls or big tits.
Rin: Nice hair. A bit bland unless Chika is around. Also seem to have a bit of a wingman personality.
Kirin: Surprisingly flirtatious... and intimidatingly so. Perhaps a bit manipulative and evil.
Karin: Absolutely adorable how bad she is with boys.
Chinami: So adorable! Must protecc!
Molly: She can be anywhere.
Haruka: Breasts are way too large for my liking but otherwise she's ok.
Kaori: Her eccentric personality is growing on me. Not a fan of the spider tattoo.
Tsuneyo: This one is rough... extremely sheltered type.
Uta: Absolutely adorable maid.

We couldn't share information as easily in the pre-internet days as we can now. Countries were more or less creating these systems in a vacuum.

Hell, rotary phones didn't even work the same way in every country. Each number dialed sends a set number of pulses, but in some countries, 1 sent 1 pulse and 9 sent 9 pulses, and in others, 1 sent 9 pulses and 9 sent 1 pulse.

Modern (post-internet) globalisation has changed how new systems are developed so that they're more standardized, but those old existing systems are so entrenched that changing them would be dangerous. The sheer expense of "911 is now 000" marketing to make sure everybody knows about the change alone ensures that no country will risk it.

Ma1phas said:
I generally agree with this idea. Renpy style games could do without the grinding, but having definite stops to do things at the players own pace, or access repeatables, secondary gameplay elements or such adds something to the experience. It's mostly monkey brain logic, but the illusion of choice makes it still feel somewhat like a game, rather than just reading.

LiL is probably one of the worst examples for it, though. No hints, many events obscurely hidden, a huge number of them only trigger on specific days, grinding for point requirements to start them rather than just click to start the next part, no secondary gameplay elements other than the repeatables which only get variation maybe once per chapter. And the ever present concern that the next event will lock you into a long chain with an obnoxious puzzle.
I recall someone referring to LiL's gameplay loop as hostile, which I think is pretty accurate.

posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
Then, the event takes place on december 28 because it's always december 28, even if it is two days after it. The days in Kumon-mi, as the passage of time, are fictional - in the real world it's always dec 28, they never left. No one ages, nothing changes, and even when they do, it reverts back.
Click to expand...
DeSkel15 said:
The next two days don't actually seem to change the date, as it's still said to be Dec 28th during 'Untitled':
Click to expand...
Isn't this boggling...

If you load a save and play through these events while paying attention to the weekday indicator, you'll find that Sensei spends Wednesday and Thursday to persuade Yumi and Tsuneyo to come to the sleepover, then on Friday the "Today is 12/28/20" Sensei monologue takes place, then on Sunday the sleepover begins, then it remains on Sunday when amiokay declares "Today is 12/28/20". Script-wise, there is a totaldays += 2 and day = 7 in that event, so a normal passage of time is at least consciously set by Selly himself during some part of the event.

Thus, if the weekday indicator and the script are valid evidences, I think at least up until the sleepover is cut short and before everything goes beyond common logics, the flow of time from Sensei making calls to RAS assemble is in the right speed and direction, cementing the idea that the sleepover really is 12/30/20. The question then goes to "Why does amiokay says it is 12/28/20 after cutting off RAS sleepover?"

A few options I have are:
- Perhaps this is amiokay directly taunting Sensei's previous introspection, mocking him about trying to figure out something but can't. The actual date is 12/30/20.

- Since actively researching resets is apparently strictly prohibited, perhaps this is an indication that RAS's efforts in gathering people together gets undone by some mechanisms similar to renpy rollback. Sleepover thus becomes "did not happen" due to time reversal and the actual date has gone back to 12/28/20.

- Team HOPE forces the date back to 12/28/20 in a deliberate attempt to have the 5th reset puzzle take place on Himawari's birthday and have her participate as well (hence the Untitled Children's Show). It has nothing to do with when Sensei makes that monologue or when RAS arranges sleepover. What team HOPE wishes to achieve via this is unknown.

- Selly fucked up. Sensei should've had that monologue during instead of before the sleepover.

- It doesn't matter. Regardless of when you arrive here, you'd better believe it when a trans-dimensional girl tells you today is 12/28/20 while the fabric of spacetime is melting.

Day 17 character count 12634. Felt like an abrupt end but I've been waking up at 2 pm the last two days and that's just not okay at all.
Think this new guitar girl is Rin's type?
Well, sort of. Only time will tell.

Also guitar girl looked down at the ground after Rin shouted at mc to leave her alone.

I don't know what to say here. Wingman mc got Rin to say a bunch of nice things to guitar girl including that Rin would give anything to kiss her. A bit too fast, isn't it?
I guess in a way it worked. Got the message across that Rin is attracted to guitar girl without too much backlash.
Guitar girl has been upgraded to Otoha. So many unique names I've never heard in this game.

Rin taking revenge by making it seem like mc is a stalker.

Ate dessert for 3 hours... wtf?

Well, I have officially completed all character events for this chapter.

Little does Molly know that 500 headpats is enough to trigger an orgasm and she wants 1000. Brave girl.

Molly have a much higher chance at losing virginia than Tsuneyo. I mean, Tsuneyo probably doesn't even know where Virginia is and have less real world experience so... what does my joke even mean? How do you lose a country? What are the conditions for losing it?

Throwback to that time Makoto LITERALLY jumped/(or intentionally fell?) off the school building and is now basically having an existential crisis.
Uhh, yeah. That face says it all. Had the mc not had his eyes closed, the moment she did the thing, would she have spawned back up?
I think her eyes look like his but with a mix of her own eye color. Coincidence? Maybe... but probably not.
Even if I'm reacting to all of this I still think I downplay the fact that Makoto did that. Have any characters done anything before that makes their world seem like a simulation or something? I think Makoto is the only one. And based on what is happening right now, that DID happen. Not a happy event, not some other worldly activity, no, she literally experienced something she wasn't suppose to. And I think the reason she did that was because he told her about that dream. He wasn't suppose to yet he did and this was the consequence. A broken Makoto.

What purpose is there to hiding secrets when the world is not what it seems? Makoto just became dangerous to the mc.
Wth? The mc was suppose to drag Mikoto aside, not Miku!

If it was me, I would just go straight for the kill and ask Makoto "What happened at the rooftop while my eyes were closed and I found you crying and silent as if in shock?"
This mc is an idiot. He just had a talk with Miku and came to the realization when the change took place. He saw her fucking crying, silent and in shock when he opened his eyes. It's pretty fucking clear that's when something happened. His not asking the right questions, his not even encouraging her to tell him what she thought he would think she was crazy for saying. She's not even repeating the part about the dream he told her about. If it weren't for the fact the player saw what happened that night, maybe I would have been equally as confused as the player but I find that hard to believe given her realized it all started after that night.

I don't remember but did the karaoke thing happen right before the first reset? It's possible that if it happened way before the reset that what Maya said about him taking too long might be true.

Being open about your interests is one thing, but you can easily make a copy pasted super advanced password and then add whatever childish nonsense you want to put at the end or beginning. At least that way it's both childish and secure. Fking casual mc.

Two separate bags for 2 scarfs? Are you serious? That's such a waste of material!

Wait, is that officially Maya's first blush? Let me guess. Never in any previous cycle has the mc ever given her something she actually likes let alone given her anything at all. Seeing Maya blushing for once seems so surreal. And a smile? What is this, Christmas? Oh wait... And cries? Wtf? Have she ever blushed, smiled or cried? Let alone all three at the same time? And what about as the actual Maya and not whatever happy dream version of her there is?
What is it about this scarf that's so special...?
I mean, considering those scarfs were not even suppose to be there in the first place and just so happen to be there during the time he came to visit, it's pretty obvious to assume someone or something wanted her to have it.

I feel like I would be weird if I try to look for every moment where Maya has smiled, blushed or cried.
Well, at least it's heartwarming to see Maya acting more human for once. Maybe it's been mentioned in the past that Maya don't like appearing weak but now that message has come across nicely. More moments like that and I might actually warm up to Maya some as well.

spoilers.title: Tierlist
spoilers.html:
No changes here. Although Kirin is getting on my nerves so there's that.



Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

I may forgive characters over time for a past mistake, bumping them back up.

A character most likely won't lose their position just because I haven't seen them enough in a while.


Some edited since yesterday.
Yumi: I can't WAIT to see how the story with her escalates. Every time he messes with her, it's so fun and I like her appearance too.
Ayane: She's obsessed with you. Her lack of a father figure hurts her more than I realized...
Ami: Red hair, she loves you.
Chika: I expected an annoying gyaru girl who acts way too popular but I got someone chill and down to earth, fun to be around.
Makoto: I love it when he messes with her. I slightly dislike her hair and how studious she is.
Sana: Very precious.
Sara: Hot mom, I repeat, hot mom!
Maya: The mystery behind her is intriguing.
Miku: Not usually into tomboys.
Futaba: Not into big girls or big tits.
Rin: Nice hair. A bit bland unless Chika is around. Also seem to have a bit of a wingman personality.
Kirin: Surprisingly flirtatious... and intimidatingly so. Perhaps a bit manipulative and evil.
Karin: Absolutely adorable how bad she is with boys.
Chinami: So adorable! Must protecc!
Molly: She can be anywhere.
Haruka: Breasts are way too large for my liking but otherwise she's ok.
Kaori: Her eccentric personality is growing on me. Not a fan of the spider tattoo.
Tsuneyo: This one is rough... extremely sheltered type.
Uta: Absolutely adorable maid.

barglenarglezous said:
The whole story of Altair and Vega on their date is telegraphing what's coming. Now that he's coming back to himself, it's only a matter of time before she loses herself. Like Altair and Vega, they are ships passing in the night. Any time they get together as their true selves is fleeting. Once she recognized him as himself, and not the echo of himself he had been for so many cycles, she knew her remaining time was limited.

However, the Altair and Vega story includes the idea that, one night a year, the birds build a bridge that allows the lovers to get together. So there's that, too.

posts.content_html_raw:
Maybe I'm crazy, but of late while playing LIL, I've been getting this odd feeling that when the game is completed, we're going to learn that the whole reset thing is a kind of time travel loop that Sensei is caught up in, likely having gone back to 'correct' something he did, and got stuck in. However like Quantum Leap's plotline, due to how the time travel works, he loses all his own memories and ends up with a kind of swiss cheese memory. If this idea is true, then it also could make sense if in a kind of longer version of Groundhog Day (taking place over several months, instead of just one day), that over time situations could happen which might have the people going through it become aware of the time loop. Perhaps the nexus point being the school roof which they have to always go to to 'survive' the reset. I could see, perhaps, Maya stumbling across that in one of the resets, and coming to realize what's going on; then going through multiple versions of Sensei before the 'real' Sensei appears again.

As to how she might stumble across it, who's to say that Sensei himself didn't do the same thing for a while, and then invite Maya up there to meet him; only to not make it up there himself and get locked 'outside' the protective bubble, forcing her to try to figure out what's going on herself. Alternatively, it could be something simple, like a kind of butterfly effect situation where a seemingly simple previous choice Sensei and Maya made saw her up there when the reset happened, and he didn't make it.

The earlier reference to a paradox makes me suspect that in the time we have until around Dec 30 when the reset happens; something is out of place. Above and beyond the weirdness we see with Nao and Kaori, or Yasu. I've often wondered if it'd be a good idea to go through the various 'events' in chronological order, looking for ones that seem to repeat and which should be reasonably similar in regards to the cast involved, and look for something out of place. Though honestly, given the game is a work in progress... I doubt I'd find an answer that way. However, it wouldn't surprise me in the least to see that the answer to what was the paradox, and what was causing the repeated looping, was already present in the story of the game, and it's just been overlooked to this point.

I think fondly of Selebus. There is a purposefulness in that phrasing: we should be conscious each time we say 'Selebus,' for it is a moniker chosen specifically for the purpose of releasing Lessons in Love (perhaps at first to partially obfuscate his identity while releasing a rape simulator, but also perhaps to more generously engage in roleplaying from the start). Every time we speak or act under a name we have chosen for ourselves, it is an act of character-building, and thus when evaluating the actions of others online we benefit from thinking of them as mere thespians upon the digital stage. There is a naïve understanding that every word or deed comes from some mystical imagined heart, but in that interpretation we must ask: what about the heartless?

Selebus is an endlessly rich character. Look at how we expound upon him and devote so many hours of thought in his name. Look at how he has invaded the castles of our mind and made himself snug in the corner of each room. Look at how he feeds us with sprinklings of japes and hostility. Have you ever considered why it is that one of the most enduring images in history is that of a jester shedding a tear? Why so many clown masks have distorted, weeping visages? It is a sad fate for clowns that with their gift for comedy and entertainment must come crippling illnesses of the opposite sort; those who put on a mask have the most to hide, and it is in the process of hiding that, indeed, the mask becomes so prominent. Just look at Selebus's posts here. How cute it is as he cloaks and shadows himself. How heartwarming it as he doles out the right degree of derision and spite to rile us up. How delightful it is as we devote so many thoughts to dissecting his antics.

What do we want from an author? The answer will probably change depending on the person. Death of the author is in the vogue nowadays, and it's likely the ideal author is a sort of machine that produces a mass amount of content with little to no audience interaction. As it stands the AI of the future may be just that. Alternatively, we may like obsequious authors; we may like kind and sensitive authors, Brandon Sanderson-likes who with their faithful creed treat all with kindness and compassion. There are many preferences as there are people. What I like is someone interesting. Someone with a conscious mind who acts individually. Someone who puts on a damn good show. It's always madness around which I find myself revolving, and Selebus is a delightful example. Come, gather and bear witness to his opera, now in the making! His script is the height of cliche, I am forced to admit, and yet his actors are of the finest fold; beyond exquisite. Thus, I believe you will find it enthralling!

As for the person behind the mask - he who appears when curtains fall and the performance ends - who cares?
I shall not be one to imagine an individual in my mind and subsequently dole out empty judgement upon them, for if I am a judge and jury it is in a courtroom with no attendants.
As for getting banned from a discord, having a negative video game experience, feeling condescended upon - who cares?
It may be you. But it is not I. For my smile only grows wider, with only a single tear in my eye.

Every time we speak or act under a name we have chosen for ourselves, it is an act of character-building, and thus when evaluating the actions of others online we benefit from thinking of them as mere thespians upon the digital stage. There is a naïve understanding that every word or deed comes from some mystical imagined heart, but in that interpretation we must ask: what about the heartless?
Selebus is an endlessly rich character. Look at how we expound upon him and devote so many hours of thought in his name. Look at how he has invaded the castles of our mind and made himself snug in the corner of each room. Look at how he feeds us with sprinklings of japes and hostility. Have you ever considered why it is that one of the most enduring images in history is that of a jester shedding a tear? Why so many clown masks have distorted, weeping visages? It is a sad fate for clowns that with their gift for comedy and entertainment must come crippling illnesses of the opposite sort; those who put on a mask have the most to hide, and it is in the process of hiding that, indeed, the mask becomes so prominent. Just look at Selebus's posts here. How cute it is as he cloaks and shadows himself. How heartwarming it as he doles out the right degree of derision and spite to rile us up. How delightful it is as we devote so many thoughts to dissecting his antics.
What do we want from an author? The answer will probably change depending on the person. Death of the author is in the vogue nowadays, and it's likely the ideal author is a sort of machine that produces a mass amount of content with little to no audience interaction. As it stands the AI of the future may be just that. Alternatively, we may like obsequious authors; we may like kind and sensitive authors, Brandon Sanderson-likes who with their faithful creed treat all with kindness and compassion. There are many preferences as there are people. What I like is someone interesting. Someone with a conscious mind who acts individually. Someone who puts on a damn good show. It's always madness around which I find myself revolving, and Selebus is a delightful example. Come, gather and bear witness to his opera, now in the making! His script is the height of cliche, I am forced to admit, and yet his actors are of the finest fold; beyond exquisite. Thus, I believe you will find it enthralling!
As for the person behind the mask - he who appears when curtains fall and the performance ends - who cares?
I shall not be one to imagine an individual in my mind and subsequently dole out empty judgement upon them, for if I am a judge and jury it is in a courtroom with no attendants.
As for getting banned from a discord, having a negative video game experience, feeling condescended upon - who cares?
It may be you. But it is not I. For my smile only grows wider, with only a single tear in my eye.

It's my random musings about chapter 2 again. So, this isn't about a single event, but more about the general outline of certain plotlines upon rewatch. And a few random tidbits at the end:

1. Firstly, about the Otoha x Rin thing. I find it interesting that, regardless of how things will go, their relationship seemed doomed from the start by things I didn't really recall.
When they first start their relationship, Otoha was afraid that she was going to be Rin's rebound after Chika. And later it's revealed through a game of truth and dare that Chika would have dated Rin if Akira didn't show up.



Now, obviously, this doesn't make Otoha's fears true. Rin was not using her as a rebound, she truly jumped into the relationship. The issue is that Rin is very hormonal, and although I believe she was being truthful in everything, the sad truth is that she loved Akira - while her feelings for Otoha were much more hormonal than having someone that actually cared for her in a healthy way (yeah, that one was Akira, shocking, right?).



And I'm not talking just about him being her father figure, although that's obviously true. I mean love love, especially on the good homie path.



After getting together with Otoha she still has her depression/cutting episodes because, yeah, that's how actual clinical depression works. And after her recovery she confesses that she loves him. Multiple times in fact. It's just not something that she's ready to face in a romantic manner (especially when she already has a girlfriend and Futaba - and all the others, like Chika - love him as well, and are more advanced in it than she is), but it is there.



This leads Rin to trying to set him up with others in bizarre ways, like compelling him to actually date Futaba, making her very uncomfortable. She does the same to other people as well, albeit not that strongly. I think this happens because she wants him to be in a relationship so that she can settle her love for him in a safer way.



Regarding Otoha part of the deal, she has to ditch Rin during the christmas party because of her parents and reveals that they don't know about her. This leads to Akira trying to help her reconcile with Rin, which leads to him seeing her being attracted to Niki during lessons - which Niki says that she's aware of and it is to be expected of everyone anyway, and they're teenagers. I don't have enough evidence at the moment to ascertain if Rin was supposed to be a "rebound" for Niki at this point, but it does seem like Otoha likes Rin at the very least.



I feel like it's ironic that they're on this double date because Rin loves Akira, and Otoha is attracted to Niki. Although obviously Rin is being taken advantage of by Otoha, because, again, Rin puts herself in this position by putting her all onto someone that barely gives anything back (something that Otoha would point out in the future).

Basically, they're teenagers doing teenage stuff. All this rambling is just because this happened:



And yes, that is basically what breaks them in the end. This is not a perfect prediction of course because it's not that Otoha eventually breaks up with Rin because of her being a girl, but rather because she's another girl. Rin will keep making herself a victim of their relationship, and Otoha will keep taking advantage of her until enough is enough.

Funnily enough, from Akira's perspective, he muses that it is this relationship blowing up in Rin's face that would ultimately lead her to him 100%, and that Otoha being attracted to Niki would lead her in his direction as well. So for him everything is a-okay - with the exception of Rin being hurt. But I'm talking from memory about these future events, so I'm looking forward to them in the replay.
2. Multiple Maya smiles to remind everyone that I had to drink a lot of water after this event (This isn't a joke, I cried so much that I had to stop playing for some time).



She just loves him so much.
3. And lastly, it's heartwarming to see Yumi caring about Akira.


There was this scene where he delivers her Yuki's gift, and for a moment she thinks it's his. And man... The only reason that she's not his girlfriend is because Akira doesn't want it. Because if he dropped the other girls and actually made an effort for two or three events, she'd be his.



Then when she meets Yuki again, Akira is extremely respectful to Yumi - which leads to her testing him in a moment of vulnerability to see if he'd kiss her again:



Akira blacks out in the middle of this and fights hard to not do anything, and manages to say he won't hurt her. And she's visibly torn between wanting him to kiss her and being happy that she can trust him a bit more.



Then, when she apologises to Futaba and stops her bullying entirely, he says he's proud of her. And despite what she says, she's clearly thankful for his support.

4. Oh, I also have these:
Yasu waited until everyone was gone to try the karaoke because she didn't want to bother anyone.



she gets embarrassed that Akira heard her, but then turns happy when he compliments her and says that she'll try hard to become better.



Noriko is really pitiful because everytime she gets with Akira she either breaks down crying or puts many restrictions on them becoming intimate, which only makes it so that Akira gets back together with Niki before her (and a lot of people too). i understand why she does this of course, but it's still pitiful due to how much it backfires.




Chika first shows her "I get it" tendencies around this time as well. As she tries to play boyfriend/girlfriend in school and at the mall, and Akira tells her that she really needs to slowdown. Like, she actually asks him for her and Chinami to move in and get Ami out of the house in three years (???). Well, from this moment on she kind of made herself a prisoner of her feelings and we know where that led.



Molly's deal wasn't as hard to deal with it in retrospect. And the problem really was just Akira being, in the words of our one true bro, a little bitch. Now, I'm not condoning his actions, but the truth of the matter is that Molly had already masturbated, changed clothes and even talked about experimenting with him. IF Akira was the actual scumbag he is sometimes, he'd have lied about it. "yeah, you were drunk and I guess I should have rejected you, but we ended up playing around and that was it". Problem solved.

All he did was not do anything, and Molly had to reach this conclusion, apologise to him and then when he said he didn't remember, she had them agree on the best possible possibility about what had happened. So yeah, huge nothingburger. Although I guess it allowed Kirin to declare that she'd be okay with him raping people if she could watch.



Himawari's first appearance, that Akira will remember, also happens around this time, after he leaves Sara's appartment and finds himself outside the school that Maya takes him to. I mention this because Maya also says that the festival takes place in a district where buses don't go anymore, on account of the school over there having been deactivated.

So it's likely to be this school (and also Sara's school, that he visits during a happy event - and also possibly Sekai's school, and further possibly the school that we see during that one happy event where Akira is talking to Maya at the roof and she's his girlfriend), which also is in the same district with the out of order shrine that we see during Maya's date (likely). Just thought I'd mention it.

Yasu waited until everyone was gone to try the karaoke because she didn't want to bother anyone.



she gets embarrassed that Akira heard her, but then turns happy when he compliments her and says that she'll try hard to become better.



Noriko is really pitiful because everytime she gets with Akira she either breaks down crying or puts many restrictions on them becoming intimate, which only makes it so that Akira gets back together with Niki before her (and a lot of people too). i understand why she does this of course, but it's still pitiful due to how much it backfires.




Chika first shows her "I get it" tendencies around this time as well. As she tries to play boyfriend/girlfriend in school and at the mall, and Akira tells her that she really needs to slowdown. Like, she actually asks him for her and Chinami to move in and get Ami out of the house in three years (???). Well, from this moment on she kind of made herself a prisoner of her feelings and we know where that led.



Molly's deal wasn't as hard to deal with it in retrospect. And the problem really was just Akira being, in the words of our one true bro, a little bitch. Now, I'm not condoning his actions, but the truth of the matter is that Molly had already masturbated, changed clothes and even talked about experimenting with him. IF Akira was the actual scumbag he is sometimes, he'd have lied about it. "yeah, you were drunk and I guess I should have rejected you, but we ended up playing around and that was it". Problem solved.

All he did was not do anything, and Molly had to reach this conclusion, apologise to him and then when he said he didn't remember, she had them agree on the best possible possibility about what had happened. So yeah, huge nothingburger. Although I guess it allowed Kirin to declare that she'd be okay with him raping people if she could watch.



Himawari's first appearance, that Akira will remember, also happens around this time, after he leaves Sara's appartment and finds himself outside the school that Maya takes him to. I mention this because Maya also says that the festival takes place in a district where buses don't go anymore, on account of the school over there having been deactivated.

So it's likely to be this school (and also Sara's school, that he visits during a happy event - and also possibly Sekai's school, and further possibly the school that we see during that one happy event where Akira is talking to Maya at the roof and she's his girlfriend), which also is in the same district with the out of order shrine that we see during Maya's date (likely). Just thought I'd mention it.

It's my random musings about chapter 2 again. So, this isn't about a single event, but more about the general outline of certain plotlines upon rewatch. And a few random tidbits at the end:

1. Firstly, about the Otoha x Rin thing. I find it interesting that, regardless of how things will go, their relationship seemed doomed from the start by things I didn't really recall.
When they first start their relationship, Otoha was afraid that she was going to be Rin's rebound after Chika. And later it's revealed through a game of truth and dare that Chika would have dated Rin if Akira didn't show up.

View attachment 4390576

Now, obviously, this doesn't make Otoha's fears true. Rin was not using her as a rebound, she truly jumped into the relationship. The issue is that Rin is very hormonal, and although I believe she was being truthful in everything, the sad truth is that she loved Akira - while her feelings for Otoha were much more hormonal than having someone that actually cared for her in a healthy way (yeah, that one was Akira, shocking, right?).

View attachment 4390584

And I'm not talking just about him being her father figure, although that's obviously true. I mean love love, especially on the good homie path.

View attachment 4390585

After getting together with Otoha she still has her depression/cutting episodes because, yeah, that's how actual clinical depression works. And after her recovery she confesses that she loves him. Multiple times in fact. It's just not something that she's ready to face in a romantic manner (especially when she already has a girlfriend and Futaba - and all the others, like Chika - love him as well, and are more advanced in it than she is), but it is there.

View attachment 4390589

This leads Rin to trying to set him up with others in bizarre ways, like compelling him to actually date Futaba, making her very uncomfortable. She does the same to other people as well, albeit not that strongly. I think this happens because she wants him to be in a relationship so that she can settle her love for him in a safer way.

View attachment 4390592

Regarding Otoha part of the deal, she has to ditch Rin during the christmas party because of her parents and reveals that they don't know about her. This leads to Akira trying to help her reconcile with Rin, which leads to him seeing her being attracted to Niki during lessons - which Niki says that she's aware of and it is to be expected of everyone anyway, and they're teenagers. I don't have enough evidence at the moment to ascertain if Rin was supposed to be a "rebound" for Niki at this point, but it does seem like Otoha likes Rin at the very least.

View attachment 4390597

I feel like it's ironic that they're on this double date because Rin loves Akira, and Otoha is attracted to Niki. Although obviously Rin is being taken advantage of by Otoha, because, again, Rin puts herself in this position by putting her all onto someone that barely gives anything back (something that Otoha would point out in the future).

Basically, they're teenagers doing teenage stuff. All this rambling is just because this happened:

View attachment 4390605 View attachment 4390606

And yes, that is basically what breaks them in the end. This is not a perfect prediction of course because it's not that Otoha eventually breaks up with Rin because of her being a girl, but rather because she's another girl. Rin will keep making herself a victim of their relationship, and Otoha will keep taking advantage of her until enough is enough.

Funnily enough, from Akira's perspective, he muses that it is this relationship blowing up in Rin's face that would ultimately lead her to him 100%, and that Otoha being attracted to Niki would lead her in his direction as well. So for him everything is a-okay - with the exception of Rin being hurt. But I'm talking from memory about these future events, so I'm looking forward to them in the replay.
2. Multiple Maya smiles to remind everyone that I had to drink a lot of water after this event (This isn't a joke, I cried so much that I had to stop playing for some time).
View attachment 4390623 View attachment 4390622 View attachment 4390625 View attachment 4390624 View attachment 4390626 View attachment 4390627 View attachment 4390628 View attachment 4390629
View attachment 4390637

She just loves him so much.
3. And lastly, it's heartwarming to see Yumi caring about Akira.
View attachment 4390642

There was this scene where he delivers her Yuki's gift, and for a moment she thinks it's his. And man... The only reason that she's not his girlfriend is because Akira doesn't want it. Because if he dropped the other girls and actually made an effort for two or three events, she'd be his.

View attachment 4390650

Then when she meets Yuki again, Akira is extremely respectful to Yumi - which leads to her testing him in a moment of vulnerability to see if he'd kiss her again:

View attachment 4390651

Akira blacks out in the middle of this and fights hard to not do anything, and manages to say he won't hurt her. And she's visibly torn between wanting him to kiss her and being happy that she can trust him a bit more.

View attachment 4390655

Then, when she apologises to Futaba and stops her bullying entirely, he says he's proud of her. And despite what she says, she's clearly thankful for his support.

View attachment 4390657
4. Oh, I also have these:
Yasu waited until everyone was gone to try the karaoke because she didn't want to bother anyone.

she gets embarrassed that Akira heard her, but then turns happy when he compliments her and says that she'll try hard to become better.

View attachment 4390663

Noriko is really pitiful because everytime she gets with Akira she either breaks down crying or puts many restrictions on them becoming intimate, which only makes it so that Akira gets back together with Niki before her (and a lot of people too). i understand why she does this of course, but it's still pitiful due to how much it backfires.

View attachment 4390667
View attachment 4390671

Chika first shows her "I get it" tendencies around this time as well. As she tries to play boyfriend/girlfriend in school and at the mall, and Akira tells her that she really needs to slowdown. Like, she actually asks him for her and Chinami to move in and get Ami out of the house in three years (???). Well, from this moment on she kind of made herself a prisoner of her feelings and we know where that led.

View attachment 4390674

Molly's deal wasn't as hard to deal with it in retrospect. And the problem really was just Akira being, in the words of our one true bro, a little bitch. Now, I'm not condoning his actions, but the truth of the matter is that Molly had already masturbated, changed clothes and even talked about experimenting with him. IF Akira was the actual scumbag he is sometimes, he'd have lied about it. "yeah, you were drunk and I guess I should have rejected you, but we ended up playing around and that was it". Problem solved.

All he did was not do anything, and Molly had to reach this conclusion, apologise to him and then when he said he didn't remember, she had them agree on the best possible possibility about what had happened. So yeah, huge nothingburger. Although I guess it allowed Kirin to declare that she'd be okay with him raping people if she could watch.

I mention this because Maya also says that the festival takes place in a district where buses don't go anymore, on account of the school over there having been deactivated.

2. I think this was my favorite sequence in the whole game so far. Should have known what was coming. Whew.

3. Yeah. Yumi.

4. Chapter 2 is the beginning of Akira trying not to be a complete dick — and mostly failing.

spoilers.title: Rin x Otoha
spoilers.html:
When they first start their relationship, Otoha was afraid that she was going to be Rin's rebound after Chika. And later it's revealed through a game of truth and dare that Chika would have dated Rin if Akira didn't show up.

View attachment 4390576

Now, obviously, this doesn't make Otoha's fears true. Rin was not using her as a rebound, she truly jumped into the relationship. The issue is that Rin is very hormonal, and although I believe she was being truthful in everything, the sad truth is that she loved Akira - while her feelings for Otoha were much more hormonal than having someone that actually cared for her in a healthy way (yeah, that one was Akira, shocking, right?).

View attachment 4390584

And I'm not talking just about him being her father figure, although that's obviously true. I mean love love, especially on the good homie path.

View attachment 4390585

After getting together with Otoha she still has her depression/cutting episodes because, yeah, that's how actual clinical depression works. And after her recovery she confesses that she loves him. Multiple times in fact. It's just not something that she's ready to face in a romantic manner (especially when she already has a girlfriend and Futaba - and all the others, like Chika - love him as well, and are more advanced in it than she is), but it is there.

View attachment 4390589

This leads Rin to trying to set him up with others in bizarre ways, like compelling him to actually date Futaba, making her very uncomfortable. She does the same to other people as well, albeit not that strongly. I think this happens because she wants him to be in a relationship so that she can settle her love for him in a safer way.

View attachment 4390592

Regarding Otoha part of the deal, she has to ditch Rin during the christmas party because of her parents and reveals that they don't know about her. This leads to Akira trying to help her reconcile with Rin, which leads to him seeing her being attracted to Niki during lessons - which Niki says that she's aware of and it is to be expected of everyone anyway, and they're teenagers. I don't have enough evidence at the moment to ascertain if Rin was supposed to be a "rebound" for Niki at this point, but it does seem like Otoha likes Rin at the very least.

View attachment 4390597

I feel like it's ironic that they're on this double date because Rin loves Akira, and Otoha is attracted to Niki. Although obviously Rin is being taken advantage of by Otoha, because, again, Rin puts herself in this position by putting her all onto someone that barely gives anything back (something that Otoha would point out in the future).

Basically, they're teenagers doing teenage stuff. All this rambling is just because this happened:

View attachment 4390605 View attachment 4390606

And yes, that is basically what breaks them in the end. This is not a perfect prediction of course because it's not that Otoha eventually breaks up with Rin because of her being a girl, but rather because she's another girl. posts.content_html_raw:
fdsasdf_p said:
Since many are on their replay, I seek fresh eyes for an age-old question of mine about a certain conversation by the end of Ch2. Why did Uta skip her work unannounced? What happened?
View attachment 4380070
This event is within the 4th reset event chain, so the last time Sensei privately spoke to Uta prior to this would be Uta's Blood Everywhere, or anywhere during the 2nd Christmas party (particularly, Dodging Snowflakes) if updates can establish some chronological order. Then, the first time Sensei had any meaningful conversation with Uta is by the end of Creatures of Habits. However, none of the event above really gives solid enough hints on why Uta skipped work without notice and I can't find any direct confirmation about anything related.

Now, even if Uta's past has not been revealed yet at that time, I am all about attributing this mysterious absence to her not feeling like working due to perhaps unsolicitedly receiving more of her own nudes yet again. Judging from what Uta said by the end of Creatures of Habits, it's easy to intentionally believe that Uta here was insinuating that her nightmare had recently resurfaced.
View attachment 4380171

What stops from just assuming so is that:
- That's not the only possible take on her words. Moreover, Uta actually looked pretty bashfully happy when delivering those words, so she might be implying her trend of having crushes rather than something haunting. Even bringing up "her pictures" would significantly dim her aura, so it doesn't really feel fitting here.
- Even if she did recently received her own nudes around the time of Somnambula, a direct confirmation on the cause/effect is still lacking (i.e., skipping work is true and receiving nudes is true, but is receiving nudes leading to skipping work true?)
- When Uta finally confided to Io in Neverender about receiving nudes again, Uta seemed to be talking only about that one scenario in After the Rain when she washed Sensei's back. I feel like Uta would've mentioned that it actually had already happened twice if we want to assume her skipping work all the way back in Ch2 was caused by nudes. It would be something like "I was about to go to work...then my phone went off" and "then months later I was about to take a bath...then my phone went off", for example. Instead, she made it sound like the nude she got during After the Rain was something that happened for the first time after a long while.
View attachment 4380204
(I took the liberty of believing that she was not being completely honest when she said "I was about to take a bath" when confiding to Io)

So, my actual question is did I miss something? Was her absence actually being brought up and discussed in some other events so I don't have to make this assumption that isn't that impeccable in my book?
Click to expand...
I've made it to this point and Uta's missing completely that day. The first one to notice is Ami, as you have pointed out. The second is Ayane:
There are very big chances that something happened and it was reset. In fact, upon rewatching Somnambula in context, Ami seems to be experiencing blackouts herself. It starts to happen when she takes a look at Sekai's poem in her cellphone and blacks out, which doesn't affect Akira at all. Actually, it's interesting because I'd assume it's what other people see as he goes into an episode.

Then Akira blacks out during somnambula. Then Ami starts blacking out again during the light of last summer.
While not a conclusive answer, it's likely that something happened to Uta, just as we assume that Chinami and old man Tojo did die during one of the resets and were brought back. For something to have happened to Uta, could be a stalker catching up to her, or just what she explains later, that they sent her another message. I don't think anything else could have happened to Uta as her backstory is just that.

Mind you, regarding Uta so far, she had already almost kissed Akira at karaoke, and Io told her they should run away together (the three of them). She also tried to seduce Akira by taking him to the mall to try out clothes and continue the date (but Maki intervenes). She's very much into Akira by this point. But that doesn't help with the mystery, since Akira doesn't hear from her during the reset about to happen.
I'll open the topic again if following events mention it, but I think you got that covered.
