I'm watching in silent amusement as Yumi is struggling with her "gift".
Honestly I'm kinda bummed he didn't somehow end up with an embarrassing present for her.
...Charming note.
Welp. I guess this holiday event didn't lack Yumi after all.
Well, I don't know what must be more shameful for Yumi. Having to gift him a "present" or having to admit she's too poor to let him keep it. Will she remain this poor forever? I hope not.

Tsuneyo's dialogue is funny sometimes.
"Please help. I must open this door to complete the quest assigned to me. I saw the others use a card to open the door, but the only card I have is for the library and it won't work. Probably because this isn't a library. I feel like a fool. Please help."

Unpopular opinion. The average person should not be allowed to use or buy fireworks. The number of times some nearby neighbour have started me in the middle of the night on random days throughout the years... I have grown to hate fireworks. Also that is a crime likely punishable by fine. Anyway, got sidetracked there.

Note to self: Never say "What?" if a girl says "knock-knock" to start a joke.

Ahem, as a redditor I am well aware of what "anti-jokes" are. (I know one of you started cringing at that, out yourself)

Rip students. Death by space explosions disguised as fireworks.

OH, OH NO!
Rin: "Woah! Maya-advice! Is this what it feels like to be Sensei?"
Maya: "I don't know. Do you suddenly have the urge to molest the entirety of our class?"
Both go silent, Rin suddenly looks to the side blushing and Maya gives a disappointed look. Oh no, am I wrong for interpreting that as if she DOES have the urge to do that?

Just looked in the hints. It has never been that empty before. Literally just the main event in the list. Wild.

Uhh, that phone call seems serious.
HOLY SHIT! Okay, yeah that was certainly unexpected. A sink hole swallowed Rin's friend's school, it sounds absolutely ridiculous but it would explain how some of these characters end up being involved in the story. Mind you, that's both Rin's friend and her new friend at minimum and the mc DID say he is unlikely to meet that new friend again. (my stupid memory for names...)
Yeah, I was about to say. Maya probably have never had something like that happen in one of these cycle/reset things. She confirmed it's not suppose to happen.
Oh shit, Uta too? Are there gonna be a forth or more? Well, I guess this is as good excuse as any to get a bunch of new transfer students.
Merry disaster Christmas I guess.
Disaster happen. Mc: "My heart goes out to any fellow teacher who will now have a significantly more difficult time seducing his students." Bruh... insensitive much?
You know for a damn fact Maya is going home to try to make sense of this.
That's the second time Maya has seen a ghost and for a very different reason... or actually for the same reason now that I think about it.

Had an interesting thought. You think all the explosions in the air sending small shockwaves may have somehow hit the ground, shaking it on a small scale we cannot see but that was somehow enough to trigger the sinkhole?

Christmas event over.
That's a lot of blue events. Invite Ami over? Umm, okay?
That's gonna be an awful lot of headpats...

I don't agree with what the mc is saying at all right now. We are completely disconnected on this opinion. The mc calling students "fucking idiots" for choosing to study at a school instead of studying at home. I call them wise for choosing that. As much as you might hate school, you will easily come to miss it knowing making social interactions or forming relationships suddenly become 10 times harder if not much more. Following a routine where you have to shower, wake up and go to bed at certain times, be outside at certain times and so on are also very important. Add onto that the fact that trying to learn keeps the brain active and fully functional while consuming brain rotting material... like this, isn't exactly training your brain and thus degrading it. I've felt all these consequences and it's not a happy life. Stay in school, kids. It will be one of the best decisions you will make, especially as the kind of person who doesn't like social gatherings and aren't very sociable.

Oh, I'm gonna guess that's THAT teacher, whatever her name was.
Yep, Watabe sounds familiar. I can already tell she's gonna be the interestingly depressing type who hates her job and probably talks badly about her students and is dead on the inside or whatever. I mean, the eyebags and the skull is a dead giveaway.
Uhh, well considering she just wished all the students would have died in that sinkhole...
Is it weird for me to say that Wakana is... strangely attractive? Am I into emo/goth teachers now? What is this?

Oh don't even fucking dare turn your students into pets, Sensei

Seriously, why do I like Wakana so much!? This is alarming. Should I get myself checked out or something?

Who would have known. One day these two girls you find out are named Ami and Maya walk into the maid cafe you work out. Later Maya shows up with an older man. Later after that he shows up again with Ami who intends to work there with you, sounds great. Then all of a sudden the school you go to decide to collapse and you find out the man you saw at the cafe is now gonna be your teacher and you will be in the same class as both Ami and Maya. Wild. Small world huh?

One of the girls... extremely wealthy family... uhhh, is there a third or is this who I think it is?

Yeah that's about the reaction I expected from inviting Ami over to her own home.

Wait, they live in the US? Are you absolutely sure about that!? So it's not Japan, it's not some weird amalgamation between Japan and the US? That's fking weird. How will I cope with this fact?

Cat Ami makes me feel all strange.

Bro, that was just straight up a jumpscare at that point. Not cool! Ami broke in the middle of this wholesome scene. Like this is the kind of shit I've been expecting around every corner and then NOW of all times you decide to throw it at me.

Welp. Ami just got another redhead to compete with, sooner or later.

500 headpats for Ami complete

Why a deer of all things? Uta could marry anything and she would choose a deer?

I knew Yumi would love the flavor beam. She looks like the type who would be all over that.

I have visual trauma with arm wrestling. I will never arm wrestle after what I saw. Just like I will never use the leg press. Too many of those clips...

I can't say I'm not surprised by that arm wrestle outcome.

Pretty sure you can fold a blazer to the mess doesn't get around the bag.

Just how oblivious is Ami really? Now he invites Ayane over of all people. I guess she's blinded by love huh. Of course from our perspective it looks like they all are.

Confirmed. Kirin likes to inflict trauma. She's a devil. Back you demon spawn!
Miku's intimate massage was easy to sniff out by Kirin. Kirin winning by logic and process of elimination here, sort of.

Does Kirin really need to explain to the mc why she doesn't want to lose her virginity in the store room while her soccer team knows she's in there and Miku is already suspicious?
It's suppose to be special.
Her reason why that it was too romantic... Bruh. Then pretend it isn't romantic, don't talk about it? If you make it romantic it will be romantic.
Now that I think about it, maybe Kirin's distaste for romanticism is what made her interrupt them at the beach. She's all about fun and don't care about whatever emotion is involved. She probably sees the whole thing as hot and fun and thinks others should see it that way too. Obviously this is a flaw because if you can't respect others who don't share your view then that kinda makes you a bad person doesn't it?

Ahh yes... Nothing beats cumming to a girl on a cross...
Too many quality name choices with Kirin. Both the brother and dad roleplays are on the hotter side but they are taken and hard to choose from. Coach is definitely more relevant but it seems a bit more playful. Kirin is the playful type so it works but it feels like it would be harder to emotionally connect with Kirin with that name somehow.
Nah dude, would rather break Kirin than protect her. She can protect herself for all I care. Gonna need some kind of trauma shit to fix my attitude towards her.

The fucking high difference between sensei and Uta... jeez, that's certainly putting things into perspective. Now if only I had his actual length. Know for a fact it's over 6 at least.
Guess there isn't gonna be a "moving in to dorm" event for every new character.

Well would you look at that. I was right. It is the green haired girl.
I don't quite remember what they said but I believe Io also doesn't have a filter. So these two are quite similar. Yeah, she's "very forward about this" referring to the cleaning of whatever disgusting deeds he would get up to with Ayane at the bathhouse.
Uta and Io's personalities seem to be opposites but they are both very open or forward, no filter or whatever. (Too much rambling again)
Wait, how the fuck did Io see that(penis)?
BRUH, a fking camera at a beachhouse! Because that's totally not a creepy thing to have installed at A PLACE OF RELAXATION!

Feels like that's normal no? We are all male on the internet until proven otherwise. Don't think that philosophy has gone away, has it?
Io got a bunch of metal stuff? I get this strange feeling of deja vu... Like I've seen a green haired animated girl before whose a blacksmith or whatever you would call it. Did I maybe... see a poster of this game at some point?

Damn dude! HAHAHA! Io just signed her friend's privacy at the bathhouse away just like that. Even if it was a joke it was a glorious one.

Oh, Ayane will fix our oven alright... wtf kind of innuendo is that?
Hmm, Makoto has the same grinding scene. Might be the first time I've caught a reused scene. But that's inevitable.
Gonna stop posting the written section of the tierlist from now on unless there is something new to add. Character notes will only be added at eoc I think.

I've decided to stop adding notes on characters and likely make a final update to them when I reach eoc. The rules of the tierlist will remain tho. I also think I will choose a lazy approach and not include this written section unless I have something to add in which case I will put it here for that day like I've always done. Saves me a bit of time as I always find myself inconvenienced by everything I include. (the initial unspoilered info, the spoiler with everything in it, the occasional written messages before the tierlist and the tierlist itself along with the now occasional added text after the image.) So I guess just refer back to one of my previous posts. Easy to find with ctrl+F or maybe my profile?



Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

I may forgive characters over time for a past mistake, bumping them back up.

A character most likely won't lose their position just because I haven't seen them enough in a while.

spoilers.title: Tierlist
spoilers.html:
I've decided to stop adding notes on characters and likely make a final update to them when I reach eoc. The rules of the tierlist will remain tho. I also think I will choose a lazy approach and not include this written section unless I have something to add in which case I will put it here for that day like I've always done. Saves me a bit of time as I always find myself inconvenienced by everything I include. (the initial unspoilered info, the spoiler with everything in it, the occasional written messages before the tierlist and the tierlist itself along with the now occasional added text after the image.) So I guess just refer back to one of my previous posts. Easy to find with ctrl+F or maybe my profile?



Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

I may forgive characters over time for a past mistake, bumping them back up.

A character most likely won't lose their position just because I haven't seen them enough in a while.


Some edited since yesterday.
Yumi: I can't WAIT to see how the story with her escalates. Every time he messes with her, it's so fun and I like her appearance too.
Ayane: She's obsessed with you. Her lack of a father figure hurts her more than I realized...
Ami: Red hair, she loves you.
Chika: I expected an annoying gyaru girl who acts way too popular but I got someone chill and down to earth, fun to be around.
Makoto: I love it when he messes with her. I slightly dislike her hair and how studious she is.
Sana: Very precious.
Sara: Hot mom, I repeat, hot mom!
Maya: The mystery behind her is intriguing.
Miku: Not usually into tomboys.
Futaba: Not into big girls or big tits.
Rin: Nice hair. A bit bland unless Chika is around. Also seem to have a bit of a wingman personality.
Kirin: Surprisingly flirtatious... and intimidatingly so. Perhaps a bit manipulative and evil.
Karin: Absolutely adorable how bad she is with boys.
Chinami: So adorable! Must protecc!
Molly: She can be anywhere.
Haruka: Breasts are way too large for my liking but otherwise she's ok.
Kaori: Her eccentric personality is growing on me. Not a fan of the spider tattoo.
Tsuneyo: This one is rough... extremely sheltered type.
Uta: Absolutely adorable maid.

We don't know that Akira's suicide is what started the cycles of TERMINAL 23, or he just killed himself amidst the cycles themselves (if he took his life at all, although that is likely). The supernatural stuff was already present in TERMINAL 22 aka "the house by the lake", and that was way before Akira was born - so supernatural does not need to equate Akira's suicide at the very least.

Regarding Pareidolia, Akira seems to have summoned him from the well when he was a kid, since we have Pareidolia talking about how Akira talked to him only about bad things when he was a kid ("Mysterious abundance of chickens"), and how it made Pareidolia concerned. The ability to conjure up gods from the bottom of the well (where they go to die, and then reincarnate into humans or worse) is something that Pareidolia himself does not understand how was done.

Mind you, even though the wishing well is explained by NAO, HOPE is also called to refill the well - which would explain his ability to create and melt stuff. There is a lot about the hierarchy of gods and how they function in relationship with other gods, makeshift gods, and the mechanics of the well itself, that we don't understand.

From Pareidolia, we gather that gods are born and die left and right, a god needs only one believer to be able to sustain itself (Pareidolia being the example for this), and it would fit with just how many gods there are, from more serious ones to absolutely ridiculous beings. This also falls into the idea of their legend having to be preserved, like in the case of Shota (knife boy), or Pareidolia being concerned.

Moving past the gods a bit, Maya references a few times that she has made a "wish", and that bad things that happen to her could be punishment for falling in love, or for being too selfish. Her past related to being a shrine maiden, praying during resets, and her knowledge of the callous god has yet to be properly addressed as well. Furthermore, granted recent information, related to her being something that should not exist/did not exist in some cycles, and how her past before the cycles is sketchy at best, Maya could also be a god that Akira conjured from the well. Her obsession with the stars and Altair/Vega's story would fit into that as well.

At the moment, the person responsible for the cycles of TERMINAL 23 gravitates from Akira/Maya to Akira/Ami, or one of those by themselves. We simply don't know enough yet, and what more we have learned have provided evidence to other possibilities rather than closing down on one.
In other news, I have failed in being able to finish the game by the end of the month, but at least I have made it to chapter 3.
Finally, given that tomorrow we'll have 0.46, I'd like to officially call for the usual "what do you most want to see for the next update?" game.
And I'll start by saying that I personally would like to see Molly finally getting the sex she deserves. The poor girl has been trying for that for years.

posts.content_html_raw:
I believe that the fact these sorts of questions are even asked is part of the point of this story, and that includes green vs red. Consider:

The philosophy behind the green vs red comes down to a meta analysis vs an emotional reaction for most. Do I follow the best story that makes the most sense, even against my better moral judgment? Or do I allow my morals to persuade me to choose something that assuages my pain and fear for now? These are questions I think are valuable, and while one can argue the virtues or detriments of either, the mere fact the dichotomy exists shows that, even if the choices are primarily superficial in the overarching narrative, they matter. On an individual basis, one must confront such questions in order to make a choice.

Even in the beginning, the scene with Yumi, the choice leads to the same result, but did you not pause and think? And if you didn’t, did you then roll back to see the other choice?

The illusion of choice present in LiL doesn’t negate the fact that said illusion is intended (in my opinion) to, at the very least, invite introspection in the reader.

posts.content_html_raw:
My God god, you guys took an interesting time to discuss such heavy topics - on New Year's and right before the update

I think I can speak for (almost) everyone here that nobody wants to see any explicit scene involving wizards. In fact, I personally find it hard to imagine a way that it would not end up being inherently tasteless.
However, I am not here to tell the author how to write and portray his story. If Sel deems it necessary to show certain parts of it, then maybe he will find a way to make it somehow seem worth it.

But as you guys already discussed, I doubt it will happen this way. First off, because it would be very brave, if not foolish, to try and pull it off when it's very much risking his revenue stream to collapse. And we know Sel enough to imagine how much he would want to avoid that at all costs.

And while the character models themselves may fall under the Loli category, the way they have been presented and their ages basically established, I don't think that would go well, probably not even on this site and certainly not on a funding/donation website that has much stricter rules.

So in the end, I'm fairly certain it will be simply implied. Which would be horrible enough. Definitely a new moral/emotional low blow for the reader. Let's just hope that if it comes to that, Sel will deliver it in a relatively decent manner, if there even is one.

Also, Happy New Year everyone lol!

Poetic meter -- and especially unrhymed iambic pentameter -- is covered in US Literature classes whenever poetry is covered, which is every year.

9th grade: Romeo & Juliet
10th grade: Julius Caesar
11th grade: American Lit, so no Shakespeare, but we cover poetic meter when talking about Walt Whitman and Emily Dickinson
12th grade: Macbeth

" I will never stop being creeped out by the people who think it’s okay to bang the high school girls but not the wizards (edited)

Treating fictional characters like real people is fucking weird to begin with but you’ve gotta be a real sketch to think just one of those things is okay if you’re going to apply real life characteristics and rights to the girls "

Sooo.... it seems like he doesn't see a difference between the lolis wizards and the class which is retarded. I think there will be explicit wizard stuff but behind an unofficial "fan" patch or something.
Click to expand...
If I could try to interpret this stance on the situation, my initial reaction to this is that Sel can't avoid the reading that someone fine with sex with the rest of the class but upset by sex with the wizards is actively moralizing fictional sex depictions based on their real-world morality. In other words, by projecting some of your real world morality into the fictional world and avoiding sex with wizards, Sel extrapolates that when you enjoy engaging with the classroom you are ALSO makings decisions based on your real world morality.

With just this to go on, it seems like Sel only finds your morality consistent if you either:
A: Find grooming and sex with students repulsive and don't want to see it even in ficiton.
B: Don't apply real world morality to fictional characters and are fine with seeing anything.

I see where it's coming from, but I think it's a pretty reductive take. To use myself as an example, this position would find my stance on gore as simlarly hypocritical. I don't like watching extra gory horror films not because I find it morally reprehensible to depict necessarily, it just makes me personally uncomfortable to see past a certain point. Some bloody and realistic depictions are fine while others are too gratuitous and just overwhelm me. It's not that I "morally and intellectually can't watch the terrible thing happen" I just start having physical reactions to certain visuals that I'd rather avoid, given the choice.

A few things. First, upon replaying, he very much never comes from a place of "I'm doing good things to these people". Akira knows what he's doing from the start, and his monologues reinforce that very much from the first half of chapter 1. If the player feels that way it's on their own, which might be a result from getting attached to the characters, but still - not a point in the story that later gets shifted. Akira had always been an asshole intending to corrupt young minds for his pleasure. In fact, he only starts to regret it later in the story around chapter 3.

So imo there's no real facade that gets broken. And although these girls suffer from their relationship with him, they also benefit from it (Rin is the most obvious example). If it was a one way street to everyone just getting a shitty life from being in contact with him, then LiL would turn into an educational "pedophilia is bad" game, and that is an insult that Selebus really doesn't deserve. His story is more complicated than that. In fact, the game states at multiple points that they all have to get broken so that things can get healed. That things will get very bad but it will be worth it.

I disagree with the idea of LiL being about a man destroying 35 lives. It's rather about 36 lives being put through the grinder. Akira just happens to be the common link that people depend on, while he himself is one of the worst possible helpers they could count on. He's just very unreliable, and yet, he didn't kill Makoto's father, he was just there for her when it happened - and Ami helped her bounce back. He was also there for Chika multiple times, both financially and being present for Chinami (which he really didn't have to be). During the same "stomachache", both he and Io find a lot about themselves as they both reenact their traumas. And what happened to Miku was offputting, sure, but the very fact that she got to that point had to do with her opening up about her PTSD and getting treatment for it.
My point is that it's just more complicated than being able to put all on him. Both from the complexity of human relationships in general, and of the nature of Kumon-mi itself.

Edit: Also, someone tell Selebus that he can release the update already. I appreciate him waiting for me to catch up in my replay, but I'd rather just play 0.46 now.

So yeah, Pareidolia was probably involved in that too. Which isn't a surprise, but hey, I'm replaying it and seeing it first hand again. Which begs a different question in that, if Pareidolia was ever just something he could put the blame on, maybe this really was all Akira? (Lavender's Green, 1999 PC CLASSIC, and the Karin assault?).
Click to expand...
I would assume what happened there was either the time with Io reminded Sensei of his groomed memories with Sekai (the core memory part) and thus he started automatically acting on them, or he became under the influence of one of the gods due to a similar downward spiraling monologue pattern being observed in Lavender Green, but that god won't be Pareidolia.

The reasons for that are that:
- This was still in Ch3 when HOPE still reigned. The idea of the weakest god already doing shenanigans before Ch4 feels bizarre.
- Unlike the "USER2 has sent you 6M Molly affection points!" in Lavender Green and the whole inner bickering with Pareidolia in Paranoid, there is no substantial cue that could effectively lead to Pareidolia. Fonts and presentation style are not enough for me.
- Mostly importantly, at that time Sensei has nothing he blamed himself for to a serious degree, not even the incident with Molly which he couldn't remembered and was only afraid to find out the truth. The scapegoat excuse by Pareidolia thus is not applicable here. My understanding of scapegoat excuse is that Sensei would start hating Pareidolia instead of himself over, specifically, Maya Prime's death (i.e., not his general trend of nihilistic self-hatred which he has always been brazen about). That means, Pareidolia should not be the cause of any ruckus when the reason for needing a scapegoat has yet to arrive.

posts.content_html_raw:
0.46 event triggers

There are 20 events in total. Most events (save two) are linked. The chain begins on a Friday. After Christmas is done with the main event "Post Nut Clarity", you have two other events:

19 - Tsukasa 2 (automatic on a sunday afternoon - I think you will need Tsukasa's route taken).
20 - Otoha 2 (visit her dorms, triggered for me on a weekday).

*How not to miss events: There are A LOT of flags being invoked, including one for Futaba which will fail a lot of events if not present. It happens during "The one with all the sextoys" and it needs Futaba Lust 40. The next one happens during Futaba's event, needing Molly's lust 10. If you got the two of them, then, and only then, Tsubasa's event will trigger.

Other than that, Kirin's blackmail will be checked leading to a difference in dialogue, as well as multiple calls for Tsukasa's route having been taken. The "amifingered" flag will change her conversation with Niki in the backstage. Most importantly however is a Himawari variation that needs Ayane affection over 3k. This happens during "Post nut clarity":
There are also new invite over costumes for Kirin, but I have no interest whatsoever in those.

Edit: New animation 1 is Imani at the dive bar. 2 is Kirin inviteover Cowgirl.

It also has been pointed out that seeing the Himawari variation unblocks Maya - mind you, it doesn't really matter that much since the events you get access to are the old ones (like Maya prime old). And the shrine will still remain locked.

**thanks for the info on both animation and Maya locked flag.

DeanNoriko said:
So are those >3000 love events supposed to be just Easter Eggs or actual canon events for people who data mine (i.e. check URM or code)?
I haven't checked those out yet, but without having spoiled myself too much, at least this one seems rather insightful, I suppose?

Click to expand...
It may be the kind of thing that's important to be there even if nobody finds it, so a sort of easter egg, but not any less important than any other scene of the game. Something that, logically or emotionally given base constraints, must be there for everything else to make sense or feel right. If we think about it, these scenes arise from some kind of demonstration of devotion for Ayane - someone has in fact grinded more than 10,000 Ayane affection out of genuine love for her. It may be that authorman feels it's important to reward or otherwise have consequences for such a display of devotion even if theoretically nobody were to find it, and in this sense, those using tools are violating this artistic intention as well. However, that too brings forth its own metaphor, like 'cheating' also being something that stomps on 'devotion.'

For anyone who doesn't use URM, you really should get on that. But in the meantime, here's the hidden scene that's gated behind 3000 Ayane affection that you will have missed (unless you're a psychopath like shmurfer):
Ayane distinctly remembered Himawari when she met her on the beach, so the fact that she only gets a vague feeling this time is concerning. More of her memory has been messed with than just the scarf. There's also the list that she couldn't remember in the alternate timeline, but that memory might be back based on how she knew about Futaba.

My reading: The scarf has a nostalgic scent because it's a memory of Maya Prime, and by hanging on to the scarf Ayane is hanging on to the fleeting hope that Maya Prime will return and everything will work out. Instead, it's show time for Ayane, as she has to take over Maya Prime's role.

Since Himawari is a time traveler, this could be how she got the scarf in the first place to sell it to Akira in chapter 1, which set in motion the chain of events that eventually led to Maya's death.

posts.content_html_raw:
Which events have the ayane Easter eggs, and what are their requirements? Been following game for a year and a half now, and this is the update that pushed me towards the green path.

When it isn't heavy handed, I enjoy how the various narrators can be interpreted as referring to the reader as well as the characters. I think that in this update's Imani vouyer scene most of the narration is targeted towards the reader as much as Tsukasa. Sel's ability to obfuscate the intent of the author is a huge chunk of the appeal of this game, especially in recent updates where he's seemingly shown some of that intent, or maybe what little narrative security we've been given is just fuel for further confusion.

Knob thing? That should be a blade slider right?

Uta is the devil, trying to get him in some serious trouble with her phrasing...

Also it looks like Akira is getting flashbacks of the weird time/space jumps but doesn't seem like anyhting is sticking. Dc345 said:
Has anybody worked up a theory on the time traveling scarf yet?
Click to expand...
I've theorized about the Scarf in The Paradoxical Theory part:
DeSkel15 said:
Something interesting that I don't think has gained much notice is that it was again implied that even Sensei being aware of the Resets isn't relatively normal in the Resets.

In Ayane's Chapter 4 'Chamomile' Event, the Alt Maya Prime reveals:
View attachment 4224372 View attachment 4224373 View attachment 4224374 View attachment 4224375 View attachment 4224376 Alt Maya Prime - "No...I've been here the whole time. My last reset was months ago. But nobody else is supposed to know about them here."
Ayane - "Not even Sensei?"
Alt Maya Prime - "Definitely not Sensei. He's too busy fucking Ami to figure any of that stuff out. And I doubt he'll-"
- "Wait..."
- "Was that you...implying he actually figures it out in your timeline? Or...is that just wishful thinking on my end?"
That in her world (Football Sensei), she is the only one who knows about the Resets. Her Sensei doesn't and it seems like her Ami probably doesn't either (or at least this Maya implies that), and it seems like none of the previous Senseis had figured it out in this world either.

Our Maya Prime actually had also implied that Sensei being aware of Resets was a new thing:
View attachment 4224426 Maya Prime - "Until recently, I was the only one whose memories carried over from loop to loop. But changes made to the formula of this for unknown reasons have now landed both Ayane and Sensei beside me."
(Chapter 3 Makoto 'Suffer the Same' Event)
So, something probably happened before our Sensei showed up that made it possible for Sensei to make it to the roof and become aware of things. (Our Maya Prime didn't seem surprised that our Sensei knew of the Resets so it probably happened before Chapter 1)

I'm thinking a certain Shapeshifter, may have been behind that:
View attachment 4224436 Himawari - "In many respects, I'm just as lost as you are."
(Chapter 3 Sana 'Ad Meliora' Event)
Her presumed father and mother both becoming aware of the Resets, one after another, seems suspicious.

There's also how Himawari was involved in our Sensei buying the Scarf that he gives to our Maya Prime, who seemed to not have had that Scarf:



Assuming that the Alt Maya Prime could be our Maya Prime in the past, she may have gave our Ayane her Scarf, which ended up in our Timeline, then perhaps this Scarf will end up going from our Ayane to Himawari who then ends up in the past, selling it to either our Sensei, or the next Sensei, in this paradoxical cycle.

That Scarf could have created a paradox. I mean, whatever even started this hypothetical time traveling stuff (Nao-chan?) created it, but the Scarf itself seems important to it. (Of course, this same Scarf seemed to show up later with Chika in Chapter 3, but I'm not entirely sure on the importance of that)

----
Yumi also making it to the Rooftop and surviving, probably disproves any sex related theory on getting to the roof, and Ayane's "only 3 membership" theory as well.

There needing to be some kind of sacrifice possibly still works. Yuki, for example, seemed to go missing soon before Yumi made it to the roof, which seems awfully similar to what happened with Ayane's chicken son (Todd)...who Sensei still hasn't told her that he had found dead... I wonder if Yumi might bring that up?...

Also:

View attachment 4224475 Ami - "No one is drugging my uncle! You're all insane!"
(Chapter 2 'Post-Game Celebration!' Main Event)
I wouldn't really put it past some of these girls to drug rape Sensei, tbh. I would expect some to be okay with it, while others wouldn't, though, in game, and probably IRL. Realistically, Morality varies from person to person, and usually from context to context.
Click to expand...
Albeit, to further advance the theory, Himawari might be trying to create a paradox to keep the Well from drying up leading to a game over. She might have been doing this Scarf Paradox to prevent a bad ending, but it depends on where this Ami/Niki stuff is going since that seems to be the current "new" thing that may break the cycle:
Ami Prime - "Oh. Yeah. That's fine. Just keep me out of it. All things considered, I'm kind of enjoying this timeline. It's...what's the word...nostalgic?"
(Chapter 4 'Caught in the Crossfire' Main Event)
Ami Prime - "I...hold on. Wait a second. You're not-"
- "This isn't how it's supposed to go! This doesn't make sense!"
(Chapter 4 'Seed of Self-Doubt' Main Event)
As for New Maya not recognizing the scarf, it might be more of a retconned in thing. Hard to say for now.

I'm also not entirely sure if current Ayane is "our" Ayane, in reference to that paradoxical theory. Ours may have simply been devoured by HOPE.

For example: The "Real Home" variants of Maya and Ami, don't seem to be the current Maya and Ami, since the current ones never made it to the Halloween Party, unlike the "Real Home" ones:
Ami Prime - "Hmm...you must've blacked out while we were on our way to the party. But don't worry! I carried you all the way here by myself because I love you so darn much."
(Chapter 4 Maya 'Right as Rain' Event)
Narrator - "To the real home."
Ami - "Um...does anyone else by any chance..."
- "Feel the ground moving?..."
(Chapter 4 'All Around the Mulberry Bush' Main Event)
Maya even had a different hairstyle, so either something very convoluted happened, or we switched something.

Of course, hard to tell when Ami is actually being serious, or making up stuff:
New Maya - "Probably because you told me the moment you realized I was still here that you would blow up the world if I informed them of your existence."
Ami Prime - "And you believed me?"
(Chapter 4 'Caught in the Crossfire' Main Event)
Especially since it's likely that Sekai is still telling Ami to say things:
Sekai - "Unless they let you join in."
Ami - "Unless you let me get in on it, of course."
(Chapter 4 Niki 'That Funny Feeling' Event)
And Sekai seems to still be "haunting" this Ami, and Niki:
Sekai - "You'll never be enough, you know."
Niki - "Hello?..."
(Chapter 4 'Seed of Self-Doubt' Main Event)

For now, more intel is probably needed to figure out what's "real".

posts.content_html_raw:
Great update. Here's some of my general thoughts on characters and events. Lore stuff will be coming in a later post.
Miku's outfit is really doing it for me.

Also, please do listen to her, Makoto.
Nodoka has apparently been acting weird since Halloween, but we're not told in what way. She does remember Nodokathon and the quadrildo, so I assume she wasn't factory reset, but clearly something changed.
I guess we need to add Touka to the list of potential psychopaths.
Thank god for Noriko and her sneaky legal skills.
It's such a great touch that Noriko gave Yumi a sea turtle.

As usual, Chinami is absolutely adorable and hilarious - my favorite part was her unintentional implication that Chika might be a lolicon.

...

...
I'm continuing to love the Kirin redemption arc. She's such a fascinating character and her scenes here were particularly well-written. It's fitting that what broke through to her and inspired her confession was hearing Sensei being dishonest with himself because he wants to be treated like the trash he is - the same thing Kirin constantly does to hide from her true feelings. After Sensei rejected her for Chika, she threatened to go right back into self-destructive mode, but she managed to overcome it and finally came clean and apologized to Ayane.

As suspected, Kirin never intended to traumatize Ayane, maybe only scare her a little. By projecting her own fucked up relationship with sex, she thought Ayane would actually ultimately enjoy being forced into a threesome. I suspect she realized she went too far and began to regret it pretty quickly, but her inferiority complex made it so she'd rather pretend to have been intentionally evil than admit she made a mistake. Of course, she's still a trash person - doubling down and forcing Ayane to do it again makes that very clear. But at least she's willing to admit to it now and wants to atone, she's making progress!
Chika is only getting more concerning. Things ended up okay (relatively) this time only because she heard Kirin and Sensei confess their love. What happens next time when she inevitably catches Sensei with someone she thinks that he doesn't "love"? Things could definitely get violent. Also, why does she know about Sensei's thing with crying girls? I don't think that's something she personally experienced or witnessed. Combined with her saying "tick tock" before following Sensei and Kirin, I'm wondering if something supernatural is starting with her.
Otoha is such a nice change of pace from all the characters who have the hots for Sensei (he's more than just a piece of meat, damn it!). Plus she gives great advice - it really would be a good idea for him to stop fucking all those teenagers, wouldn't it? Of course, her own hypocrisy (which she's well aware of) just makes it all the more interesting. She'd love it if this particular thirtyish adult would stop wanting to fuck teenagers, but she really wants a different thirtyish adult to start doing the same thing.

It's annoying, but quite fitting with her personality, that for Otoha "closure" refers to her non-relationship with Niki rather than her real relationship with Rin. I guess she gave Rin some closure in their banana boat talk, but she still hasn't really come clean about Niki. Misleading Sensei into thinking she was going to kiss him was pretty funny and fully deserved, though.
Well, I guess it's confirmed that Tsubasa is evil incarnate. First she leans into the Sekai thing again (mother figure who takes a dominant role - not to mention the unsubtle red lighting) to heighten Sensei's vulnerability and remind him of his own trauma, then forces him to think about Tsukasa sexually. Then she's deliberately cruel to Tsukasa, starving her of affection and attention, and suggests that she turn to Jeeves instead.

On the flip side, I feel so awful for Tsukasa. Everyone around her (except Chinami) is completely failing her. Sensei is grooming her and actively wants to repeat his relationship with Sekai from the other side and become "her ghost". Her own mother is egging Sensei on and treating Tsukasa like trash to push her into the arms of her groomer. Her sister bluntly tells her that she doesn't belong and then leaves her alone with a serial predator who "wants her here". When asked about sex by a wizard, Chika says nothing except how good it feels - like seriously, I know you're crazy, but what the fuck, Chika?!?

The creepiest of the many creepy things in the Imani sex scene: the roleplay in which Sensei is clearly assigning Imani the role of Tsukasa.
I have to say, I wasn't expecting patient, maternal (materteral? - thanks google), protective Niki who wants to do nothing more than fix her disgusting, perverted, annoying fucking incest gremlin by showering her with love; in retrospect, it makes perfect sense with her personality, though.

Niki seems completely unsurprised to find out Sensei is "hypothetically" fucking Ami and all of her friends. Apparently this was a revelation she was fully prepared to deal with because she really is that committed to fixing him. I don't know whether I like this or not, she's starting to feel a bit "overly perfect" just like Noriko. Though in her case it could make sense if she knows more than she lets on about Akira and Sekai.

I don't want to weigh in on the Ami in the room, yet, but I do want to say, this was an absolutely shit plan for getting rid of Niki. First she lets her move in and for two months does nothing more than drop annoying incest references. And since that wasn't working she just tells Niki exactly what she's doing and tries to hurt her feelings. It would have been so easy for her to engineer Niki finding her (or any of the other girls) with Sensei, so why stick to hypotheticals? Why ever let Niki move in in the first place?

First she leans into the Sekai thing again (mother figure who takes a dominant role - not to mention the unsubtle red lighting) to heighten Sensei's vulnerability and remind him of his own trauma, then forces him to think about Tsukasa sexually. Then she's deliberately cruel to Tsukasa, starving her of affection and attention, and suggests that she turn to Jeeves instead.
On the flip side, I feel so awful for Tsukasa. Everyone around her (except Chinami) is completely failing her. Sensei is grooming her and actively wants to repeat his relationship with Sekai from the other side and become "her ghost". Her own mother is egging Sensei on and treating Tsukasa like trash to push her into the arms of her groomer. Her sister bluntly tells her that she doesn't belong and then leaves her alone with a serial predator who "wants her here". When asked about sex by a wizard, Chika says nothing except how good it feels - like seriously, I know you're crazy, but what the fuck, Chika?!?
The creepiest of the many creepy things in the Imani sex scene: the roleplay in which Sensei is clearly assigning Imani the role of Tsukasa.
Spoiler

spoilers.title: Niki and Ami
spoilers.html:
I have to say, I wasn't expecting patient, maternal (materteral? - thanks google), protective Niki who wants to do nothing more than fix her disgusting, perverted, annoying fucking incest gremlin by showering her with love; in retrospect, it makes perfect sense with her personality, though.

Niki seems completely unsurprised to find out Sensei is "hypothetically" fucking Ami and all of her friends. Apparently this was a revelation she was fully prepared to deal with because she really is that committed to fixing him. I don't know whether I like this or not, she's starting to feel a bit "overly perfect" just like Noriko. Though in her case it could make sense if she knows more than she lets on about Akira and Sekai.

I don't want to weigh in on the Ami in the room, yet, but I do want to say, this was an absolutely shit plan for getting rid of Niki. First she lets her move in and for two months does nothing more than drop annoying incest references. And since that wasn't working she just tells Niki exactly what she's doing and tries to hurt her feelings. It would have been so easy for her to engineer Niki finding her (or any of the other girls) with Sensei, so why stick to hypotheticals? Why ever let Niki move in in the first place?

Re: Scarf, I shall spare our timid fellow a direct reply, but if I remember correctly then the scene commentary for Stray Cat (the initial scarf scene) reveals that Maya lost it when the time loop began since she got it at the end of the year. It says, 'how long has it been since she has touched this fabric,' which implies ownership and then loss beyond what was already apparent. We can imagine something happening at the end of the school year that made someone Wish they were back at the start of the school year, which unfortunately was before she was gifted the scarf, which means bye bye scarf. It would follow, then, that Neo Maya would not know the scarf, since she was reset to the 'start' of the loop, and never experienced the pre-loop (or end-of-loop) where the scarf was initially given. P.S., it seems intuitive to me that Maya would only have 'confessed her feelings' for Sensei after several years of fucking and so on, which means that I doubt it was from the tutorship era or anything too long ago. Perhaps the scarf is what inspired her confession.

Of course, LiL continuity is intentionally mysterious so I don't take any of this as factual, and at this point my brain is rotten with LiL lore being mere patchwork, but it has never seemed strange to me that Neo Maya would be unfamiliar with the scarf.

Edit: Also, fact-checking this post forced me to re-read the parts where Selebus describes all the girls as extensions of himself, and Maya calls herself a 'part of Selebus' and thus capable of reading his thoughts, so fuck all of you. I am now miserable and my day is ruined.

posts.content_html_raw:
Tsukasa seriously deserves the world… She was definitely the standout character for me in this update.


Also, surprise surprise. Tsubasa is still a horrible mother.

I did have an interesting thought on some of Tsubasa’s actions this time, though; particularly when she runs into Tsukasa soon after the “Yes, Mother” event.

Tsubasa’s treatment of Tsukasa feels almost… orchestrated and intentional. Like… she’s being distant and cold for some higher purpose we don’t know about. Obviously that ‘purpose’ involves driving Tsukasa closer to Akira, but one must wonder exactly why…

Tsubasa must still be following the will of the Wishing Well. Or at least, that’s how my half-asleep brain is processing this right now.

It’s just like when Tsubasa gave Akira Tsukasa’s phone number on impulse or when she told Touka that Akira saw her as a mother figure, which upset her initially, but ultimately brought them a bit closer in the end.

It would be soooo simple to just chalk it up to: “Yeah well, Tsubasa simply sees Tsukasa as annoying and disposable and that’s that”, but personally, I think it’s more complicated than it seems on the surface.

Hmm… what else.

- Oh yeah, the scene where Akira and Kirin lay out their feelings for each other was really cute. I even duped myself for a moment into believing it would somehow end well. But uh… yeah. Chika’s still fucking loco.

- Niki is slowly losing her sanity, but is seriously trying really hard for Ami’s sake. Ami even seemed confused by Niki’s supportiveness, as if it wasn’t meant to happen. As if this were part of a timeline she hasn’t experienced yet. Intrigued to see where it’ll end up.

- Noriko’s Secret Santa gift for Yumi being a callback to her love for sea turtles just proves how thoughtful she really is. I like these two as friends.

- Yasu was extra sweet this update. Like, it genuinely surprised me. I’m definitely into her wacky, preachy antics, but it’s also really refreshing to see Yasu talk more like a normal girl for once and just have a heart-to-heart.

- The chipmunks were annoying. I didn’t fuck with it.

- Let’s goooo, Imani! You finally got the D! I’m so proud! And so will your friends when they inevitably find out soon.

- Miku wants to work at the Porn Shop? That could be... an interesting change of pace I wouldn’t have thought of before. Miku seems more assertive too, calling out Makoto for making a lot of her decisions for her. We’ve never seen that side of Miku, so it was definitely surprising.

- Otoha’s such a damn tease… I have a feeling it won’t be long until we see some good progress out of her too, though.

- There’s a whole scene with Himawari if Ayane’s affection is over 3,000?? That’s… interesting, but… I have to wonder the reasoning for it. Is it simply a bonus scene for supposedly grinding that many affection points, or will this affect something major eventually? I suppose we’ll have to see.

Soo yeah. Pretty solid update overall. It feels good to be back to our monthly LiL fix.

Fundamentally, renpy uses both sets of saves at the same time, and the DRM would delete both at the same time. PART I

I purposefully waited to comment on the Himawari thing, so after reading the regulars' opinions, the time is now.
Okay so, first things first: Himawari has a plan. This has been painfully obvious for some time now. Pareidolia also has a plan, and their respective plans are opposite to one another to an extent:
Regardless if that narrator is Himawari (it seems to be because of the call for Ayane love 3k), this opposition is reinforced on the roof, as Himawari faces Pareidolia directly:
Himawari tries to save Nodoka, but she gets caught in Pareidolia's plan (sending her to Sekai's happy ending timeline). This also confirms that Himawari (to an extent) has been the done helping Nodoka through dreams, and yet opposes Nodoka revealing things to everyone. So how much Himawari intended for Nodoka to go is unclear.

Nevertheless, we wrongfully assumed that Himawari's plan was going to happen during the reset:
While Himawari is present in both SENSEI QUEST and on the waiting room, she doesn't seem to interfere with the reset itself. Meaning that her plan is yet to come, and what we're seeing during the reset is Pareidolia's plan (or at least he has a part in it).

I'll get back to Himawari's plan when we reach 0.46. For now, let's go back a bit and talk about her interference and what's happening to Ayane.
She goes out of her way to save Ayane during Perfect harmony, during the night where only a day is supposed to have passed, but it's actually an entire week. Ayane doesn't seem to have any recollection of this, so it's unclear of what Himawari saved her from, but possibly Ayane was going to be reset there. Instead, she only lost memories of that time.

I bring this point because there's been many people talking about how it's strange that Ayane doesn't remember the scarf, but the thing is, Ayane has been having memory problems before that:
She forgets about the list that she had Akira make, where he noted everyone he had sex with. And, mind you, this is during the chain of events where alt Maya Prime explains how it's impossible for them to retain most of their memories after so many cycles:
Maya has hidden notes (in boxes) throughout the whole school and can barely remember what's written in them, or if there even is something written in them - that's just how much her memory is fucked.

The weird thing about the scarf is that, the way they talk about it, it seems to be something Akira gave her during the Winter of the resets. This could just be because from Ayane's understanding that's all it is, and yet from Maya's is something from the distant past that got reintroduced in a magical way to her (by Himawari selling it to Akira). We still need clarification on that, which should be coming soon.

Another point of interest is why alt Maya Prime didn't choose to go to the roof upon hearing that a reset was happening that she couldn't feel, and was a notification from Kaori to Yumi. Another interpretation of that I have in retrospect is that maybe it wasn't a reset at all, but a trap/test.
Nodoka warns Akira of that same thing during her sacrifice. Maybe alt Maya Prime managed to figure it out too from that chain of events.
So, in retrospect, alt Maya Prime made the correct choice by not going to the roof.
When we come back, although memories of what happened keep trying to come back to Akira, none of them remember anything, with the exception of Ami and Maya. Although the Ami that comes back is not our Ami (?), but that's another post altogether. My point is that they don't remember - including the scarf, which no one seems able to recognize.

Well, regardless, before addressing the Himawari and scarf finale, I'd like to point out that it is a bit convenient that Akira is getting knives by Noriko's intervention left and right:
Noriko was the one that made him recall his memories first, and now he's also trying to recall the events that led to Nodoka's death (stabbing).
So, to recap this gigantic post: Ayane is having memory issues despite Himawari saving her time and time again. Alt Maya Prime gave Ayane the scarf, and yet no one can remember it - even though Akira is actively trying to remember Nodoka's death. The roof seems to be a trap (to some extent), and alt Maya Prime may have figured that out last second (and instead chose to do something else, maybe leave a note to herself about it?). Himawari's plan is yet to be put into action, which leads us to this:
(This post continues on Part II)

PART II
First off, it seems like we have jumped the gun on the scarf thing. Going back to Rough cuts, it doesn't seem to be that the scarf is that important, but moreso the act of Akira gifting Maya a green scarf, because the very same scarves show up again during a later reset without Himawari being involved.
To check for sure I went back to when Maya gets it:
There's nothing in it that says it's the same old scarf. However that does beg the question of why alt Maya Prime has it. Maybe it's that we're lacking additional models, and that the scarf we see in Stray cat is just a green scarf, whereas the scarf we're seeing with alt Maya Prime is the actual old original green scarf... idk.

Back to Himawari's plan though, I'd just like to make mention of this which may or may not have been Himawari:
I mean, it doesn't have to be - but since it may be relevant to the next event I though I'd add it.

Now, finally to the actual event:

Maya requests to go to the same festival where Himawari interferes yet again:
As it has been pointed out, you can miss this - And I think we have no option but to assume that these things happen regardless and you're just, well, missing them, in the sense that you're not seeing them and yet they still happened. The same I think is true to the following scene, as I think Himawari will take Ayane's scarf regardless, and it's just that you're able to see the scene when it happens:
Well, since Akira is refusing to go the festival of tears, they set up a date to go buy a scarf, and that's when Himawari meets Ayane to get this specific scarf from her.

Now, there is a lot of things from this event which haven't been addressed. First of all, this bit is important because it frames the conversation as Himawari praising her mom. She finds it amazing Ayane can remember her at all after the events from both the beach trip and the reset trap, "no wonder your daughter turned out to be amazing too".
Next, notice that Himawari asks her if the scarf is important to her, to check if any memories of alt Maya Prime remain. I also find cute that Ayane goes into mom mode without noticing by asking if she can do anything else for her:

Anyways, here's a few thoughts from my side on the update:
First off, this update really shone a light on the differences between the green and (various) red paths. Reading others experiences, it became clear that quite a lot of dialogue and even whole events were completely absent if you were diverting from the green path.
Examples:
  • If you're on the good uncle path, Ami is apparently a lot less straightforward to Niki on Akira's behaviour. She does openly say that she wants to fuck her Dad, but she didn't (in this timeline) so from Niki's perspective it's still just threats from a rambling and hormonal, albeit weird, kid. There's no great revelation that Akira is fucking half the class or his niece/daughter. Which begs the question, how will that really impact the story going forward, given that in one instance Niki is apparently made aware and in the other still blissfully unaware? Unless I misread the other point of view presented by other user's posts.
  • If you are not on the correct path with Tsukasa, you just straight up miss out on her second event apparently. And the same goes for Tsubasa's, unless there was a different trigger for that one.
  • If you are not on Kirin's blackmail path, Kirin never apologizes to Ayane at the end of her event chain, in fact, she storms past her and explicitly tells her she is the second to last person she wants to see right now.
  • If you are like me and you don't specifically enjoy the sex acts with Futaba since they feel like taking advantage of a severely insecure teen (not like it's not the case with others, but with Futaba I actually do feel bad), you will likely miss out on her second event, which in turn, will also lock you out of the Molly event, even if you fulfill her lust requirement. Which is an odd programming choice, but I assume that Molly's event must somehow pick up from Futaba's event, so that it could not work alone by itself without the previous one happening?
There might be more, other than obvious dialogue variations, feel free to let me know if you noticed anything else.
And yes, I know, I could just use URM to change the values and get the events anyway. But first of all, it's about the principal, I'm evaluating the natural user experience when playing the game blind and how much content can be missed by seemingly arbitrary player decisions. And while I don't say this is bad per se, I feel like it should still be highlighted that the game might feel incomplete if you don't follow something like the guide mod or alter values in URM.
Which brings me to my second point, altering the values to see certain events still won't necessarily give you context. Sure, you will see the situation unfolding as if the requirements were met, but you effectively did not experience the exact events that led to said outcome. This may not always be relevant, especially for lewd scenes I assume, but it's still a reason for me to disregard URM for now. Instead this just gives me more motivation to finish my replay quickly and get a green path up to date so that I can use it for a second run of new updates to complete all events.
I'm still a bit unsure of how to feel about it. It kind of seemed...meh? I guess it's cute to see Imani all giddy with teenage-like anxiety, asking out Akira and everything. But maybe that's what was weirdly annoying me about it in a way too.
To illustrate my point, I want to remind you guys that a lot of you gave Akira (or basically by extension Sel) shit for acting way too affectionate and optimistic with Io on the red (aka not Stomachache) path, saying that it was grossly out of character.
Now we have a whole event with Akira, mentioning several times how he finds Imani very cute and that he feels like squeezing her to death?

(by the way, really hated this outfit, no offense Imani, but yuck)
To me, this is at least as sweet and overly affectionate as the whole Io scene if you went the red path. And this is canon, unavoidable. So all arguments in the lines of "well you see, the red path is clearly wrong and not authentic at all, since Akira acts way out of character, it is clearly not supposed to happen" could be thrown out the window after this event, no? It does seem that Akira is simply opening up more, emotionally. Which is also further evidenced during his conversation with Maya. More on that later.
Since I don't think anybody mentioned it all so far (apologies if I missed it), there has been another DnD event. I know a lot of you don't like them or even skip them. But I like the idea that those sessions might include subtle foreshadowing or have deeper meanings. Like der Crumpet Krampus (an actual mythological Christmas figure from Austrian/Bavarian folklore) who was apparently simply interested in evaluating whether the girls were good or bad. Sure, it seemed mostly like a Christmas themed insert, almost like a filler. But given the references to endgame plot developments thrown in throughout this update, as Moonflare mentioned, I couldn't help but think whether this could also be some sort of foreshadowing regarding the dark route and the purity routes. Something like, "admit you are bad, face your trauma and your inherent flaws (dark route), until you fix them and can rightfully claim to be good (purity route)". But I might be reading too much into it.
Anyway, Rin was there as well, so I was happy. Also this render/view somehow had more of an effect on me than it should have. I just really have a sweet spot for that girl.
Tsuneyo picks up on a joke by telling Ayane she missed the birth of her child. Interestingly enough, Himawari's birthday is coming up soon...

I don't know, they kind of grew on me. I was wondering whether the color of their names indicated they were somehow representing Makoto (being the reasonable and smart one), Sekai (being the daring and irrational one) and Spork (a glutton, he is. Just like Maya.) but I think that's too much reading into it. It really probably is just as Akira said, a manifestation of his child's mind's way to disassociate from his body during Sekai's "advances" by conjuring up cartoon characters that he knows. Sad, really.
As mentioned once shortly in a previous post, Kirin's redemption arc is in full swing. I get why people would hate her, but she is actively trying to better herself. She is kind of in similar shoes as Nu Maya, as she is trying to adept to a new situation and coming clean with her feelings and what she wants. She does love her sister, and that kind of redeems her earlier subpar reaction to the whole incident where she just ended up hate-fucking Akira.
As aramaug said, this whole event was beautifully written, even with the monks basically forcing Akira to say out loud what he honestly thinks, making Kirin realize even more how alike their situations are and that Akira actually may be a right fit for her. She was very sweet and honestly very relatable, acting like a decent human being with her own interests but showing that she is indeed capable of caring for the ones closest to her. It makes me think back to the "fuck, marry, kill" event and her reaction to picking her for marriage and how it all makes sense now.
Also she looks hot in that outfit. Like an actual adult for once.
Also Chika is super crazy, I hate her. I still don't want to talk about her.
Otoha being her inconsistent and contradicting self is giving great advice.
She is not afraid to tell him how it is. The irony of course being that a lot of the advice and correct analysis on Akira also applies to herself. But that is what makes her authentic, there are no teenagers that are wise and perfect and act according to their own moral compass all the time. They are hypocrites, even most adults are. But I do believe that her heart is in the right place.
I find it cute how she keeps trolling him, it does kind of feel a bit like how an older sister would act towards her lil brother. She cares about him, she forgives him for his flaws, tries to lead him to the correct direction for his own good. I do hope Akira learns to appreciate her more. And gets to make out with her in her dorm room outfit, hnngh. I already went over her dorm room event, here's the post if you are interested.
For the record, I don't think this is any indicator for rabies or an inherent insanity hidden inside Touka. Just some comedic relief and and insight in her...love for horses
I also got to learn two new words and add them to my vocabulary, thank you Selebus.
So my wish from a few pages ago that Akira is to finally overcome his bitchy emo phase and reconcile with the Nu Maya and give her a chance has actually come true. Great Success.
The whole interaction was pretty wholesome and another sign that Akira is bettering himself. As mentioned during the Imani part, as well as with how he interacted with Kirin, he does seem to open up more emotionally. Dare I say, he might be actually growing as a person. For now at least.

spoilers.title: Maya
spoilers.html:
So my wish from a few pages ago that Akira is to finally overcome his bitchy emo phase and reconcile with the Nu Maya and give her a chance has actually come true. Great Success.
The whole interaction was pretty wholesome and another sign that Akira is bettering himself. As mentioned during the Imani part, as well as with how he interacted with Kirin, he does seem to open up more emotionally. Dare I say, he might be actually growing as a person. For now at least.
But there are still a lot of stepping stones. It was disappointing to see how he still lacks the backbone to properly reject Chika and get her head back on. A situation he obviously created himself and admittedly not an easy one to solve. How do you cure someone who has rabies? I could imagine Sel having deliberately chosen this metaphor to have it end in her being "put down" by someone. Whether literally or not. Either causing another reset or maybe even the beginning of the dark route.

Which brings me to my main point. As Moonflare mentioned first, a lot of those developments (including those I missed) seem to lead towards some sort of major escalation, in one way or another.
As previously mentioned by others, it is now being openly discussed that everyone basically knows Akira is screwing almost all the girls by now, it's really no secret anymore. This is sure to cause tension sooner rather than later. More and more characters are becoming manic or are at least experiencing intense emotional turmoil. It feels like a powder keg that is just waiting for a spark to ignite it all.

What will Chika do once she inevitably understands that her concept of how Akira "loves" the girls and treats everyone does not align with her wicked view of this situation?
When will Ami (attempt to) murder someone? (knife foreshadowing was very on the nose this update)
What is Ami's gameplan in the first place? For an infinitely wise and all-knowing being, she seems kind of stuck and unsure of how to reach her end goal. Which I'm actually still not sure about what it is exactly.
She mentioned straight up that this timeline feels "nostalgic" to her. Which I have no clue how to interpret. Given Prime Maya's assessment, this timeline was apparently an extreme outlier in how Akira behaves, how far everything was developing, so how would this feel nostalgic to Prime Ami? Unless this goes so far back that even Prime Maya would not remember how it used to be. Maybe a sign that Akira is coming closer to change the world to it's original/destined form?

And what if that world would actually not include Maya? This update really made the "Maya is not real" stocks sky-rocket. She herself admitted that she does not remember anything prior to her being adopted by Akira.
I mean, it's as clear as day.
Unless...
Unless maybe this is going to end up being a situation where (again MASSIVE SPOILERS for who has not seen the movie Oldboy) it's an Oldboyesque scenario where Maya ends up being Akira's daughter, hence why her memories were deleted as she would have to remember her Mom or whoever raised her and where she came from. Ayane even shortly mentions how alike Maya and Akira are. Now this might of course lose a bit of its impact, given he is basically already doing that with Ami, but the difference, I guess, being that Ami is doing it willingly and knowingly, while Maya might have been coerced into doing it by certain entities (erasing her memory) for some ultimate goal, completely left in the dark that her lover is also her Dad. Maybe Ami actually is only so much into screwing her Dad, simply because she knows about the consequence of Maya baring a child with Akira and is somehow trying to emulate her and "taking her place". I don't know, this theory is kind of getting out of hand. I guess I just really like the movie Oldboy. But yeah, maybe there is an ounce of something sensible in there.

There are three primary flags you have to set in order to see the ‘green’ Tsukasa scene like you are:

1. Chose to see Chinami in the bath during “The Gap in the Door” way back in Chapter 2.
2. Chose Tsukasa instead of Chinami during the “Holden Caulfield” event.
3. With the above two flags set in motion, you unlock the prerequisites needed to see Tsukasa’s three character events from 0.38: “Vow of Silence (Pole Position)”, “Blood & Sunset”, and “Failsafe”.

Note how the last event is underlined. It’s that event in particular that, if seen, triggers the curious Tsukasa content in this update.

Edit: You also need to have watched Tsubasa's h-scene, which first requires you to have seen Futaba and Molly's lust events. Futaba requires 40 lust and Molly needs 10 lust for you to see them both. Thanks Bingoogus for the reminder on that one.

Anyways, here's a few thoughts from my side on the update:
First off, this update really shone a light on the differences between the green and (various) red paths. Reading others experiences, it became clear that quite a lot of dialogue and even whole events were completely absent if you were diverting from the green path.
Examples:
  • If you're on the good uncle path, Ami is apparently a lot less straightforward to Niki on Akira's behaviour. She does openly say that she wants to fuck her Dad, but she didn't (in this timeline) so from Niki's perspective it's still just threats from a rambling and hormonal, albeit weird, kid. There's no great revelation that Akira is fucking half the class or his niece/daughter. Which begs the question, how will that really impact the story going forward, given that in one instance Niki is apparently made aware and in the other still blissfully unaware? Unless I misread the other point of view presented by other user's posts.
  • If you are not on the correct path with Tsukasa, you just straight up miss out on her second event apparently. And the same goes for Tsubasa's, unless there was a different trigger for that one.
  • If you are not on Kirin's blackmail path, Kirin never apologizes to Ayane at the end of her event chain, in fact, she storms past her and explicitly tells her she is the second to last person she wants to see right now.
  • If you are like me and you don't specifically enjoy the sex acts with Futaba since they feel like taking advantage of a severely insecure teen (not like it's not the case with others, but with Futaba I actually do feel bad), you will likely miss out on her second event, which in turn, will also lock you out of the Molly event, even if you fulfill her lust requirement. Which is an odd programming choice, but I assume that Molly's event must somehow pick up from Futaba's event, so that it could not work alone by itself without the previous one happening?
There might be more, other than obvious dialogue variations, feel free to let me know if you noticed anything else.
And yes, I know, I could just use URM to change the values and get the events anyway. But first of all, it's about the principal, I'm evaluating the natural user experience when playing the game blind and how much content can be missed by seemingly arbitrary player decisions. And while I don't say this is bad per se, I feel like it should still be highlighted that the game might feel incomplete if you don't follow something like the guide mod or alter values in URM.
Which brings me to my second point, altering the values to see certain events still won't necessarily give you context. Sure, you will see the situation unfolding as if the requirements were met, but you effectively did not experience the exact events that led to said outcome. This may not always be relevant, especially for lewd scenes I assume, but it's still a reason for me to disregard URM for now. spoilers.title: A tale of two  ̶c̶i̶t̶i̶e̶s̶ paths
spoilers.html:
First off, this update really shone a light on the differences between the green and (various) red paths. Reading others experiences, it became clear that quite a lot of dialogue and even whole events were completely absent if you were diverting from the green path.
Examples:
  • If you're on the good uncle path, Ami is apparently a lot less straightforward to Niki on Akira's behaviour. She does openly say that she wants to fuck her Dad, but she didn't (in this timeline) so from Niki's perspective it's still just threats from a rambling and hormonal, albeit weird, kid. There's no great revelation that Akira is fucking half the class or his niece/daughter. Which begs the question, how will that really impact the story going forward, given that in one instance Niki is apparently made aware and in the other still blissfully unaware? Unless I misread the other point of view presented by other user's posts.
  • If you are not on the correct path with Tsukasa, you just straight up miss out on her second event apparently. And the same goes for Tsubasa's, unless there was a different trigger for that one.
  • If you are not on Kirin's blackmail path, Kirin never apologizes to Ayane at the end of her event chain, in fact, she storms past her and explicitly tells her she is the second to last person she wants to see right now.
  • If you are like me and you don't specifically enjoy the sex acts with Futaba since they feel like taking advantage of a severely insecure teen (not like it's not the case with others, but with Futaba I actually do feel bad), you will likely miss out on her second event, which in turn, will also lock you out of the Molly event, even if you fulfill her lust requirement. Which is an odd programming choice, but I assume that Molly's event must somehow pick up from Futaba's event, so that it could not work alone by itself without the previous one happening?
There might be more, other than obvious dialogue variations, feel free to let me know if you noticed anything else.
And yes, I know, I could just use URM to change the values and get the events anyway. But first of all, it's about the principal, I'm evaluating the natural user experience when playing the game blind and how much content can be missed by seemingly arbitrary player decisions. And while I don't say this is bad per se, I feel like it should still be highlighted that the game might feel incomplete if you don't follow something like the guide mod or alter values in URM.
Which brings me to my second point, altering the values to see certain events still won't necessarily give you context. Sure, you will see the situation unfolding as if the requirements were met, but you effectively did not experience the exact events that led to said outcome. This may not always be relevant, especially for lewd scenes I assume, but it's still a reason for me to disregard URM for now. Instead this just gives me more motivation to finish my replay quickly and get a green path up to date so that I can use it for a second run of new updates to complete all events.
