spoilers.title: Maya
spoilers.html:
So my wish from a few pages ago that Akira is to finally overcome his bitchy emo phase and reconcile with the Nu Maya and give her a chance has actually come true. Great Success.
The whole interaction was pretty wholesome and another sign that Akira is bettering himself. As mentioned during the Imani part, as well as with how he interacted with Kirin, he does seem to open up more emotionally. Dare I say, he might be actually growing as a person. For now at least.
But there are still a lot of stepping stones. It was disappointing to see how he still lacks the backbone to properly reject Chika and get her head back on. A situation he obviously created himself and admittedly not an easy one to solve. How do you cure someone who has rabies? I could imagine Sel having deliberately chosen this metaphor to have it end in her being "put down" by someone. Whether literally or not. Either causing another reset or maybe even the beginning of the dark route.

Which brings me to my main point. As Moonflare mentioned first, a lot of those developments (including those I missed) seem to lead towards some sort of major escalation, in one way or another.
As previously mentioned by others, it is now being openly discussed that everyone basically knows Akira is screwing almost all the girls by now, it's really no secret anymore. This is sure to cause tension sooner rather than later. More and more characters are becoming manic or are at least experiencing intense emotional turmoil. It feels like a powder keg that is just waiting for a spark to ignite it all.

What will Chika do once she inevitably understands that her concept of how Akira "loves" the girls and treats everyone does not align with her wicked view of this situation?
When will Ami (attempt to) murder someone? (knife foreshadowing was very on the nose this update)
What is Ami's gameplan in the first place? For an infinitely wise and all-knowing being, she seems kind of stuck and unsure of how to reach her end goal. Which I'm actually still not sure about what it is exactly.
She mentioned straight up that this timeline feels "nostalgic" to her. Which I have no clue how to interpret. Given Prime Maya's assessment, this timeline was apparently an extreme outlier in how Akira behaves, how far everything was developing, so how would this feel nostalgic to Prime Ami? Unless this goes so far back that even Prime Maya would not remember how it used to be. Maybe a sign that Akira is coming closer to change the world to it's original/destined form?

And what if that world would actually not include Maya? This update really made the "Maya is not real" stocks sky-rocket. She herself admitted that she does not remember anything prior to her being adopted by Akira.
I mean, it's as clear as day.
Unless...
Unless maybe this is going to end up being a situation where (again MASSIVE SPOILERS for who has not seen the movie Oldboy) it's an Oldboyesque scenario where Maya ends up being Akira's daughter, hence why her memories were deleted as she would have to remember her Mom or whoever raised her and where she came from. Ayane even shortly mentions how alike Maya and Akira are. Now this might of course lose a bit of its impact, given he is basically already doing that with Ami, but the difference, I guess, being that Ami is doing it willingly and knowingly, while Maya might have been coerced into doing it by certain entities (erasing her memory) for some ultimate goal, completely left in the dark that her lover is also her Dad. Maybe Ami actually is only so much into screwing her Dad, simply because she knows about the consequence of Maya baring a child with Akira and is somehow trying to emulate her and "taking her place". I don't know, this theory is kind of getting out of hand. I guess I just really like the movie Oldboy. But yeah, maybe there is an ounce of something sensible in there.

I don't really understand your point. I see Chapter 4 as a natural progression of things.
In chapter 1, Akira is some dude trying to pretend he's sensei and just corrupt some girls cause why not.

Chapter 2 is about him slowly realising he is that one dude, and that his past and who he is is really fucked.

Chapter 3 is when things come to a head: His name is Akira, he got fucked by Sekai's death, his one true love since then is Maya. He is also a puppet in the hands of many gods, he tries to control his life and yet it only makes it get further out of control until Maya dies because of him.

Chapter 4 is the breakdown. Maya is gone. He knows enough of the past to be put into a situation that he can't deal with it and yet the one person that dealt with it for him isn't here anymore. So he leaves school. He tries to depend on Ami but she turns insane, so he tries to focus on being a parent. But his mind becomes more and more deranged, so he relies on fighting against Pareidolia for control, until, surprise! Pareidolia is also gone. What now? Akira is unhinged. He's making passes at snowmen during parties and the girls don't even blink, that's how bad it's gotten.

Chapter 4 is uncomfortable imo, but that's because we're deep into the spiral, and he becomes even more passive. This update points that out rather well. Maybe if you try replaying it you'll notice how pitiful Akira becomes. It's not a mindless sex-bot going around and that's our game. It's a very sad vestige of a human being that is insane, and breaks down monologuing enough to make Kirin of all people start crying just hearing what he's saying about himself (I cried during the scene as well).

Now, imo, Akira needs to bounce back. I get that he was off for christmas (with the monks and all), but he needs to get on. It's understandable that the harem will start interacting more and more because well, they need to since everyone is starting to know that everyone else is also fucking him. Chaos and breakdowns in that sense are fine. But if Akira doesn't step up regarding supernatural stuff soon, it will start getting really tiresome. He can't just keep going around being insane when everyone has been telling him left and right that it only happens because he lets it.

This update seemed to point at this also since it's supposed to be about Akira finally waking up enough to get New Maya back into his life and be a little less passive about everything. We'll see how it goes.
On a different tangent, man - so, we're officially on the second half of chapter 4 and yet we have NO SANA PROTAGONISM that would justify her being the chapter cover yet lol what is up with that?

spoilers.html:
In chapter 1, Akira is some dude trying to pretend he's sensei and just corrupt some girls cause why not.

Chapter 2 is about him slowly realising he is that one dude, and that his past and who he is is really fucked.

Chapter 3 is when things come to a head: His name is Akira, he got fucked by Sekai's death, his one true love since then is Maya. He is also a puppet in the hands of many gods, he tries to control his life and yet it only makes it get further out of control until Maya dies because of him.

Chapter 4 is the breakdown. Maya is gone. He knows enough of the past to be put into a situation that he can't deal with it and yet the one person that dealt with it for him isn't here anymore. So he leaves school. He tries to depend on Ami but she turns insane, so he tries to focus on being a parent. But his mind becomes more and more deranged, so he relies on fighting against Pareidolia for control, until, surprise! Pareidolia is also gone. What now? Akira is unhinged. He's making passes at snowmen during parties and the girls don't even blink, that's how bad it's gotten.

Chapter 4 is uncomfortable imo, but that's because we're deep into the spiral, and he becomes even more passive. This update points that out rather well. Maybe if you try replaying it you'll notice how pitiful Akira becomes. It's not a mindless sex-bot going around and that's our game. It's a very sad vestige of a human being that is insane, and breaks down monologuing enough to make Kirin of all people start crying just hearing what he's saying about himself (I cried during the scene as well).

Now, imo, Akira needs to bounce back. I get that he was off for christmas (with the monks and all), but he needs to get on. It's understandable that the harem will start interacting more and more because well, they need to since everyone is starting to know that everyone else is also fucking him. Chaos and breakdowns in that sense are fine. But if Akira doesn't step up regarding supernatural stuff soon, it will start getting really tiresome. He can't just keep going around being insane when everyone has been telling him left and right that it only happens because he lets it.

This update seemed to point at this also since it's supposed to be about Akira finally waking up enough to get New Maya back into his life and be a little less passive about everything. We'll see how it goes.

DeanNoriko said:
Very good post that sums it up well.
This is no love story, no harem game. This is a drama about a deranged man with trauma-induced mental illness in a strange world. You get what you paid for. And the worst is still ahead of us.
At least there is the prospect of purity routes to give closure, so I don't think it's fair to judge the game as being too depressing and degenerate before the plot has even moved on towards the climax.


I'm telling you guys, it's just Sel being "Ah fuck, I need to pick a girl, whatever, let's pick Sana YOLO lol". You guys will be utterly disappointed if you still expect her to become the center of the plot for chapter 4. (I will probably be wrong now and look stupid in hindsight)

On another note though, since I haven't seen it mentioned yet:
What's that about Akira quitting teaching altogether? I feel like that came way out of left field, at least I didn't see it coming.
It also doesn't really seem too sensible. Being a school teacher has essentially given him the alibi to even be seen around teenage girls or to participate in their "school" events.
I mean, not that the world building in this game has been very much focused on moral logic so far, given the behavior of parents and basically the absence of a school principal that would give even 0.1% of a fuck about what the teachers are actually doing (or not doing) during their classes.
Even abandoning all logic, what would Akira want to do in his free time anyway?
It seems like Sel has an idea and is steering the story towards it now, I just don't see it yet.
Unless he is planning to watch football with (a forgiving) Karin at home from now on, which I would accept as the entirety of the dark route, thank you.

What do you guys think Akira will do once he quits teaching (which I think is inevitable now that it has been brought up)?

On another note though, since I haven't seen it mentioned yet:
What's that about Akira quitting teaching altogether? I feel like that came way out of left field, at least I didn't see it coming.
It also doesn't really seem too sensible. Being a school teacher has essentially given him the alibi to even be seen around teenage girls or to participate in their "school" events.
I mean, not that the world building in this game has been very much focused on moral logic so far, given the behavior of parents and basically the absence of a school principal that would give even 0.1% of a fuck about what the teachers are actually doing (or not doing) during their classes.

It seems like Sel has an idea and is steering the story towards it now, I just don't see it yet.

Click to expand...
So much to talk about. Well, Akira has said that he wanted to be a teacher to prevent people like him ending up like him. Which is a very believable positive outcome of a trauma such as his. Has he ever achieved this though? It's debatable. He seemed not to engage in grooming before the resets (other than Maya and maybe Yumi).
But then again is that even the truth? Or did he get into teaching because it was yet another step in becoming Sekai? It's hard to say for sure. Aditionally, he has hardly taught for a single day during the entire game. At most he taught for a bit on the roof and stuff like that.

So if Akira ever started to teach it would definitely be novel. But also, who would he teach? The entire classroom is a harem or soon to be one - they're stuck in a loop and knowledge vanishes. It's kind of pointless (which is the crux of Wakana's existence as one).

Regarding what would he do with the rest of his time, well, it depends on Himawari (and Selebus) I guess. If the world keeps getting more and more chaotic, him being a teacher will hardly matter.

If I had to make a guess, we can go one of two ways from here, solving all the mysteries of the backstories (Sana/Sara's is a strong contender to go first) and resolving harem stuff (both in the sense of threesomes and in the sense of lingering stuff, like Nodoka having sexually assaulted Yumi and Futaba still unaware of it). The latter has become a bit more probable given that the Kirin blackmail got resurrected in order to be finally resolved.
Regardless, as always, Akira needs to deal with Sekai stuff - which, to his credit, he has been for some time. Let's hope he can make enough peace with it to discover what he can be in spite of it.

Black Raven said:
A statement made by Selebus on discord following the recent events [from February 2023]. Now with 40% less hostility. [snip]
Click to expand...
... What even was the point of all this?

Honestly speaking (with the added infallibility of a year's worth of retrospective), there isn't a lot of "talent" in LiL that can't be found elsewhere. To compress an essay's worth of critique into a single sentence, I think a significant majority of LiL readers have been long exhausted with the writing of Selebus, and are exclusively—or at least mostly—invested in LiL for two sole reasons: the characters and the purpose of it all (the time loop overarching plotline). Beyond this, I would say very little matters.

It doesn't take an awe-inspiring amount of talent to drop a winning hook and spend actual years drawing it out while simultaneously bragging about the length, but not the efficiency of said story. I've joked about this before, where I wagered that Selebus could probably finish his game using ChatGPT AI writing prompts and nobody would notice. I understand why a lot of people are interested in LiL solely for the premise and character interactions, but beyond that, a lot more people are simply bored of LiL's writing and gameplay loop, and just want to know how it all ends for their favorite girls (or Gods). I wouldn't call that talented per-se, maybe closer to a passionate one-trick pony type of deal.

I admit this a very simplistic take but springtime is associated with sexual/romantic exploration ("springtime of our youth", spring break/Girls gone Wild). I don't really have a lot of evidence to support this on hand but it FEELS right. In other words, if Sel has to solve for orgy, leaning into spring and it's symbolism in poetry/culture seems like a perfectly sensible way to do it.

posts.content_html_raw:
I'd say he's great at character writing. This does take some talent. But a lot of the rest is heavily reliant on minimal information, leaving the audience to speculate (which he seems to get mad about?). And the massive crutch of using deliberately opaque writing. Phrasing things in weird, murky ways is interesting in small doses, in large doses the sheen wears off and it just comes off as pretentious.
If you strip all of the strange phrasing and and visuals away, the resulting story is extremely basic, if dark, propping up a well written though immoral slice of life.

Marie IV said:
I think a significant majority of LiL readers have been long exhausted with the writing of Selebus, and are exclusively—or at least mostly—invested in LiL for two sole reasons: the characters and the purpose of it all (the time loop overarching plotline)
Click to expand...
On a meta level, you can only be exhausted with Selebus' writing and still be invested in the story and characters if what you like is the idea behind the story or the characters. The execution is too tied to Selebus' writing. Being exhausted with Selebus, tho, is a different matter.
If it's the case where what you like is only the idea, there's a multitude of LiL "clones" to choose depending on how close to the LiL idea you want to be, and in each of those, you can see the quality is VERY different compared to LiL (not being too critical on SOME of those, LiL just set the goal too high, the few of them I chose to read have all my love). Like it or not, Selebus' way of telling the story is what has kept this going on despite Selebus.
Or, if you want.
Marie IV said:
It doesn't take an awe-inspiring amount of talent to drop a winning hook and spend actual years drawing it out while simultaneously bragging about the length, but not the efficiency of said story.
Click to expand...
As pretentious as this may sound, the story that is being told through LiL needs the drawing out, otherwise it's efficiency WILL suffer. It'd just feel like a disturbing apologetic piece, or worse, something that even with a thorough reading feels like it's just throwing shit to the wall for mere shock value. Only actual critic would be to the sandbox model, though even there the generic events flesh out stuff.
EDIT: And, as mentioned in the post above mine, the basic idea is that, basic, but LiL has been kept afloat because of the execution of said idea.

People who can sleep standing up freak me out in a "I have never thought about this ever before but now that I do I kind of feel it in a very mild sort of way"... sort of way? I don't know, but you get the point. It's just kinda strange.

Of course calling anime stupid would wake Molly up...
Oof... Poor Rin... That "date" got canceled huh.
I still remember that goofy gamer... Molly was it? Ahh, that was so long ago...

At least Molly was included in the list of people Rin would go for.

Suddenly the mc is being more open about his memory issues with Rin. Guess that's sort of understandable.
Oh, well that came out of nowhere. Or did it? That first kiss between the mc and Rin. Maybe they aren't so far apart romantically/sexually after all.
I guess it kinda makes sense. This world has a way of making everyone suddenly drawn to him. Rin is bi but mostly lesbian and his been there when Rin has been going through some tough times and I guess spending so much time together under the pretenses of it being a hang out but actually a date.
Now that I think about it, this kinda feel more pure than many of the other relationships he had.

Autovn is weird... I just had it do a morning activity and then go meet Ami at the maid cafe. You can't visit the maid cafe in the afternoon so how did the game manage to do that? Yes, I doublechecked so it didn't happen on Saturday.
I knew Ami was gonna instantly cheer up to hearing "I love you", I knew it was coming. So obvious too. She's way too easy.

Does the game actually remember that you patted someone 500 times? Ami just pointed out something weird happens when he pats her head and I can only imagine that would only be weird once he gets a couple hundred pats in at least... at least in this game.

One thing I'm noticing is that I think autovn chose to visit Io to see her and Uta's dorm for the first time instead of Uta like it did last time as it offers more unread dialogues. I'm guessing autovn is quite literally coded to automatically target whatever path has the most unread dialogues.
Okay, I skipped ahead and yes, 500 headpats do INDEED affect the dialogue here. Ami feels awkward having an orgasm from headpatting. Was it worth the 10 minutes of skipping or whatever it was? I dunno.
Of course autovn is stupid and doesn't automatically select unread events sometime over deciding to go home for the millionth time but what can you do.

Aww, Karin getting exciting he liked her cookies!
To be fair, I bet talking to him is harder than a sport for Karin.
Ahh yes, the disembodied organs circus. I can't say I've heard about it before but I'm sure it exists... somewhere. Well, the organ as an instrument appears to exist but not actual organs. Weird.

Oh god... Not again. Another difficult decision I feel.
Oh? I see I see. So being honest with Karin puts you on the red path. You have to lie out of your teeth or you get a missed event check. It hurts to see Karin like that anyway.

New girl time! But the portrait on the tierlist doesn't match...

Wait a damn minute... No she's already on the tierlist, it's Niki who isn't. Noriko just had spiky hair when I saw her last.

UH OH! Maya has never reacted like that before!
I don't even know what the fuck to say about this. Something is very clearly wrong and you know that if Maya is reacting like this, it's serious. She called her a "filthy stalker bitch".
Her fucking eyes are scary. You know the entire class is already shaken up by the appearance of Noriko but if they aren't shaken to the fucking core by Maya's reaction, I don't know what possibly could.
You just know that this point in time has some serious significance. Like yeah, the school sinking through the ground is one thing but Noriko finding her way here seems like a nuclear level serious.
At this point, it should be absolutely impossible to figure out what the reason for Maya's reaction is, but man do I want to find out.
Is Noriko somehow the cause for the space war? Was there some kind of romance going on between Maya and Sensei Noriko ruined? Did Noriko somehow cause Sensei's now shifting personality? Maybe Noriko caused Maya to relive this moment in time over and over again? I personally feel like that last one sounds convincing enough but only time will tell.

Oh, is Noriko the "Anarchist" or whatever Wakana said?
Knowing Maya called her some stalker, reacted that badly and Noriko just said some sketchy stuff about being arrested and serial killer, who the fuck knows? Something tells me she might just be the most problematic girl in the game and no one who comes after will be any less problematic.
Okay that's just weird, like super fucking weird to me. Ami reacted concerned by Noriko but it's like Ayane doesn't even care even tho Noriko is basically exactly the same as her if not MORE obsessive. I mean, I can't imagine what it's like developing a love at that early age that has time to root itself like that.
Already 50 affection, and let me guess. Her lust is at N/A because she doesn't need it due to how obsessive she is.
In other news, I've aligned her name to her appearance to her profile. Still weird that she has two different main-ish hairstyles.

But not only does she appear to be the most special of them all but she actually can pull of a hair style I don't immediately reject the idea of. Just wonder if the weird clothing sense will stick too...

What if Noriko is borderline Yandere and that would explain both the love and her behavior?
She... carries knives.

I dunno about you, but the only 6 year olds I spent time with while I was much older than them was blood related and I wanted to be far away from them anyway.
Ahh, neighbours. No that explains it... I mean, sort of.
I see. That means the sister should be close to his age. Will probably show up sooner or later. But that must be some sort of age gap between the sisters.
I want to say Noriko's use of "eternity" holds some deeper meaning, but there is nothing besides the word that could imply it does. Maybe I'm just on edge right now?
I expected a visit from either Maya, Noriko or someone concerned about the situation between them. I didn't expect both Maya and Noriko. Wild.

In other completely irrelevant news. Maya's new winter outfit in profile is really cute. That is all.

So let me get this straight. Maya just doesn't like Noriko and is concerned Noriko can somehow fuck up Sensei's life quicker than he thinks. So that either means she's hiding something serious that justifies her reaction, or this whole thing is blown WAAAAAAY out of proportion and it's really just that simple that there is a person she hates so much more than him without a proper reason.
No, it's too early. What would be the point in revealing everything right away?
Dude. This entire section ever since Noriko shows up have added 4500+ characters to this. This is how easy a giant plot twist can influence how much I write... and this isn't helping either sooo...

Didn't take long for the stalker thing to become a reality.

I feel like if anyone is gonna die in this game it's gonna be because of Noriko and there might be some weird reset shenanigans that show up and save the day.

Oh, here we go. I had a tiny spoiler about this Niki from elsewhere so I know she is famous enough to hide her face.

Well this is interesting. A very attractive "famous" idol with some justified anger issues who he used to get along with... probably.
Ahh yes. She made the menu music. Should I also pretend this is her voice? It's pretty nice.

Oh, I should have guessed Noriko and Kirin would end up in the same room. Guess my mind was elsewhere (surprisingly).

Hundredth reminder that the mc has not bothered looking up his own name which should be written on paperwork all over his house. No, it's totally fine, I'm not frustrated by this plot what so ever...

Gotta love how the events preview picture in Niki's profile spoils the next couple seconds. Also that's the second girl who apparently has sex scenes coming up by the end of this chapter who was just introduced. That bugs me for whatever reason.
Anyone knows what diner from a first person shooter the game was referring to? Niki's first event.
Okay... Knowing who the waitress is gonna be, I would be surprised if she recognizes her.

Niki's angry face is so common and so different from others for some reason. Think it's the makeup.

What a weird day...

posts.content_html_raw:
It's...getting more difficult to give her the benefit of the doubt regarding how she handles Tsukasa. But as naive as it sounds, I want to believe that she genuinely loves Tsukasa, I want to believe that her reactions when learning firsthand about Tsukasa's loneliness in We Happy Few, and the subsequent pool time in To Lift This Aching Head were real. However, as a head Tsukioka, Tsubasa can only do so in very roundabout, nonsensically medieval ways because of her environment, because of her priority, and because of the fact that her mindset has already been shaped into a classic Tsukioka.

Among all the horrifying plays she does in this update, one line of hers stands out the most for me. "With an attitude like that, you'll never last in this family." This line isn't a response to Tsukasa being a whiney brat. No, this line is the response to Tsukasa verbalizing her worries of being a nuances to everyone as someone not old enough for attending middle school. Whether or not Tsubasa considers this an weakness or other qualities unfit as a Tsukioka, her response gives me a sense of real concern for Tsukasa. Moreover, it gives me the feeling that when it comes to Tsukasa's foreseeable future, there are only three viable options that don't spell misery: either Tsukasa fulfills her role as a backup and replaces Touka, or she leaves the family for good to avoid the fate of a backup that no longer has its use, or Tsubasa climbs to the absolute apex of the pyramid so that it empowers her to keep Tsukasa here with her just as her daughter against any screwed up traditions the Tsukiokas may or may not have been practicing on heirs that didn't end up on the throne.

Mostly importantly, with a status already so high up in the hierarchy, I don't see the need for Tsubasa to be this mindful around Tsukasa if Tsubasa really is done with being Tsukasa's mother and will only treat Tsukasa as just another asset. Any of this by no mean absolves her from being a horrible mother, but I am willing to believe that Tsubasa does see Tsukasa as her own daughter and have a plan for Tsukasa that isn't simply just giving her away to a groomer.

spoilers.title: Thoughts on 0.46 Tsubasa
spoilers.html:
It's...getting more difficult to give her the benefit of the doubt regarding how she handles Tsukasa. But as naive as it sounds, I want to believe that she genuinely loves Tsukasa, I want to believe that her reactions when learning firsthand about Tsukasa's loneliness in We Happy Few, and the subsequent pool time in To Lift This Aching Head were real. However, as a head Tsukioka, Tsubasa can only do so in very roundabout, nonsensically medieval ways because of her environment, because of her priority, and because of the fact that her mindset has already been shaped into a classic Tsukioka.

Among all the horrifying plays she does in this update, one line of hers stands out the most for me. "With an attitude like that, you'll never last in this family." This line isn't a response to Tsukasa being a whiney brat. No, this line is the response to Tsukasa verbalizing her worries of being a nuances to everyone as someone not old enough for attending middle school. Whether or not Tsubasa considers this an weakness or other qualities unfit as a Tsukioka, her response gives me a sense of real concern for Tsukasa. Moreover, it gives me the feeling that when it comes to Tsukasa's foreseeable future, there are only three viable options that don't spell misery: either Tsukasa fulfills her role as a backup and replaces Touka, or she leaves the family for good to avoid the fate of a backup that no longer has its use, or Tsubasa climbs to the absolute apex of the pyramid so that it empowers her to keep Tsukasa here with her just as her daughter against any screwed up traditions the Tsukiokas may or may not have been practicing on heirs that didn't end up on the throne.

Mostly importantly, with a status already so high up in the hierarchy, I don't see the need for Tsubasa to be this mindful around Tsukasa if Tsubasa really is done with being Tsukasa's mother and will only treat Tsukasa as just another asset. Any of this by no mean absolves her from being a horrible mother, but I am willing to believe that Tsubasa does see Tsukasa as her own daughter and have a plan for Tsukasa that isn't simply just giving her away to a groomer.

posts.content_html_raw:
Although by all rights this update should have appealed to me immensely with its focus on entertainment and developing the romances, by this point I cannot help but feel that many of the beats ring hollow to me. This is not to criticize the text itself - in the first place, the degree of 'engagement' one is supposed to feel in the Predation Of High Schoolers is something the game calls into question, so this is exclusively a personal matter for me. Where previously I might have felt significantly engaged and excited by such scenes as Futaba, Rin, Ayana, Nodoka, and Sana all openly discussing their lust for sensei, or scenes such as Kirin proclaiming her love for Sensei, now I felt no stir within my breast or smile upon my face. In a sense, I really just don't care or like it that much. The first two reasons that came to mind for this were: one, it's been 2 months and perhaps my investment in all of the characters faded more intently in these months than in any months prior, or two, advancements in the plot have made it difficult to take these elements as seriously.

For the first point it's a miracle I've remained engaged in any long-running serial for more than a year, but the second point is potentially more interesting. It does indeed feel hard to take Kirin's proclamation of love seriously as Sensei existence as a lumbering sex automaton only continues to be reinforced, and one must thank Chika for her interruption since it saves us potentially tens of thousands of words of drama on the subject later. Perhaps at one point I felt there was tension and risk in the story; now, I have no such illusions, which itself is also pronounced with the whole arc of Sensei bemoaning he can do nothing wrong. It is in fact wholly disheartening to see the fact that it becoming public knowledge that Sensei is fucking 1/2 of the class is not really changing the inevitable course of the harem route. The artificial hand guiding the fiction in this direction was always opaque in its presence, but now it presses its palm firmly against the camera.

This is a lot of meandering (even for me) to say that while the game may have previously danced (or seemed to dance) a toe between realism and fiction, this update fully dunks one's head into fiction and such that we emerge with our hair sopping wet with the glistening juices of more girls than one can count on both hands. The idea of there being a sort of hivemind compelling all of the girls to lust for Sensei has always been floating about, and at this point it seems more likely than ever that the girls are indeed being forced to act like this - being blinded, having their memories altered, having alpha male pheromones blast their skulls, having other people wear their skin, etc etc. In short, 'harem characters being controlled by a harem narrative,' and at this point it feels like a large part of their personal agency / individuality / realism has been sacrificed on this alter. Call me a curmudgeon, but Chika is by far acting the most realistically right now, and it strains belief that most of these girls would be so casual about Sensei fucking all of their friends.

[[[It is at this moment I make an aside to say: if you are Selebus and reading this, FUCK YOU!!! I TOLD YOU NOT TO READ THIS!!! FUCK YOU FUCK YOU FUCK YOU!!! CLOSE THE TAB! GO AWAY! SQUASH YOUR OBSESSION TO READ EVERYTHING ABOUT YOURSELF THAT EXISTS ON THE NET! THIS ISNT FOR YOU! REEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE]]]

One potential problem is that while I once struggled to parse the sanctity of Sensei's character, I now struggle to parse the sanctity of EVERY character. Are they themselves? Are they all being brainwashed? How many of them even 'exist' at all? Each time a comparison is drawn between Sensei and another character I wince as I add that to the evidence pile that they are a fragment of his personality, for instance. This is not to say I interpret the 'some guy is semi-metaphorically strapped to a chair in front of a computer imagining all of what happens as idealistic fiction' theory to be unquestionable, but rather that it is SO questionable that I have to keep questioning it, and the girls are really not doing any favors with their strained autonomy. For a LONG time I staved this sensation off due to 2021-era Selebus enthusiastically proclaiming that 'the girls had a lot of story to them, and he couldn't want to tell each,' but like, as these stories increasingly converge around Sensei's dick, I start to question whether that is truly strong evidence of their realness attribute being comfortably high. (Good Lord, the nightmare reality of Selebus being the guy in the chair, and each girl being a fragment of him (which is already true literally but hopefully not within the text), is not even fully deniable, since e.g. there is the fact Molly was based on his Irish ancestory).

So it is that like, even this built-up-to revelatory scene between Kirin and Sensei rings totally hollow to me. Not only have we been through it before, but there is zero romance when Kirin is clearly 'not looking at Sensei' and Sensei is clearly 'not looking at Kirin,' just like nobody is looking at anyone here. Is Kirin even real? Is Sensei even real? Is she acting with agency or because Sensei's magic musk overwhelms her puny girl brain? After she got pissed over Karin I never even questioned that over time she would get right back over it following some trivial prodding, and so it has happened, with a scene seeming to highlight her own confusion and difficulty grasping the situation - did she really get over it or is the harem narrative forcing her to? When I am questioning these foundational elements it's hard to really feel moved by her crying over him or him announcing his affection. As one may say - take out the foundation, and everything crumbles after. And of course, that may be the point. I don't mean to be too dramatic here. I'm not gnashing my teeth and proclaiming LiL to be totally dead to me or poorly written or whatever. Rather, an update I looked forward to a lot that ended up having exactly what I wanted ended up not speaking to me at all when I expected the opposite, and now I must contemplate this.

I do wonder if Selebus finds himself caught in the contradiction of the fakeness vs realism dynamic (altho as LiL itself proves, it is always a contradiction which creates the most compelling foundation for mythology). This is to say: as Sensei points out in this update, it's very plausible he could have raped Futaba on the first day without severely impacting their relationship. The other Senseis have stood as silent, implied reinforcements of LiL's existence as a porn game for the characters within it as well. And yet, there has been much richness to Futaba's character despite that, as well as with the other characters. It may be that what I am observing now is the moment where the fakeness attribute is shot so unbelievably damn high that the realness attribute ends up impoverished as a result. I think I remember Selebus saying on the discord in 2020 or so, early on, that harem stories are fucking retarded and can't be written competently. I must doff my hat and confirm that, as the Harem route becomes increasingly Harem, that it does feel like witnessing an increasingly retarded farce. At some point I genuinely believed (call me stupid) that some girls may end up not being in the harem after all; that, for example, perhaps Rin would stay with her girlfriends, or that he would settle things platonically with Yumi, or that maybe Touka would outmaneuver him. Now it's not even a question the full harem will be formed with any drama just proving to be roadbumps. And I'm not upset, just less engaged for now.

That said, I may enjoy the next update more; you never know! My favorite event in this update was, ironically given my comments above, Otoha moving in for a smooch with Sensei. The reason is not because I am invested a romance blooming between them or anything: it's because I really just did not expect that whatsoever. LiL stopped being exciting or surprising at the start of Chapter 4 for me, I think, and from then to now, that scene was the first (as I recall) that felt like I wanted to lean forward in my chair like, "wait, what's about to happen?" And so it did end on a high note. But I hope it keeps being surprising. Hopefully the 'show' Himawari has been building up to will be a big surprised in probably 3 months.

The reason is not because I am invested a romance blooming between them or anything: it's because I really just did not expect that whatsoever. LiL stopped being exciting or surprising at the start of Chapter 4 for me, I think, and from then to now, that scene was the first (as I recall) that felt like I wanted to lean forward in my chair like, "wait, what's about to happen?" And so it did end on a high note. But I hope it keeps being surprising. Hopefully the 'show' Himawari has been building up to will be a big surprised in probably 3 months.
spoilers.text:
Although by all rights this update should have appealed to me immensely with its focus on entertainment and developing the romances, by this point I cannot help but feel that many of the beats ring hollow to me. This is not to criticize the text itself - in the first place, the degree of 'engagement' one is supposed to feel in the Predation Of High Schoolers is something the game calls into question, so this is exclusively a personal matter for me. Where previously I might have felt significantly engaged and excited by such scenes as Futaba, Rin, Ayana, Nodoka, and Sana all openly discussing their lust for sensei, or scenes such as Kirin proclaiming her love for Sensei, now I felt no stir within my breast or smile upon my face. In a sense, I really just don't care or like it that much. The first two reasons that came to mind for this were: one, it's been 2 months and perhaps my investment in all of the characters faded more intently in these months than in any months prior, or two, advancements in the plot have made it difficult to take these elements as seriously.
For the first point it's a miracle I've remained engaged in any long-running serial for more than a year, but the second point is potentially more interesting. It does indeed feel hard to take Kirin's proclamation of love seriously as Sensei existence as a lumbering sex automaton only continues to be reinforced, and one must thank Chika for her interruption since it saves us potentially tens of thousands of words of drama on the subject later. Perhaps at one point I felt there was tension and risk in the story; now, I have no such illusions, which itself is also pronounced with the whole arc of Sensei bemoaning he can do nothing wrong. It is in fact wholly disheartening to see the fact that it becoming public knowledge that Sensei is fucking 1/2 of the class is not really changing the inevitable course of the harem route. The artificial hand guiding the fiction in this direction was always opaque in its presence, but now it presses its palm firmly against the camera.
This is a lot of meandering (even for me) to say that while the game may have previously danced (or seemed to dance) a toe between realism and fiction, this update fully dunks one's head into fiction and such that we emerge with our hair sopping wet with the glistening juices of more girls than one can count on both hands. The idea of there being a sort of hivemind compelling all of the girls to lust for Sensei has always been floating about, and at this point it seems more likely than ever that the girls are indeed being forced to act like this - being blinded, having their memories altered, having alpha male pheromones blast their skulls, having other people wear their skin, etc etc. In short, 'harem characters being controlled by a harem narrative,' and at this point it feels like a large part of their personal agency / individuality / realism has been sacrificed on this alter. Call me a curmudgeon, but Chika is by far acting the most realistically right now, and it strains belief that most of these girls would be so casual about Sensei fucking all of their friends.
[[[It is at this moment I make an aside to say: if you are Selebus and reading this, FUCK YOU!!! I TOLD YOU NOT TO READ THIS!!! FUCK YOU FUCK YOU FUCK YOU!!! CLOSE THE TAB! GO AWAY! SQUASH YOUR OBSESSION TO READ EVERYTHING ABOUT YOURSELF THAT EXISTS ON THE NET! THIS ISNT FOR YOU! REEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE]]]
One potential problem is that while I once struggled to parse the sanctity of Sensei's character, I now struggle to parse the sanctity of EVERY character. Are they themselves? Are they all being brainwashed? How many of them even 'exist' at all? Each time a comparison is drawn between Sensei and another character I wince as I add that to the evidence pile that they are a fragment of his personality, for instance. This is not to say I interpret the 'some guy is semi-metaphorically strapped to a chair in front of a computer imagining all of what happens as idealistic fiction' theory to be unquestionable, but rather that it is SO questionable that I have to keep questioning it, and the girls are really not doing any favors with their strained autonomy. For a LONG time I staved this sensation off due to 2021-era Selebus enthusiastically proclaiming that 'the girls had a lot of story to them, and he couldn't want to tell each,' but like, as these stories increasingly converge around Sensei's dick, I start to question whether that is truly strong evidence of their realness attribute being comfortably high. (Good Lord, the nightmare reality of Selebus being the guy in the chair, and each girl being a fragment of him (which is already true literally but hopefully not within the text), is not even fully deniable, since e.g. there is the fact Molly was based on his Irish ancestory).
So it is that like, even this built-up-to revelatory scene between Kirin and Sensei rings totally hollow to me. Not only have we been through it before, but there is zero romance when Kirin is clearly 'not looking at Sensei' and Sensei is clearly 'not looking at Kirin,' just like nobody is looking at anyone here. Is Kirin even real? Is Sensei even real? Is she acting with agency or because Sensei's magic musk overwhelms her puny girl brain? After she got pissed over Karin I never even questioned that over time she would get right back over it following some trivial prodding, and so it has happened, with a scene seeming to highlight her own confusion and difficulty grasping the situation - did she really get over it or is the harem narrative forcing her to? When I am questioning these foundational elements it's hard to really feel moved by her crying over him or him announcing his affection. As one may say - take out the foundation, and everything crumbles after. And of course, that may be the point. I don't mean to be too dramatic here. I'm not gnashing my teeth and proclaiming LiL to be totally dead to me or poorly written or whatever. Rather, an update I looked forward to a lot that ended up having exactly what I wanted ended up not speaking to me at all when I expected the opposite, and now I must contemplate this.
I do wonder if Selebus finds himself caught in the contradiction of the fakeness vs realism dynamic (altho as LiL itself proves, it is always a contradiction which creates the most compelling foundation for mythology). This is to say: as Sensei points out in this update, it's very plausible he could have raped Futaba on the first day without severely impacting their relationship. The other Senseis have stood as silent, implied reinforcements of LiL's existence as a porn game for the characters within it as well. And yet, there has been much richness to Futaba's character despite that, as well as with the other characters. It may be that what I am observing now is the moment where the fakeness attribute is shot so unbelievably damn high that the realness attribute ends up impoverished as a result. I think I remember Selebus saying on the discord in 2020 or so, early on, that harem stories are fucking retarded and can't be written competently. I must doff my hat and confirm that, as the Harem route becomes increasingly Harem, that it does feel like witnessing an increasingly retarded farce. At some point I genuinely believed (call me stupid) that some girls may end up not being in the harem after all; that, for example, perhaps Rin would stay with her girlfriends, or that he would settle things platonically with Yumi, or that maybe Touka would outmaneuver him. Now it's not even a question the full harem will be formed with any drama just proving to be roadbumps. And I'm not upset, just less engaged for now.
That said, I may enjoy the next update more; you never know! My favorite event in this update was, ironically given my comments above, Otoha moving in for a smooch with Sensei. The reason is not because I am invested a romance blooming between them or anything: it's because I really just did not expect that whatsoever. LiL stopped being exciting or surprising at the start of Chapter 4 for me, I think, and from then to now, that scene was the first (as I recall) that felt like I wanted to lean forward in my chair like, "wait, what's about to happen?" And so it did end on a high note. But I hope it keeps being surprising. Hopefully the 'show' Himawari has been building up to will be a big surprised in probably 3 months.

I don't really understand your point. I see Chapter 4 as a natural progression of things.
In chapter 1, Akira is some dude trying to pretend he's sensei and just corrupt some girls cause why not.

Chapter 2 is about him slowly realising he is that one dude, and that his past and who he is is really fucked.

Chapter 3 is when things come to a head: His name is Akira, he got fucked by Sekai's death, his one true love since then is Maya. He is also a puppet in the hands of many gods, he tries to control his life and yet it only makes it get further out of control until Maya dies because of him.

Chapter 4 is the breakdown. Maya is gone. He knows enough of the past to be put into a situation that he can't deal with it and yet the one person that dealt with it for him isn't here anymore. So he leaves school. He tries to depend on Ami but she turns insane, so he tries to focus on being a parent. But his mind becomes more and more deranged, so he relies on fighting against Pareidolia for control, until, surprise! Pareidolia is also gone. What now? Akira is unhinged. He's making passes at snowmen during parties and the girls don't even blink, that's how bad it's gotten.

Chapter 4 is uncomfortable imo, but that's because we're deep into the spiral, and he becomes even more passive. This update points that out rather well. Maybe if you try replaying it you'll notice how pitiful Akira becomes. It's not a mindless sex-bot going around and that's our game. It's a very sad vestige of a human being that is insane, and breaks down monologuing enough to make Kirin of all people start crying just hearing what he's saying about himself (I cried during the scene as well).

Now, imo, Akira needs to bounce back. I get that he was off for christmas (with the monks and all), but he needs to get on. posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
I agree to an extent, and also, this has not been questioned - but I got the sense that the meeting was about setting Tsukasa up with someone. There's no evidence of this during the update, it's just something that kept showing up in my head as the one thing with narrative significance to her being kept apart from causing issues (because it's hard sell out the demon of the family if she shows she's a demon).

But back to your point, I read that line from Tsubasa a little differently: "acting like this you will not last long in this family" means "you are at this moment part of this family, and we're still holding expectations for you". So in a very roundabout insane manner, Tsubasa was giving Tsukasa what she wants. Which is the opposite of what Touka says btw.

Because Touka goes in with "dude, I get that you're jealous of the attention because you're young, but you'll eventually find out that you're free because of me. You have all of the money and none of the responsabilities, go live your life".

Regarding Tsubasa in general though I've given up on her. Her motives are insane to me to a degree that I just can't understand. Her whole event was extremely offputting to me, as she capitalizes on Akira's trauma during a day he's constantly blacking out in the first place (if she wants to arrest him or have him sent to an asylum, fine, understandable. But to prey on someone that, let's be honest, is mentally challenged by this point is just disgusting). And then I just don't get her deal with encouraging a predator to have sex with her child, it's bordering on nonsense tbh.
Edit: Been struggling with lack of reactions at the moment, as per usual after an update.
Click to expand...
I decided to revisit a little bit of early Tsubasa events to remind myself of what's she's supposed to be all about. The bit about leaving a rock garden legacy to her two beautiful daughters from a good man stands out somewhat, but then we walked into the golden room:

Everbloom (Pride of the sinful sort)


--
And of course, our latest Christmas event.
--


DON'T TALK TO MONKS

--

I'm not sure what to make of this myself, other than that my gut has been telling me that ever since spring started, many characters seem to have had their priorities shifted in major and almost unnatural ways. Maybe this is just a convenient map to use for a pretty room but in my experience, authors tend not to forget the emotional or contextual significance of their own set pieces. With the subtly creepy snowmen with yellow snowflakes (?) and Yasu in center frame fulfilling her classic role in these compositions despite being disconnected from HOPE, it really seems deliberately setup to make the viewer feel ever so slightly uncomfortable and insults the stated significance of the room in the process. Almost like a small-scale version of the bastardization of the world itself throughout Chapter 4. It's like a satire of a satire. Are the girls themselves being made into pretty things with no real purpose? Was that always the case?

Anyway, maybe I'm giving too much credit here but one of the patterns we've been experiencing all spring is that both characters and players are seeing familiar things replaced with something cosmetically similar but WRONG. Between the implications of spring, the missing week and the timeline revelations, I'm beginning to think that there's some major influence instigating the behaviors we're seeing this chapter. It feels like the dark path would be preserving and continuing this open debauchery direction while other routes involve our cast gaining some form of agency over the world and it's resets and using that to escape the cycle in some way, thereby regaining agency over themselves they didn't realize they'd lost.

Not that I'm really focused on trying to predict the writing of an author with so much more experience than I. Just trying to make sense of the direction Chapter 4 is headed.

I'm not sure what to make of this myself, other than that my gut has been telling me that ever since spring started, many characters seem to have had their priorities shifted in major and almost unnatural ways. Maybe this is just a convenient map to use for a pretty room but in my experience, authors tend not to forget the emotional or contextual significance of their own set pieces. With the subtly creepy snowmen with yellow snowflakes (?) and Yasu in center frame fulfilling her classic role in these compositions despite being disconnected from HOPE, it really seems deliberately setup to make the viewer feel ever so slightly uncomfortable and insults the stated significance of the room in the process. Almost like a small-scale version of the bastardization of the world itself throughout Chapter 4. It's like a satire of a satire. Are the girls themselves being made into pretty things with no real purpose? Was that always the case?

Anyway, maybe I'm giving too much credit here but one of the patterns we've been experiencing all spring is that both characters and players are seeing familiar things replaced with something cosmetically similar but WRONG. Between the implications of spring, the missing week and the timeline revelations, I'm beginning to think that there's some major influence instigating the behaviors we're seeing this chapter. It feels like the dark path would be preserving and continuing this open debauchery direction while other routes involve our cast gaining some form of agency over the world and it's resets and using that to escape the cycle in some way, thereby regaining agency over themselves they didn't realize they'd lost.

Not that I'm really focused on trying to predict the writing of an author with so much more experience than I. Just trying to make sense of the direction Chapter 4 is headed.

It's...getting more difficult to give her the benefit of the doubt regarding how she handles Tsukasa. But as naive as it sounds, I want to believe that she genuinely loves Tsukasa, I want to believe that her reactions when learning firsthand about Tsukasa's loneliness in We Happy Few, and the subsequent pool time in To Lift This Aching Head were real. However, as a head Tsukioka, Tsubasa can only do so in very roundabout, nonsensically medieval ways because of her environment, because of her priority, and because of the fact that her mindset has already been shaped into a classic Tsukioka.

Among all the horrifying plays she does in this update, one line of hers stands out the most for me. "With an attitude like that, you'll never last in this family." This line isn't a response to Tsukasa being a whiney brat. No, this line is the response to Tsukasa verbalizing her worries of being a nuances to everyone as someone not old enough for attending middle school. Whether or not Tsubasa considers this an weakness or other qualities unfit as a Tsukioka, her response gives me a sense of real concern for Tsukasa. Moreover, it gives me the feeling that when it comes to Tsukasa's foreseeable future, there are only three viable options that don't spell misery: either Tsukasa fulfills her role as a backup and replaces Touka, or she leaves the family for good to avoid the fate of a backup that no longer has its use, or Tsubasa climbs to the absolute apex of the pyramid so that it empowers her to keep Tsukasa here with her just as her daughter against any screwed up traditions the Tsukiokas may or may not have been practicing on heirs that didn't end up on the throne.

Mostly importantly, with a status already so high up in the hierarchy, I don't see the need for Tsubasa to be this mindful around Tsukasa if Tsubasa really is done with being Tsukasa's mother and will only treat Tsukasa as just another asset. Any of this by no mean absolves her from being a horrible mother, but I am willing to believe that Tsubasa does see Tsukasa as her own daughter and have a plan for Tsukasa that isn't simply just giving her away to a groomer.

Is it a core belief of Chika changing for her to stop believing that love is monog- ahaha, I don't even have to finish this one.

Another interesting thing is how getting Ayane to accept the harem was once an excruciating character-defining scene centering around the list, but now she seemingly doesn't remember the list, but is still totally okay with it.

Of course, an excellent aspect of fiction is that characters are black boxes of infinite depth which can surprise and delight, so I profess zero mastery or total knowledge regarding their core beliefs, but this update (along with some prior) did seem to reach the point of core aspects of characters being altered/modified such that they are increasingly a bit unrecognizable. I may be totally off base though. 0.46 event triggers

There are 20 events in total. Most events (save two) are linked. The chain begins on a Friday. After Christmas is done with the main event "Post Nut Clarity", you have two other events:

19 - Tsukasa 2 (automatic on a sunday afternoon - I think you will need Tsukasa's route taken aka "tsukasacurious").
20 - Otoha 2 (visit her dorms, triggered for me on a weekday).

*How not to miss events: There are A LOT of flags being invoked, including one for Futaba which will fail a lot of events if not present. It happens during "The one with all the sextoys" and it needs Futaba Lust 40. The next one happens during Futaba's event, needing Molly's lust 10. The "amifingered" flag will change her conversation with Niki in the backstage. Most importantly however is a Himawari variation that needs Ayane affection over 3k. posts.content_html_raw:
Regarding everyone acting so chill about Akira fucking different people: I for one am not surprised in the slightest. Why? Because something is currently amiss; something different than what has happened before. We're even warned about it not once, but twice:



Mysterious Narrator - "Congratulations! You've made it through another Halloween!"
- "You must have a lot of questions, huh?"
- "Well, stop!"
- "Stop having them."
- "Just play the fucking game, Akira. PLAY THE GAME."
- "Go back to normal and PLAY THE GOD DAMN GAME."
- "Have sex! Spread your seed! Make snowmen! Sniff the flowers! Go to the beach! GO TO THE BEACH!"
- "Go swimming -- and ignore the inconvenient truth that sometimes, when people are acting normal?..."
- "They are filthy"
- "fucking"
- "liars."

Event name: "What We'll See When We Get There" (Chapter 4 Main Event)

Note how I bolded and underlined one line in particular up above: 'GO TO THE BEACH!' Spoken in all caps. Perhaps the narrator trying to indirectly tell us something?

Now what could have happened at the Beach that was weird and no one else remembers?...


As far as the second hint we receive, it was actually in the latest update:


Sensei Narrator - "We haven't spoken much since Halloween, have we?"
- "I've had a lot of time to think since then."
- "Well, maybe not a lot. But almost two months' worth. And that's more than enough for me to tell you this."
- "Something is wrong here."
- "I haven't figured out what yet. And I'm sure I'm not going to while I'm preoccupied by the vagina of a celebrity, but I know that something has changed."
- "No one else thinks so, though."
- "Not even Ayane -- which makes me worry that it's potentially impacted her in some way."
- "It just always feels like something is missing. And with the circumstances surrounding our last trip to the rooftop being omitted from all of our memories, we're drawing blanks trying to retrace our steps."

Event name: "Aunt Niki (A Hundred Christmases)" (Chapter 4 Main Event)

So in short: something is very wrong with the residents of Terminal 23 right now. It started at the last Beach Trip and has become more apparent after the latest Reset. It's not too far fetched to think that, along with the Reset, the girls' behaviors have simply been altered, no?

Or better yet, what if we're still trapped in some weird alternate reality right now that mimics the one we've known and the key to breaking out of it is at the beach (AKA the edge of the world)?

Could be something to keep in mind.

posts.content_html_raw:
My only real concern with Yuki is that she has said that basically, she can’t fully control how things will go. She’s talked about the inevitability of relapse, and while it may be broadly true given the intense nature of addiction, for her to be so willing to admit to it makes me wonder about her convictions.

I’m not saying that being realistic is bad, and addiction is unlike anything else in the world, but for me, if I acknowledge the potential for failure, I’ve already doomed myself to it. It’s the disappointment I have in myself when I fall that keeps me striving to not repeat my mistakes.

It’s a heavy topic, and Yuki is a great exploration of it. But personally, I’m concerned her character is still setting herself up to fail, even if she is trying in some regard to be better. But those nuances to complicated topics make her a wonderful character to explore.

Moonflare said:
Seeing with your eyes closed is first talked about by Ami, that claims she has something called "nightvision", which allows her to know things by discarding her vision. The same nightvision is then talked about by other characters, like Yasu.

HOPE wants Akira's eyes, by the time of the fourth reset - and his followers would "blind" themselves to allow him to see through them (you can see this during Yasu's ritual at the church, and, conceivably, through the rabbits with blindfolds).

IF nightvision equates to sacrificing vision for HOPE is unknown. Neither Wires nor Pareidolia seem to have a connection with either.
Click to expand...
I think seeing with your eyes closed comes directly from Pareidolia. I've written some scattered ideas about this before, but this seems like a good opportunity to put things in one place.
The first time the phrase is used is by Tsubasa the narrator on the first beach trip.
There's three different connections to Pareidolia here. First, the text in the background image is full sentences but without capitalization. Second, Pareidolia is described as a voice in the back of Sensei's mind.
"Slumber Party"

"Mysterious Abundance of Chickens" after SeKaori briefly wakes up, Sensei collapses, and Pareidolia talks to him.

"Metal in Microwaves"
Third, this particular smiley face is regularly used for Pareidolia.
Earlier on the beach ("Prayer Position"), we're shown the trinity tree with it's three parts: the roots (Wires), branches (where HOPE's smile is), and the leaves (Pareidolia - where this smile is).

74 72 69 6e 69 74 79 = trinity

It's also used for Parry consistently in later events. For example, repeated flashes in "Lavender's Green", and when (presumably) Big P is talking in "The Scary Room" and "Empty Eyes".

The phrase is used by Makoto in "Bluejay" just before she kills herself. This is less obviously tied to any particular god, but the event does start with a flash of the same smiley.

...
Most recently, it was used by Sekai in "Kyoto". All signs indicate Pareidolia was in Sekai's mind while she was alive (like most/all other Arakawas) and now Ghost Sekai and Pareidolia are working closely together.

In contrast, HOPE wants Sensei to open his eyes. Yasu keeps telling him this throughout Chapter 2.
"The Hole that Swallowed Everything"

"Transference"

"Armor of Older Gods"
Earlier, when they're in Pareidolia's domain, HOPE says that he's the only one who can help Sensei open his eyes.

Love hotel on paper seems like the most "romantic" place to lose your virginity at. Guess it's kind of odd that Kirin would be the one to lose it there but whatever. But there's no nostalgia so the romance is still lacking in a way... I dunno, I'm no expert on these things.

As much as I enjoy seeing Niki get a little pissed, I don't think forcing her to have breakfast at a place she already doesn't like is a good idea.

Iirc, Maya didn't say anything that could make it seem like the mc is her boyfriend. If anything she just really showed that she hated Noriko and I got the impression Maya is the victim of Noriko's stalking. SO HOW THE FUCK did people come to the conclusion the mc and Maya somehow has a secret relationship!? Man, this is the kind of irrational mental behavior that really ticks me off.
Had to go back and confirm this. In between insults and demand, Maya did tell Sensei to stay out of it which I guess can be interpreted wrongly as a love rivalry between Maya and Noriko, but once again, how the fuck did you get to that conclusion?

Maya: "I'm cold and blunt. A kuudere with slowly dissipating "cool" and "dere" buried somewhere so far underground that you'll likely never find it."
I'm struggling to figure out which form of "cool" she means. Cool like in you are in awe of how cool they are, sort of like what the girls see in the mc, or if she means cool as in containing those emotions. If in the former case then she appears emotionless but people see her more as a freak than someone worth admiring and she lacks the caring part so she's basically just an outcast in every sense. In the latter case she's slowly losing the "kuu" in kuudere but she still doesn't care in this case. Given some of her outbursts with the scarf and the appearance of Noriko with the numerous instances of anger, disgust, few instances of blushing and so on, I'm starting to think it's actually the latter in this case. But I feel like she already is the former.

In other news, I just found out I want to see Maya get kabedon'd. Lovely.

Huh... So the previous versions of the students wouldn't have accepted the idea of him not teaching, but these once were rewritten to just magically accept it and not report him. Like this set of girls are literally made for him.
Uh oh. That means my theory that the girls can continue learning and getting wiser definitely don't apply if old information is erased when a new human occupy his brain.
I don't know when that came about but I guess if you had rejected Ami way back, Maya probably would have said something different here regarding figuring out that they fucked.
Him talking to the other girls about Maya and his secret relationship is probably not something I will get to see. That would be a lot of girls to ask and tell after all.

I guess the only thing Maya fears that he can easily use on her is reminding her he can just go see Noriko instead. He can weaponize this against her... the question is what the limits to it's effect is. I can imagine it stops at something sexual... for now.

This Maya event, feels like something is about to happen, that she's going to reveal something the player will react to, but like there's a barrier preventing her from saying it.
Some disturbing baby bird story followed by a crying distressed Maya, hmm.
Uhh, and that's a picture of Maya, likely from a very long time ago?
Okay, maybe it doesn't end at something sexual... it's just that the mc might not be comfortable with that because Maya doesn't actually want it. Bah... too little info.
"It's... not even hard? But... by now it... would always..." Hmmmmmmm...
Guessing they used to be lovers. Somehow Noriko is involved and Maya is hurting severely by whatever happened like a curse. Either way it's starting to feel like Maya is the victim somehow.

It's times like these that make me wish I had discovered this game like 6 years later where I predict it will probably be finished, probably. Because I just know I'm not gonna get all the answers up to the current version. Of course if the game WAS finished, then I still have a long time to go and I kinda need some breaks from the game every now and then, but never enough to forget, which I risk doing in the 1-2 months it takes the game to update.

If this really is as bad as I think, Maya is probably gonna end up at the top of the tierlist by the end. Suffering somehow has a tendency of making me like a character more and it seems like Maya has had a fair share of suffering.

The very next Maya event and she's suddenly more welcoming... or concerned.

The things I never would have expected Maya saying so soon into the story... "You said all sorts of strange things as I was frantically trying to get you aroused"
Something I still don't understand is why she would go out of her way to have sex if it means he won't disappear again. For someone who doesn't like this timeline very much, she... I dunno. I can only chalk it up to what she said earlier about him being different this time around, and maybe how different everything else is made it seem like a huge waste to undo all of that. I can't imagine a person who doesn't like change who have gone through god knows how many cycles are suddenly gonna want to get rid of the change when it happens. It sounds counterintuitive but too much of a good thing is bad and if you can predict everything that will happen, you will get bored of the way things are.

WTF DOES THAT MEAN?
Maya: "If I could tell you more, I would."
Sensei: "Really?"
Maya: "Really."
Sensei: "Even though I'm the most disgusting person in the world?"
Maya: "Right."
Proceeds to have one if not the most out of place facial reaction I've ever seen. A regular wide smile, blush, regular wide eyes with that tear stuck in both eyes.
The event is called "Stop looking for answers". It looked like she was laughing, in distress, embarrassed, on the verge of crying, psychopathic-ish, all at the same time and I can't figure out which it is. I expected her usual stoic expression but I got a deranged one instead. I don't know about you but that's just not normal. It seems like there's deeper meaning but the text doesn't imply there is, or at least it doesn't feel like it.

"I don't know what I want. What I want is you, Yumi" The first part of that message was crossed out followed by "What? I didn't-" Kinda implying whatever force is driving him to be more forceful with Yumi spoke for him. I feel like what Maya said about him being near the middle of the middle where his more likely to have these blackouts or whatever should be enough reason for him to not be near Yumi as much.
Guess I shouldn't be surprised by an event named "Abyss" that conveniently needs to be completed before "Little miracles" to get an alteration to Yumi's events. Think last time this happened was between Chika and Rin.
Are we talking with Tsuneyo's shirt now or what?

Is it possible that every other loop has resulted in Yumi being sent to detention and not treated like a friend or someone he wants to fuck and that all these blackouts are happening because his not following the pattern/cycle/thing that Maya talks about?

Holy fuck... Yumi just casually described herself on accident. Who would want to be with him? "Would have to be a real screw up. Equally as douchey. Zero work ethic. A whole bunch of shit"

Saying no to going out with Chika for that hot spring 4 part event thing she had tickets for places you back in the phone menu, as if autovn didn't expect you to pick that option.
I would say yukata's are completely gender neutral. You don't lose manliness nor do you loss your femineity. I wish a housecoat all the time when I'm home which is also gender neutral so I bet that's why.

I guess Tsubasa likes his sense of humor. Maybe she's starved for that stuff and that's how they will get along.

Wow indeed. They are indeed massive...

bobloblawwwwwww said:
So, how do you use URM to guide you through the game? This is the first time I've played a brand new update and I'm not sure what to do to get things rolling.
Click to expand...
Guide mod gives hints about what to do. it's only updated when public versions of LiL are released.

URM's biggest feature for LiL is letting you know when there's branches in the story logic. One of the biggest ones talked about this update is whether you've seen failsafe (which we're assuming means you chose to groom Tsukasa. The logic is wrong currently, might be fixed next update). There's several points in the dialogue where the top left says something like "choices available", you can click them and find out through the logic provided what dialogue you are about to get, and sometimes you can pick something you haven't earned just to see the dialogue (Though I'd roll back to before the choice when you're done reading it. Committing to dialogue you didn't earn will break things irreparably)

It also lets you find variables and event names, and allows you to change variables or jump (or view in a replay) events that the game says you aren't allowed to see yet. You can also watch certain variables to have them appear in a tab to watch them change in real time, though this is rarely useful in LiL.

I was about to make a kind of a masterful troll post to the tune of like

"Yeah, I'm kinda fucked up. I hear phantom sounds and talk to inanimate objects in my room. I beat someone up in daycare, too. Using my middle finger on the mousewheel is nothing to me."

Then it struck me that Selebus based Yumi beating someone up in daycare on a real event from his life. Nothing new there; that was an intuition I had a while ago, as well as the obligatory connections. But what's new is the potential humor value. What better troll and grand finale would it be for Selebus to reveal that every single heroine is actually himself? Like, I say this on two levels. First is the meta revelation that every author goes through that all characters are fragments of themselves. A famous quip is that you can't write a character smarter than yourself (though you can give the impression you have (see: Nodoka)), and on top of that, the process of modeling characters in your mind often ends up in a kind of ghost chorus of said characters taking on tulpa-like lives of their own in your mind. Writers talk about how characters 'wont shut up' until a scene is written. Basic stuff - I've touched on it before and it's something we all subconsciously accept. But it just so happens that this aligns incredibly well with the SECOND level, which is the narrative of Lessons in Love being self-insert fiction. What do we know? We know that the world was made for someone, we know that perception is dubious, we know that it's a 'game,' we know the purpose is to be happy, we know Sensei is being seemingly controlled by unknown force(s), we know we players were given Options so that we can Communicate with the Narrator and interface with the game, we know there are explicit/obvious hints of Sensei/others being American rather than Japanese... all of this has led me to think for some time that Selebus (most likely Pareidolia (and therefore the whole trinity) for obvious reasons) has been acting as that external force on Sensei and pushing himself into Sensei as the Game Developer. It's no surprise that Sensei would often be suffering the ailments Selebus complains about 1:1 (and after Selebus already wrote an explicit self-insert with Yuu in NiB who goes through the same shit again). Again, basic stuff. The problem I have had is where the students of LiL fit into this: are they really Sensei's students? Did they fall into the well with him? Are they unerring evidence of an external reality? How many of them are Subahibi ghosts? And so on.

(Selebus's refusal to acknowledge Himawari is as profound as people imagine it to be; I imagine it means she is a force outside of the Game Developer / Writer's awareness. I don't really want to speculate on this too much, though, since it gets out of the meta of the game to speculate on an external existence Selebus would let work on the game. I only ever speak of Lessons in Love Selebus, never of any real life being. And it may be nonsense anyway.)

The comedy intuition, which I just had, and which to share enthusiastically, is the moment where all of this could theoretically coalesce into the most hilarious narrative twist of all time. Conceive of a being of pure white. Then conceive of Molly popping out of existence and the White being turning more green. Conceive of Yumi popping out of existence and the Greenish-white thing turning more aggressive. Imagine Ayane popping out of existence and the thing suddenly having more of a moral backbone or something. Imagine Karin popping out of existence and the thing's thighs get thicker. And then, when EVERY SINGLE heroine has popped out of existence... the being turns into Selebus. And Selebus looks at the screen like "Thank you for putting me back together." Or something.

Basically. The absolute funniest interpretation I can think of, and I apologize for taking so long to set up the scene here, is the twist that every single heroine is actually Selebus. (Except Maya, who is Selebus's cat or something.*). And then like, imagine the seething. All the people who have busted loads to Sana were actually busting loads to Selebus in disguise. Everyone who wore a like Yumi avatar while dunking on Selebus were unwittingly singing his praises. Man, imagine. This is completely schizo but it's so funny I have to convey it.

*The only reason I'm hesitant about the 'heroine(s) are actually cats' theory is that I don't think Selebus wants to fuck his cats even if they are in anime girl form. However, it is a common anime trope for cats to take human shape and, as they say, to flock to their master when they are miserable to cheer them up. Perhaps Sensei is thinking 'a cat is fine too' at this point but even for LiL that would be extremely bizarre. I'm kind of convincing myself as I type this though... Sensei is probably fucking a desk or that fleshlight instead of the cat anyway.

(P.S.: All too easily forgotten is that LiL starts with a suicide. It would naturally follow from that that someone would be tied into bed/chair in a hospital room listening to the ticking of a clock. The question for me is whether that person, Sensei, is a wholly independent being, or if that person is an abstraction of Selebus. Is that where Sensei is being forced to observe this, or is that where Selebus is writing this? Whatever LiL is, it must follow from suicide.)
