When I first started playing Lessons in Love, I found it enrapturing to theorycraft about the three gods and Sensei's background and so on. There was just the right mix of mystery and intrigue, combined with suitably rich-feeling text, that made it feel incredibly rewarding. I am proud to say that in my day I have made no less than three insight-driven predictions that successfully foretold a future plot development or character reveal years before anyone else did, which is quite an accomplishment with so many great minds competing in the arena of this game. I imagine in these moments I felt a euphoria as great as Moonflare would feel if an update revealed Himawari's name to be Ami.

However, over time, this line of thinking has completely lost its luster to me. I find myself skimming theory posts on f95 with only minimal interest, and when my associates excitedly begin discussing the plot implications of such-and-such god making such-and-such statement in the latest update, the greatest response I can muster is a shrug and a nod.

In short, in the great words of Ahab from the previous great American novel Moby Dick:

“Hark ye yet again—the little lower layer. All visible objects, man, are but as pasteboard masks. But in each event—in the living act, the undoubted deed—there, some unknown but still reasoning thing puts forth the mouldings of its features from behind the unreasoning mask. If man will strike, strike through the mask! How can the prisoner reach outside except by thrusting through the wall? To me, the white whale is that wall, shoved near to me. Sometimes I think there’s naught beyond. But ’tis enough. He tasks me; he heaps me; I see in him outrageous strength, with an inscrutable malice sinewing it. That inscrutable thing is chiefly what I hate; and be the white whale agent, or be the white whale principal, I will wreak that hate upon him. Talk not to me of blasphemy, man; I’d strike the sun if it insulted me. For could the sun do that, then could I do the other; since there is ever a sort of fair play herein, jealousy presiding over all creations. But not my master, man, is even that fair play. Who’s over me? Truth hath no confines. Take off thine eye! more intolerable than fiends’ glarings is a doltish stare!”
Click to expand...
The 'little lower layer' of visible objects has just ceased to compel or interest me whatsoever. This has, I think, only little to do with myself, and more with a purposeful transition in the presentation of the game; while Chapter 1 was a dark, brooding mystery with a plethora of shocking happy events, as of late happy events are sparing in number - often lucid in nature - while we have characters openly speaking about the abstract structure of the narrative. How in this environment am I supposed to give a single flying shit about narrative consistency and plot reveals?

Thus I find my fickle interest much more drawn to the meta-layer. I feel convinced down to my bones that there is One Singular Truth that busts this game wide open: one key insight, key concept, key foundation from which everything else was founded. There is one single box from which all the madness spews forth, and if I can find it, then everything will click into place. If I can strike through the pasteboard masks of these animal girls there will be some beating heart pumping sickly blood throughout the entire game. THAT is what catches my interest and what I find myself thinking about - for now.

And what more hilarious SINGLE TRUTH could there be then a megalomaniac so haughty that he designs a harem of himself? One who when conceiving brides plucks history and idiosyncrasies from himself? One who cackles as he woos the hearts of millions with his own mirror images? Every time someone has said 'go fuck yourself' - that he has!!!!!!

Maybe. That's what I find funny and what I find value in exploring right now, anyway.

(p.s. MASK OFF: quoting moby dick is a joke. It's a reference to the past. I hope to increase the quality of my post with running gags and callbacks which build up to a mythos we can all enjoy exploring ourselves.)

To me, spoilers are not bad if you don't plan on going through the story in question. If you are planning to you have to ask the question "am I/they interested only in the action or the story or both?" in two out of the three cases, spoilers are bad, but if they are only interested in the action and experience and not the audio and dialogue then spoilers are okay. Spoilers are obviously things that have not happened yet for the person. You can get into specifics like how much of a spoiler something is, like what I did at the start. If I ask if the game has jumpscares that's more a gameplay or action thing imo. If I ask if any characters will die then I think that's technically a story thing but if they explicitly say they want to know, you can just say yes but not elaborate on who. General rule of thumb tho, just DON'T speak about things that haven't happened yet and be vague if someone asks for it, identify a rhetorical question and non rhetorical. If you are not sure what is rhetorical, you can just be even more vague or just don't comment at all.
Another note, sometimes people can change their mind and suddenly get invested in the story. This can happen in these games too. Someone comes along only interested in the sex scenes but fall for the story. I believe I cared about spoilers at the start but that became even stronger as I progressed.

To me, spoilers are not bad if you don't plan on going through the story in question. If you are planning to you have to ask the question "am I/they interested only in the action or the story or both?" in two out of the three cases, spoilers are bad, but if they are only interested in the action and experience and not the audio and dialogue then spoilers are okay. Spoilers are obviously things that have not happened yet for the person. You can get into specifics like how much of a spoiler something is, like what I did at the start. If I ask if the game has jumpscares that's more a gameplay or action thing imo. If I ask if any characters will die then I think that's technically a story thing but if they explicitly say they want to know, you can just say yes but not elaborate on who. General rule of thumb tho, just DON'T speak about things that haven't happened yet and be vague if someone asks for it, identify a rhetorical question and non rhetorical. If you are not sure what is rhetorical, you can just be even more vague or just don't comment at all.
Another note, sometimes people can change their mind and suddenly get invested in the story. This can happen in these games too. Someone comes along only interested in the sex scenes but fall for the story. I believe I cared about spoilers at the start but that became even stronger as I progressed.

posts.content_html_raw:
Yggdrasil_Frahma said:
When I first started playing Lessons in Love, I found it enrapturing to theorycraft about the three gods and Sensei's background and so on. There was just the right mix of mystery and intrigue, combined with suitably rich-feeling text, that made it feel incredibly rewarding. I am proud to say that in my day I have made no less than three insight-driven predictions that successfully foretold a future plot development or character reveal years before anyone else did, which is quite an accomplishment with so many great minds competing in the arena of this game. I imagine in these moments I felt a euphoria as great as Moonflare would feel if an update revealed Himawari's name to be Ami.

However, over time, this line of thinking has completely lost its luster to me. I find myself skimming theory posts on f95 with only minimal interest, and when my associates excitedly begin discussing the plot implications of such-and-such god making such-and-such statement in the latest update, the greatest response I can muster is a shrug and a nod.

In short, in the great words of Ahab from the previous great American novel Moby Dick:



The 'little lower layer' of visible objects has just ceased to compel or interest me whatsoever. This has, I think, only little to do with myself, and more with a purposeful transition in the presentation of the game; while Chapter 1 was a dark, brooding mystery with a plethora of shocking happy events, as of late happy events are sparing in number - often lucid in nature - while we have characters openly speaking about the abstract structure of the narrative. How in this environment am I supposed to give a single flying shit about narrative consistency and plot reveals?

Thus I find my fickle interest much more drawn to the meta-layer. I feel convinced down to my bones that there is One Singular Truth that busts this game wide open: one key insight, key concept, key foundation from which everything else was founded. There is one single box from which all the madness spews forth, and if I can find it, then everything will click into place. If I can strike through the pasteboard masks of these animal girls there will be some beating heart pumping sickly blood throughout the entire game. THAT is what catches my interest and what I find myself thinking about - for now.

And what more hilarious SINGLE TRUTH could there be then a megalomaniac so haughty that he designs a harem of himself? One who when conceiving brides plucks history and idiosyncrasies from himself? One who cackles as he woos the hearts of millions with his own mirror images? Every time someone has said 'go fuck yourself' - that he has!!!!!!

Maybe. That's what I find funny and what I find value in exploring right now, anyway.

(p.s. MASK OFF: quoting moby dick is a joke. It's a reference to the past. I hope to increase the quality of my post with running gags and callbacks which build up to a mythos we can all enjoy exploring ourselves.)

This is surprisingly intimate for being a fully clothed sneak "sex" scene in an awkward position while Makoto is right there. Can't blame her for suddenly becoming overwhelmed by emotion.

Now even Miku is questioning this time anomaly. And here I thought it was suppose to be stable... Clearly not.
What horrible timing. They are having a moment and then BANG, the upstairs neighbours dropping something heavy. Gotta be real fucking awkward having to deal with a distressed Miku in the middle of a sexual moment.
Does Io and Uta even know about Miku's trauma? If they don't, then they should really be the first to be made aware of it to avoid making too much noise. At least Io should be made aware of it since she builds things.
Why the fuck would Makoto snap like that when the reaction Miku is having is one she has with noise? She's not thinking rationally here at all. I hate misunderstandings, but it's not like his innocent. But no seriously wtf? She's spent month(years) seeing Miku react like that so she should automatically know she's having a noise induced trauma attack. Fuck dude... Can't even be pissed off correctly because of how they ended up in that position to begin with.
And then a couple messages later and there is Mikoto's apology... GREAT! No I am pissed now I have decided, fuck that logic! She clearly isn't very good at taking care of Miku if her first instinct is to missunderstand the situation that she should already know how to handle. I could have done without this event turning out like this, fucking erase that part of the event and pretend he just abruptly decided to leave, much fucking easier.
I don't get it, why do I hate misunderstandings so much!? Why do they piss me off!?
It was like Nodoka was looking through your soul just now. Cornering us and asking all these questions about what we want...
Out of all the things that could make Otoha blush, it was finding out his "returning home to Ami" and "She's my niece".
Wait a minute... I should probably stop worrying if Makoto gets suspicious of Chika. His pretty much already confirmed there are more.

I feel like it's important to recognize here that Tsubasa is consciously aware that he had sex with one of his students and she is willingly signing away her daughter to his class knowing this. I don't think I can convince myself to interpret this any different than "She is okay with him having sex with her daughter".

Yggdrasil_Frahma said:
I was about to make a kind of a masterful troll post to the tune of like

"Yeah, I'm kinda fucked up. I hear phantom sounds and talk to inanimate objects in my room. I beat someone up in daycare, too. Using my middle finger on the mousewheel is nothing to me."

Then it struck me that Selebus based Yumi beating someone up in daycare on a real event from his life. Nothing new there; that was an intuition I had a while ago, as well as the obligatory connections. But what's new is the potential humor value. What better troll and grand finale would it be for Selebus to reveal that every single heroine is actually himself? Like, I say this on two levels. First is the meta revelation that every author goes through that all characters are fragments of themselves. A famous quip is that you can't write a character smarter than yourself (though you can give the impression you have (see: Nodoka)), and on top of that, the process of modeling characters in your mind often ends up in a kind of ghost chorus of said characters taking on tulpa-like lives of their own in your mind. Writers talk about how characters 'wont shut up' until a scene is written. Basic stuff - I've touched on it before and it's something we all subconsciously accept. But it just so happens that this aligns incredibly well with the SECOND level, which is the narrative of Lessons in Love being self-insert fiction. What do we know? We know that the world was made for someone, we know that perception is dubious, we know that it's a 'game,' we know the purpose is to be happy, we know Sensei is being seemingly controlled by unknown force(s), we know we players were given Options so that we can Communicate with the Narrator and interface with the game, we know there are explicit/obvious hints of Sensei/others being American rather than Japanese... all of this has led me to think for some time that Selebus (most likely Pareidolia (and therefore the whole trinity) for obvious reasons) has been acting as that external force on Sensei and pushing himself into Sensei as the Game Developer. It's no surprise that Sensei would often be suffering the ailments Selebus complains about 1:1 (and after Selebus already wrote an explicit self-insert with Yuu in NiB who goes through the same shit again). Again, basic stuff. The problem I have had is where the students of LiL fit into this: are they really Sensei's students? Did they fall into the well with him? Are they unerring evidence of an external reality? How many of them are Subahibi ghosts? And so on.

(Selebus's refusal to acknowledge Himawari is as profound as people imagine it to be; I imagine it means she is a force outside of the Game Developer / Writer's awareness. I don't really want to speculate on this too much, though, since it gets out of the meta of the game to speculate on an external existence Selebus would let work on the game. I only ever speak of Lessons in Love Selebus, never of any real life being. And it may be nonsense anyway.)

The comedy intuition, which I just had, and which to share enthusiastically, is the moment where all of this could theoretically coalesce into the most hilarious narrative twist of all time. Conceive of a being of pure white. Then conceive of Molly popping out of existence and the White being turning more green. Conceive of Yumi popping out of existence and the Greenish-white thing turning more aggressive. Imagine Ayane popping out of existence and the thing suddenly having more of a moral backbone or something. Imagine Karin popping out of existence and the thing's thighs get thicker. And then, when EVERY SINGLE heroine has popped out of existence... the being turns into Selebus. And Selebus looks at the screen like "Thank you for putting me back together." Or something.

Basically. The absolute funniest interpretation I can think of, and I apologize for taking so long to set up the scene here, is the twist that every single heroine is actually Selebus. (Except Maya, who is Selebus's cat or something.*). And then like, imagine the seething. All the people who have busted loads to Sana were actually busting loads to Selebus in disguise. Everyone who wore a like Yumi avatar while dunking on Selebus were unwittingly singing his praises. Man, imagine. This is completely schizo but it's so funny I have to convey it.

Yggdrasil_Frahma said:
I was about to make a kind of a masterful troll post to the tune of like
"Yeah, I'm kinda fucked up. I hear phantom sounds and talk to inanimate objects in my room. I beat someone up in daycare, too. Using my middle finger on the mousewheel is nothing to me."
Then it struck me that Selebus based Yumi beating someone up in daycare on a real event from his life. Nothing new there; that was an intuition I had a while ago, as well as the obligatory connections. But what's new is the potential humor value. What better troll and grand finale would it be for Selebus to reveal that every single heroine is actually himself? Like, I say this on two levels. First is the meta revelation that every author goes through that all characters are fragments of themselves. A famous quip is that you can't write a character smarter than yourself (though you can give the impression you have (see: Nodoka)), and on top of that, the process of modeling characters in your mind often ends up in a kind of ghost chorus of said characters taking on tulpa-like lives of their own in your mind. Writers talk about how characters 'wont shut up' until a scene is written. Basic stuff - I've touched on it before and it's something we all subconsciously accept. But it just so happens that this aligns incredibly well with the SECOND level, which is the narrative of Lessons in Love being self-insert fiction. What do we know? We know that the world was made for someone, we know that perception is dubious, we know that it's a 'game,' we know the purpose is to be happy, we know Sensei is being seemingly controlled by unknown force(s), we know we players were given Options so that we can Communicate with the Narrator and interface with the game, we know there are explicit/obvious hints of Sensei/others being American rather than Japanese... all of this has led me to think for some time that Selebus (most likely Pareidolia (and therefore the whole trinity) for obvious reasons) has been acting as that external force on Sensei and pushing himself into Sensei as the Game Developer. It's no surprise that Sensei would often be suffering the ailments Selebus complains about 1:1 (and after Selebus already wrote an explicit self-insert with Yuu in NiB who goes through the same shit again). Again, basic stuff. The problem I have had is where the students of LiL fit into this: are they really Sensei's students? Did they fall into the well with him? Are they unerring evidence of an external reality? How many of them are Subahibi ghosts? And so on.
(Selebus's refusal to acknowledge Himawari is as profound as people imagine it to be; I imagine it means she is a force outside of the Game Developer / Writer's awareness. I don't really want to speculate on this too much, though, since it gets out of the meta of the game to speculate on an external existence Selebus would let work on the game. I only ever speak of Lessons in Love Selebus, never of any real life being. And it may be nonsense anyway.)

aramaug said:
The context of the conversation is that Tsuneyo is trying to remember what happened during the fifth reset. The initial questions are about the slumber party, and then the rest are about whatever supernatural experience she had after leaving the party. Sensei underwent a trial created by Pareidolia ("Untitled") and at least some of his companions also had trials, so it's plausible these questions come from Tsuneyo's own Pareidolia trial.

Also, immediately after the passage you quoted, we're shown red eye SeKaori arrive at the ramen shop.
And then the next event in the ramen shop, Wires claws his way out which causes Pareidolia to panic and quite literally piss himself.
I think Sekai/Pareidolia were taking advantage of Wires's absence to do something naughty with the ramen shop and/or Tsuneyo.

I'm not saying this is evidence for a Pareidolia connection, but it's certainly not inconsistent with one.
Click to expand...
If I understand correctly, you are proposing that since Tsuneyo got weird after almost poking her nose into a reset set up by Pareidolia, what gibberish Tsuneyo said afterward was actually her own part of the trial. Hence, the "seeing with your eyes closed" she brought up would have to come directly from Pareidolia.
(I'll ignore the Sekaori part and Wires clawing his way out part as they provide nothing to the context above. Unless you can articulate on how they can prove/disprove anything, they remain something that did happen but were unrelated)

First is that we don't know if those unsettling questions really come from Tsuneyo's personal reset5 or if personal trial really is a thing even. Girls that haven't become a RAS member can barely recall events immediately before a reset with zero discrepancy, let alone remembering something during a reset. The way I see it, it's closer to Tsuneyo trying to dig up sensitive information but being stopped supernaturally. This absolves the necessary involvement of Pareidolia in the matter, as things go from "Tsuneyo reciting her trial questions prepared by Pareidolia" to "Tsuneyo being halted by a certain divine power".

I am not saying my interpretation is more correct and I am not saying that the aforementioned certain divine power cannot be Pareidolia (though I will say that it's very unlikely to be Pareidolia considering its performance in TH15 15NT ME; the third god clearly has little to no power here in Tojo Ramen). The point is, the necessary bridge that connects "seeing with your eyes closed" and Pareidolia is not the only option on the table and is far from being the most possible one either. I personally get fixated on this type of thing frequently because most of the time we only have moon logic or false causality to back ourselves up whenever we claim A is connected to B, all because this fucking game won't give any clear hint. The least I'd do is to make sure that what is proposed is either the only possibility or the most possible option by a significant margin, and I don't see that being the case here.

Second is that, are we 100% sure that reset5 is hosted by Pareidolia? Did I overlook something? Is it because of Sekai hiding on the roof right before reset5 ended? (which, by the by, is something I also don't understand. How does this Pareidolia-Sekai connection come to be?)
To me Untitled reeks of HOPE. We have: youdidit, amiokay, we have that warning of "taking something that does not belong to you before the summer end". All of these are heavily associated with HOPE, not just in wishful symbolism but in actual context. One really needs to really get around these before certifying Pareidolia's presumed presence in Untitled.

TLDR is that I think your argument doesn't really bring "seeing with your eyes closed" and Pareidolia any closer and makes the phrase become a saying exclusive to the third god, which is all I am on about. I don't think it is impossible for a previous "seeing with your eyes closed" and Pareidolia to coincide, but that never guarantees "as soon as we see this phrase, it means Pareidolia is in the play".

daagagsdgd said:
Any character in fiction (or literature in general) would inevitably bear resemblance to its own author due to aesthetic contextualization. Just think about how drama started from mimesis of rituals. Though the artificiality and self-insertness, which were intendedly and tirelessly emphasised throughout LiL, did separate LiL from other non-Japanese VNs. All of intense overflow of self-consciousness and mockery constantly reminds me of Nabokov who in an interview, seemed to be spitefully and consciously polemical against Bakhtin's famous theory on polyphonic nature of Dostoevsky's novels, said that idea that "characters getting out of hand is nothing but a trite little whimsy" and his characters under disposal are "galley slaves". It wouldn't surprise me even a bit if those words came from mouth of Selebus.
Click to expand...
I think the main thing which may differentiate our analysis is that I perceive an immense love from Selebus for his characters. Although they go through horrible things, that is because he is under the belief that people need to go through horrible things to grow. A very classic thesis:antithesis situation where the thesis is strengthened by the antithesis. Furthermore, the dev commentary shows that Selebus relates to Rin's depression, and Futaba's lack of self-worth; it is unlikely to me he would be disparaging them as galley slaves when he is using them to tell his own story indirectly. It's for this reason I would also expect the love for characters to be a representation of self-love, and this self-love could crystalize in a certain wholeness of being coming about.

(Note: A very fascinating bit of psychology is that self-hate is closely related to self-love. Often those who proclaim to hate themselves, in fact, love themselves more than anything; even someone utterly convinced they hate themselves may in fact be total narcissists. Not to lobby that accusation at Selebus, just it's something to keep in mind; irony is, after all, the song of a prisoner who has come to love their cage, and when trapped in a prison it's hard not to develop intense affection for all its nuances.)

Honestly, re:Lolita, I seem to recall Selebus saying he hates reading books and hasn't read a book in like 10 years (due no doubt to his aphantasia), so I shy away from intensely literary reads like this one. It would not surprise me if when literature comes up in LiL it was researched lightly beforehand on Wikipedia rather than being based on his own reading. Which, I really want to stress, is not an insult or backhanded spite from me; it's important for a character like Nodoka to be making literary references and allusions, and if he doesn't have that knowledge off-hand it's good to research it. Anyway, therefore I would be pretty stunned if there was any amount of thought put into LiL being a 'visualization of Nabokov's literacy tools and manipulation,' although the comparisons are definitely there for us to read into. (And let there be egg on my face if this read is totally off.)

That said, I haven't read Invitation to a Beheading, and that sounds fascinating. Will definitely read it - thanks for bringing it up. Actually, it seems so similar I might really have egg on my face regarding the above comment. This reminds me of the story The Egg by Weir which I was convinced was the Egg allusion in LiL until I discovered it was actually a Wonder Egg Priority reference. Check out its plot to get very anxious very fast.

As for Maya, we must understand that Selebus loves cats. I myself didn't really understand all the allusions to Maya being a 'stray cat' in Kumon-mi and stuff. If I were to turn a cat into an anime girl, I would not know where to begin: what behaviors she would display, what the allegory would be, etc. It's only because Selebus loves cats so much and has such a deep affinity for them that he could craft Maya as a cat-figure, and I start to understand her role as the cat who sticks with Sensei no matter how depressed he gets, etc. Therefore I would be quite surprised if he had any 'malice' for her. But I may just be dull to these things.

On Otoha, by replaying I got to reevaluate her somewhat, and while I certainly didn't grow to like her or anything - I can understand her better.
The thing is, we had all sort of came to the conclusion that Otoha is a teenager doing stupid stuff, and while that's certainly true, now I feel like there's more to it. I'm currently on the perspective that Otoha, much like Rin, is a disaster.

The difference is that Rin is a loveable disaster born out of hormones and wanting genuinely to spread love and good feels, and Otoha is a disaster born out of being entitled and self-centered.

She's not evil and she's not going out of her way to do damage about other people, she just cares about herself over everyone else while being a teenager. She's a single child of a stable home, that had everyone fawning over her to the degree that she doesn't even understand it. She's talented enough to have a literal pop star offer her free lessons, and people trying to "kidnap" her to their school since she's so cool.

She doesn't really have a primary goal of being loved, or forming a family, or an actual dream or overcoming trauma - she's just having new experiences and gathering content for her songs I guess.

I'm not going to go over her entire arc, but basically what governs Otoha's thinking is "how do I feel about this, and what should I do to help myself in this situation?" - she cares about people when it suits her, and doesn't care when it doesn't. It's just not sociopathic (thought out), it's chaotic.

Which leads me to my final point in that Otoha probably would kiss Akira, because none of what she ever did was careful manipulation - it was just her winging it on the fly.

(even though her giving him a gift really reeked of a bribe so that he'd deliver Niki her letter/gift or whatever the hell that was) - then again that's no real great manipulation so my point stands.
Which yeah, Otoha still sucks. But I can't really fault a storm for wrecking stuff, I'd just keep my distance. Then again I'm not faulting Akira because 1. He just doesn't care as long as it somehow gets him closer to having sex with said person, and 2. Her ass.

I strongly disagree, characters repeating sentences said by others (even unintentionally), is a relatively common writing tool to establish commonality, it is only a problem when it's way too specific and holds no narrative relevance. What you used as an example is a sentence generic enough that it's easy to imagine anyone using it, and the narrative significance was already established.

A far better example of a problematic scenario is Sekai (Kyoto) and Sara (I think her last scene), the similar framing of the shot, identical facial expressions and the similar theme all work to not simplify imply commonality but to grab you by your ears and scream the message of the scene at you.

If the first example works as a subtle way to convey meaning and as such works on its own, the second example is so blatant that there has to be something more to it, some in universe explanation, otherwise it is simply a sloppily written scene.

No? She's a shitty person, and yet I can respect and even love a shitty person, as long as being shitty isn't all they are. Yumi bullying Futaba is reprehensible and yet this isn't her whole character. Yumi is also the girl being sexually assaulted (multiple times), and neglected and put into toxic conditions, and trying her best to change and cope with what's thrown at her.
Same goes for Yuki, and Maya, and many other characters. Even Kirin, I guess - just not for me. Nodoka is a special case. My point is that most characters aren't just one thing. I don't have to "forgive" them, they're just complex - bad parts and good parts.

As for Otoha, one of the issues is that there are no special circumstances nor character arcs. She's barely anything out of her obsession for Niki and fucking up her relationship with Rin. First time she's introduced is already as Rin's potential girlfriend, and that goes from her being on the fence about it, to creating problems regarding Chika and Akira, to being ashamed of Rin and their relationship, to creating more problems because of Chika and Akira, to abandoning her to assault Niki, to physically assaulting Rin and taking advantage of Rin's dependency, to ever escalate things with Rin every time she receives a rejection from Niki, to keep trying to make her girlfriend's bestfriend complicit in her keeping the cheating a secret (including confessing to Akira the confession she wrote to Niki), to eventually breaking up with Rin because Niki told her she was delusional in trying to get with her, to trade Rin's nudes for Niki's after all of this (...) if I were to ever "forgive" Otoha there'd be no Otoha left in the game because her "sins" are almost all her screentime.

Furthermore everything about Otoha comes down to Otoha. There's no Yumi growing up in a den of criminals and drugs. Nor Yuki giving birth to a child fruit of rape. Nor a lonely abused child trying to fight alone against supernatural cycles. Hell, even Kirin has somewhat of a trauma in being the underachiever sibling. What does Otoha have? lol

Eveything she does is just because she felt like it (or "I'm a confused teenager" as she puts it). Which again, no issue there, my initial post was exactly about understanding her more and thus lessening the hate instead of increasing it. So it's kind of whatever, but since you ask, there it is.
Other important factor is that a lot of us love Rin, while not that many tend to hold Futaba in (that much of) a special place. So that is also a bias that factors in, as I'm much more affected by someone hurting a character I love than one that's just there (especially if said bullying happened and stopped so many chapters ago).

spoilers.html:
Have a feeling we will have a lot of weird encounters with Yasu from now on.

She claims to not have a name. Is lying suppose to be a sin? How wonderful.

The only experiments I can imagine Nodoka doing on the mc if he passes out in her room at this time is either see how long it takes her to carry his body out the dorm, how long it takes him to wake up or study the anatomy of his penis. Hey I'm just saying, I think the mc is being afraid of nothing.

I wonder what the name is of the humor where you transition into a verbal or written dialogue that's extremely confusion, sounds funny and makes you wonder what the hell lead them to that point.

Touka lecturing him about not lecturing, then proceed to be made fun of, even her name. She's gonna be that spoiled brat being pushed down a peg and the mother is not gonna do anything about it for some reason.
How big was her desk...? Like a literal throne?
She is the peak of spoiled, so fucking opposite from Ayane it's not even funny. Honestly Yumi might as well be more spoiled than Ayane is now that I think about it.
I didn't think I could like this Touka girl and I guess I sort of don't, I just like her because the mc is giving her hell right now and I consider that a victory in character development.
I thought he was gonna continue the name joke... It was very funny.

There are plenty of options to counteract loud sounds, both cheap and less effective or expensive and very effective all around. But yeah, sure. Maybe Miku has opted to train herself and deal with the trauma rather than block it out.

And by can't, I'm guessing... Miku just doesn't know what happened to her? Part of me believes that but I feel like she should have been told the details of what happened.

So, Miku is a bit clueless about that stuff. Ends up getting into a compromising position, want it to stop. Time goes by, it happens again, later she says she wants it to stop, he convinced her to continue. It happens again, it goes wrong, later she says she wants it to stop for good. 3/7 scenes yet to be unlocked.
I'm sensing a pattern here.

Have the mc considered the fact that the sun does not have a gender and therefore is an "it"? Apparently not.

NIIIIIICE! This interaction is so funny! He called Niki again just to piss her off and make her "jealous" of Otoha and it's gold.
They are still doing that name thing. I went with Barack because I thought that was the funniest.

Holy fuck dude! Sending such a picture of Futaba moments after getting her number.

I would prefer Otohas' hair while it's down over the hairstyles Ami have had. Long straight hair is great. I guess it just seems to natural and clean. The red parts of Otohas' hair makes it more unique and while fully red hair could be nice, this particular tone of red is very strong and since she's a bit of a unique person in appearance the primary color is fine like that.

Mc has ascended. He can now defeat a tv in grabbing a teenagers attention. That is... surprisingly difficult in this day and age, probably. Only that teenagers wouldn't be using tv's anymore... I don't think.

Otoha got startled, not scared. I used to say scared too but eventually I realized there is a clear difference.

HAHAHAHAHA! Mc spoke in the middle of her phone call and she had to ask him to pretend to be the tv out of suspicion and he went for "Take that, you little slut." and it broke me!
Molly being a hypocrite. She was the one who made the noise and now she complains Otoha is making too much noise.

Discovered my favorite animation so far. Ayane dorm cowgirl position. Like the only scene I would consider good by my preferences...

Uh oh, here comes trouble...
Oh? Something is wrong with Sana... Oh right, they have met before. And Yasu mentioned something about her brother.
You know that was intention too. The way her eyes went from looking at the class to him, it took a second or two longer than normal, like she did that unsettlingly slow eye movement.
Yeah, I don't think there is anything remotely normal about Yasu. I kinda want to see how Yumi and Yasu will interact... They both have 4 letter names starting with Y. Coincidence? Starting to think there are no coincidences.(which I've probably said before)
Well at least Yumi is interested in this Yasu girl so there's that.
Who even says "So many voices" followed by "Can I have them?"
And then suddenly asks "How much can you see in the dark, Sensei?" There is something seriously wrong with this girl. It wouldn't fucking surprise me if she's a literal ghost or dead person.

Maya: "I am not touching this girl(Yasu) with a ten foot pole."
Yasu: "Touch me."
Yep. She's fucking insane. The mental asylum gave up and didn't even say bye as she left.

Uhh... Because having a girl who says she sees dead people and repeats "How many bodies?" multiple times is a perfectly desirable trait in a student.
And these two are suppose to live together? I don't think there is any girl in that school that would want that.

I feel like there are gonna be a lot of happy events involving this girl... Also walking into her dorm will be like a contrast between rich as fuck on one side and fucking... possessed dolls or something all over the walls on the other, all suspiciously looking at you when your eyes are elsewhere.
She's guilt tripping Touka into sharing the dorm...
"Resident rich girl cursed by the ghost girl" Thinking about that non existing quote.
Oh great... and now she's standing in the corner of the room for too long for only god knows what reason...(literally?)

You know the mc is gonna talk to Maya again about this girl and Touka is gonna talk to her mother about how weird this girl is... probably.

I've bene in another one of those deadzones where nothing really happens. Just the occasional main event and waiting for new character events that don't show up.

Ahh yes. I see he is now embracing his role as a human trafficker. Kaori would be proud.

I've always had this mentality that nobody what you do, life will find a way to screw you over. So in Touka's case, washing her hands after everything she does mean she will be less resistant to sickness and bacteria when she isn't able to get rid of them. If you live the easy life, doing hard things will be difficult. If you always have fun, fun will always be boring. If you work too hard, you might forget to relax(not quite the same thing but sort of). Also if you move around fast with a driver and a limo everywhere your body will grow weaker. Kinda the reason I don't invest in something like one of those electric scooters everyone drives around with nowadays... there are just too many of them.

Having this cheerful tune playing with an angry Touka and a Yasu just being weird instead of creepy is unsettling in a completely different way.

How DOES she "keep switching from smiling to crying so quickly"? I'm telling you. She's not normal.

Interesting new song. Touka "Trial Period" event.

Touka has some similarities to Tsuneyo, Ayane and Yumi but only like 10% Yumi. Nodoka has some similarities to umm sort of just Kirin? Maybe a bit of Futaba in terms of hobbies? Only that she didn't sell her virginity the moment she showed up and is actually being hard to get despite her overly flirtatious and suggestive behavior.

Well I can definitely relate with Nodoka a bit. Imagining what it's like being someone else is sort of a thing I've done most of my teens and early adult years in the form of gaming. Doing that makes it harder to live your own life however. If you spend every waking moment living someone else's life, you lose the time you could spend living your own. Miserable existence. But there are some things you just can't change and being born with too many flaws and a perfectly functional consciousness debating every aspect of everything... well, we can't all be fortunate.
Umm, Is Nodoka okay?
"I kind of hate reading, actually." SAME! Dude, I'm literally Nodoka right now. I don't proof read any of what I write here, surprise. And I don't like reading anything I'm not interested in, which is almost everything. At this point, if it's not an AVN, there is a good chance I'm not interested. Reading for the sake of reading isn't fun.

Holy shit... She's not a picture book, she's a very advanced coloring book requiring rare colors "just waiting to be filled in".

Okay that's definitely a bug with Autovn. Fuck that. Apparently autovn can make you go to the dojo to visit Osako even tho I don't have that option when visiting it, nor do I have her phone number. There should be literally no way for autovn to make me visit Osako right now.

Aww, how cute. Touka is a bit childish at heart. Or just of age? Pretty sure you watch cartoons through your teens and if in Japan that would probably be anime in many cases until you discover anime.

Isn't Touka's the first and maybe the only case where the mc hangs out with her and then goes to hang out with the other one in the hallway?

I guess her room is kind of expensive looking but I would still think Nodokas' mini library looks better.

Money has power, and assassination is one use for it.

"Uhh..." is an understatement... I feel kinda bad for Touka having to live in the same room as a girl sitting on a school chair facing the wall and doing absolutely nothing. Wtf... I'm telling this, there is nothing normal about this girl.
What does that even mean? "tidac muleac" written upside down.
I guess she really doesn't have anything to her name at all... It's eery how empty Yasus' side of the room is. Even Yumi has more things... I mean obviously. Like is this just Yasus' thing? She's a mental asylum patient or something?
Remember how I said Touka's room was gonna be decked out with rich person things and Yasus' side was gonna have creepy dolls or some shit? Well I was way off and this just confirms my theory even harder that Yasu isn't human.
It's honestly like the dev looked at all their characters and thought: "They aren't insane enough."
I feel so unsettled that I'm expecting Yasus' neck to snap 150 degrees and look straight at us or something...
Ahh... I can't stress enough how unsettling it is to be talking to Touka while Yasu is just sitting there on her empty half of the room. I may never get used to that.
Oh... Great... She laughs like a maniac. Yeah, okay, she is the literal definition of a mentally insane person...

I didn't think he would bring that up but yes, Touka is using a love hotel bed... That innocent soul...
She sent a driver to drive him back home... She is something else.

Oh... and of course Yasu just stands in the middle of the hall looking at him... Well it's not the first time that has happened. A certain happy event.

Easier to get away with horrible shit at a cathedral? At this point I would like to deny that but what do I know about the power of forgiveness and what law will suddenly overlook because of prayer or some shit?

You are a deranged motherfucker if you read that and thought "I'm going to go eat fly eggs now because the funny dev said they won't taste like anything"

Oh, I thought that entire time Yasu was looking at us when we got to the cathedral but no, she is looking at the book. Weird angle. Looking at us? Sensei? Him? Mc? Yeah, I have no idea which word to use and when because they all seem correct and you have probably noticed this. So have I. Probably a lot worse having to read than write tho so my apologies for that...

Well I was conveniently wondering just now how old you have to be to be a bishop but I still internally complained about the second godnote...

If humans could lay 500 eggs over a 3 day period, we would have a pretty big problem right now... no really, getting pregnant would be banned and most people would have to get mandatory "tubal ligation" and "vasectomy". Fancy words. So only like the smartest and richest people would be allowed it and most of their babies would be spread out through adoption with adoption being the go to way for anyone to have a child. Now doesn't that just sound fantastic? I wonder if they would make it mandatory for like the middle class or to adopt after marriage or something. Who knows how the world would really be. What a weird thing to be talking about at 8:46 AM on a Tuesday after having been apparently unable to sleep because my mind won't stop thinking about this game and I let it.

Part of me would entrust my passed out body to Yasu, part of me wouldn't let that happen as if my life depends on it. Only time will tell which judgement is the most accurate.

I'm not surprised God said no. This mc hasn't done many god approving things, has he?

Yeah I was about to say, missionary is a stupid word for people who worship a god. Who even thinks of that?
"mission"ary... questary? No that's dumb.

Oh great... I was about to say I don't care about this religious nonsense but then she mentioned sex... I am but a simple man, you see.

I expected him to take Touka to the love hotel to embarrass her and show her that her type of bed is indeed used there. But I guess showing her the other side of town is a bit more... acceptable and wholesome?
Actually now that I think about it, it makes perfect sense that he would be showing her this place and talking about Chinami's situation. The answer is a tiny bit of a spoiler tho if I remember correctly but nothing special.

I expected something bad to happen and the mc had to come to Touka's rescue while she talked to that poor man. Instead there was a jump cut with creepy images followed by hexdecimal "sudden". Like yeah, I get that the dev didn't want to have to watch her talk with the man but based on what we have been hearing about that side of town and everything I've been hearing about "don't wander around poor neighbourhoods with money or fame" or whatever, I kinda get the impression that something bad was going to happen and that maybe it even did but the world somehow erased what happens or undid it, teleporting them into the convenience store instead.
Well clearly the jump cut was not just on the player's side.

No fucking way... HAHAHA! This innocent rich girl doesn't know what condoms are!
Every time a customer walks in while his there, something weird happens and the customer leaves. Yep, this is just a thing that happens now...
Well her reaction to that was rather restrained all things considered but it was cute.
I can't help but feel like her family would have not been okay with him taking her to that side of town, especially without a proper body guard, especially while interacting with one of the locals who also happen to be a man(excluding the mc).

Well then. That's interesting. We all expected Touka to get embarrassed and mad at him for seeing her in so little clothing but I guess that is not the case. A welcome surprise to be sure but without a funny embarrassing moment, the scene does become stale.

Asks if she may stand. He says if she wants to sit she can sit. She says she wouldn't have asked to stand if she wanted to sit. Welp.
Touka giving most of the girls a run for their money in beauty. Just look at her... I'm sure her hair could use a bit more color to stand out more but I don't think anything but straight black would suit her status.
It's kind of hard to feel bad for Touka right now knowing she doesn't even need to be at that school. Any under other circumstances I might feel something. I guess my reaction is common when confronted by a rich spoiled girl suddenly in an unfamiliar situation without friends.

I meeeean... she kinda is the rich girl stereotype tho? At least at the start. We already have Ayane, are we gonna have two rich girls who aren't following the rich girl stereotype now? I suppose the fact she's willing to adapt to the middle class and is willing to look at what people see from an outside perspective by figuring out what the rich girl stereotype is not something I see people with that stereotype doing so I guess she's making an effort to be less stereotypical.

I've had that thought a couple times now. She is the heir of her family which is traditional. Normally the heir would be male so I imagine for someone born into that, she faces occasional critique which might as well be seen as a curse or disease as she so mildly puts it.
Ooooo. So because of tradition or the family name or whatever, they also can't have more children than two and as we know, they have two daughters. I'm not gonna pretend to agree with this because it's quite stupid so there is that.
Oof, she's only saved from an arranged marriage because most of the males are gone.

Uuuuh... Wth is going on at the church?
Very mysterious...
What's so bad about perception?
"Are you on drugs?"
"Not anymore."
Oh, great. I guess I shouldn't be surprised.

There it is. "That" Nodoka. The result of what happens when a writer enters that creative flow and don't want to lose it so they caffeinate themselves and do nothing but write until it's done.
As someone who reads a lot nowadays, I find myself rereading the same thing because my brain cannot process it. I also blank out completely, forgetting everything I was just talking and thinking about.

Nodoka is way too intelligent. My brain already crashed at the first question.
